who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 21 years old at the start of employment. No prior professional experience is required.
how_to_apply: Complete the in-person application and interview during the scheduled Application and Interview Weekend.
notes: The organization's Gallery Fellowship (ages 16 to 24) and 10-month Mural Studio job are separate programs. The old ArtWorks web address now redirects to 1001colors.org. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: 8 weeks, June to July; 20 to 30 hours a week, Monday to Friday about 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
pay_detail: $13 an hour

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Most programs are ages 14 to 18 (14 by Sept 28, 2026 for the fall session). Outreach Assistantships need age 16+.
how_to_apply: Apply online (up to six programs, ranked). Save your Application ID for the Teen Dashboard. Most programs require an interview; offers must be accepted within 72 hours. A parent/guardian consent form is required after you accept.
notes: One program per session. A Social Security number or ITIN is not required for every program; teens without one should contact ASM. Applying again each session needs a new application. The apply page still shows fall 2026 wording, but fall programs began Sept 28, so the fall round is over for new applicants until the spring window opens. Work permit rules for under-16 not stated on ASM pages.
duration: Spring: late Feb to mid May. Summer: late June to early Aug. Fall 2026: Sept 28 to Dec 12.
pay_detail: Paid stipend based on program level and frequency. Dollar amounts vary by program and are not stated on the apply page.

who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. The page says internships are open to all ages, including high schoolers. No minimum age is stated for teen volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Then meet a staff member for an interview and training. Interns use a different form. Teen Advisory Board members use their own form.
notes: Alive says it runs free drop-in hours after school and over the summer, plus teen-led clubs. Locations named on the site are Naperville, Aurora and Hanover Park. The page says internships are open to all ages, including high schoolers.
duration: Teen volunteer hours are not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens get service hours for volunteering. Internships are non-paid.

who_can_apply: In-person volunteer roles are for ages 16 and up. At-home projects are a good option for anyone under 16. Vet clinic support is 18 and up. School service roles need an agreement signed by a parent and a teacher.
how_to_apply: Dog Care, Cat Care, Shelter Support and School Service Hours are open as of 2026-10-10. Wildlife is closed and Clinic Support is full. Sign up on the volunteer page for the role you want. You also take a short online Safety and Protocols training and pay the $35 membership fee. For school hours, use the School Service page.
notes: Animal care roles ask for at least six months. The page says Shelter Support is not eligible for court-ordered service hours. Sites include South Elgin, Bloomingdale Petco, Algonquin Petco and Geneva Petco. Others are the St. Charles office and Elburn Forest Preserve.
duration: Dog and cat care: at least 40 hours over 6 months, with weekly or every-other-week shifts. Animal care roles ask for at least six months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $35 volunteer membership fee for all opportunities.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who go to school in Michigan and play a string, wind, brass or percussion instrument (harp too). Pianists are not considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the A2SO site. Send a one take YouTube video of you playing one part of a solo piece with an accompanist.
notes: This is a contest, not a job. The page is for the 2026 contest. Expect similar timing next year, from August to late September.
duration: Final round Nov 7, 2026. Winner plays Feb 23, 2027.
pay_detail: $50 application fee (email jpepper@a2so.org if the fee is a problem). Prizes: $500 grand prize, $250 runner-up.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in Washtenaw County. Ages and grades are not stated on the page. The page does not say where the council meets.
how_to_apply: Application not open. Watch the Youth Council page in 2027. Contact: Community Investment Officer at (734) 663-0401 x116.
notes: One member also serves as a voting member of the foundation board. Pay and time commitment are not stated on the page.
duration: Time commitment not stated
pay_detail: Pay not stated

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Ages 14 to 17 need a signed permission slip from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. After review you are contacted with details on signing up for a required volunteer orientation, then you pick shifts.
notes: Older library posts mention a summer teen volunteer program. The current page only describes the year-round program. Michigan's Youth Employment Standards Act covers employers of anyone under 18, including volunteers. Ask the program if you need a work permit.
duration: Ongoing; you commit to the shifts you sign up for
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: You must live in Michigan and go to a Michigan high school. You must be close enough to travel to Ann Arbor. Rising juniors and seniors are best. Most students come from partner schools: Ypsilanti Community, Lincoln and Belleville. There is no GPA minimum.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest form. One letter of recommendation is required. The page does not describe the later steps.
notes: The page shows an Interest Form Closed button even though it says the form opens Oct 12, so check the page for the current status. Commuter program, so you live at home.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027. You must be on campus at least 35 of the 40 days.
pay_detail: $4,000 for taking part

who_can_apply: Teens 14 and older.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application or the 2026 printable PDF. Teens must also complete a work permit. The page says that from October 2, permits are done online in the Youth Employment Permit Portal (YEPP). Call Stacey at 734-475-8732 ext. 212.
notes: Chelsea is about 15 miles west of Ann Arbor. The library page says teen volunteers need a work permit even though the role is unpaid.
duration: Year-round. Hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older to volunteer alone at the warehouse or Community Kitchen. Younger kids can come with an adult. The warehouse takes ages 8 and up. The kitchen takes ages 12 and up.
how_to_apply: Create a user account with Individual Registration and sign up for shifts in advance; no walk-ins. If you need school hours signed or an observer will attend, call the volunteer coordinator first.
notes: Not teen-specific, but a steady way for teens 14 and up to earn volunteer hours. Warehouse work involves moderate lifting. Groups of four or more use a separate group form. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Single shifts; you can volunteer as often as you like
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High-school-aged youth who live in Ypsilanti and the surrounding townships. For the summer, you must have finished 9th grade and cannot miss more than 4 days. The school-year program is for teens who finished the summer program in good standing.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Youth and Schools page when applications open. Questions: Jenny Pritchett, jenny@growinghope.net.
notes: Michigan requires a work permit for workers under 18. From Oct 2, 2026 permits come through the state Youth Employment Permit Portal.
duration: Summer 2027: June 15 to Aug 6, Monday to Thursday, 9 AM to 2:30 PM. After school: Sept to May, Tue/Wed/Thu, 4 to 6 PM.
pay_detail: $14 an hour, plus free weekly produce bags in the growing season.

who_can_apply: The page says community volunteers include high school and college students, corporate partners and retirees. It does not state a minimum age. Ask before you apply.
how_to_apply: For the Hands-On Museum, email volunteer@aahom.org. For wildlife volunteering at Leslie Science & Nature Center, fill out the application linked on the page. Or email volunteer@lesliesnc.org.
notes: The page is short. It gives no age rule, hours, training or start dates, so email first. The Hands-On Museum's old address (aahom.org/volunteer) now sends you to this page. The Leslie wildlife application link goes to a file named Adult_Volunteer_Application.pdf, so ask Leslie before a teen applies for wildlife work.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer roles.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 17 (must be 12 before registering). Those about to turn 18 within 6 months may prefer the adult orientation.
how_to_apply: Online registration only, which opens about 30 days before each session. You must attend all six classes; there are no make-ups, refunds or transfers. A waitlist is available.
notes: Demand is higher than space, so you may wait months. After training you volunteer without a parent present. Inactive for 6 months or more means retaking the training. Shelter is at 3100 Cherry Hill Rd, Ann Arbor. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: 6 training sessions, then a 2 to 4 hour per month volunteer commitment
pay_detail: $205 program fee for the 6 session training (training, T-shirt, supplies). Limited scholarships for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. Beginners are welcome.
how_to_apply: Register online on the Film Camp page. Questions: Holly Behrend, hbehrend@marquee-arts.org.
notes: This camp costs money. Check the page in spring for 2027 dates.
duration: 2026 dates: June 29 to July 3, July 6 to 10 and 13 to 15, and July 20 to 24
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $576.25 for session 1, $901.25 for session 2, $576.25 for session 3, or $1,901.25 for all sessions.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24. You live in Hillsdale, Jackson, Lenawee, Livingston or Washtenaw County.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the page and choose your county.
notes: This prepares you for internships. It is a course, not a job. The same agency runs SummerWorks, a paid summer program, for Washtenaw County.
duration: 4 weeks per cohort
pay_detail: The course is free. Eligible participants can earn cash incentives for finishing it. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Any teen of high school age. It is best to sign up ahead, but you can sign up when you come.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen sign up form on the website or sign up when you come. Questions: Hananiah Wiggins, hananiah@neutral-zone.org, (734) 214-9995.
notes: This is a free teen center, not a paid job. Future Corps for high schoolers meets the first Monday of each month, 4 to 6 PM, and helps with first-job support. Neutral Zone is at 310 E Washington St, Ann Arbor.
duration: Weekly programs all school year
pay_detail: Free. Donations are welcome.

who_can_apply: High-risk youth ages 13 to 18 in Washtenaw County.
how_to_apply: Not stated for this program. The page lists the Drop-In Center at (734) 485-2222 and a contact form at ozonehouse.org/contact-us/.
notes: The page also lists a monthly Career Panel for youth 13 to 20. It is the third Thursday at 5 PM at the Ypsilanti Drop-In Center, and food is served. A Peer Outreach Worker team for youth 15 to 19 was coming back in winter. WorkZone paid internships are for ages 18 to 20.
duration: One week, offered twice a year at the Drop-In Center
pay_detail: All Ozone House services are free.

who_can_apply: The course is open to ages 15 and up. The page says you are prepared to be a lifeguard when you turn 16. Fifteen year olds who finish the course can join the city's Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program.
how_to_apply: Register for the course by calling 734-794-6237 or at Mack Indoor Pool (715 Brooks St., inside Ann Arbor Open School). Pool jobs are applied for online through the city's job board when posted.
notes: The lifeguard certification page says 15 year olds can join the Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program. The recertification section says 15 year olds can be eligible for a city lifeguard job. These two statements differ. Ask the pool at 734-794-6237 what age you can be hired. Michigan says minors must get a work permit before starting a job unless exempt. The permit comes through a Michigan school. See the state youth employment page. You get no refund of the course fee if you fail the course.
duration: Weekend course: Friday evening, Saturday and Sunday
pay_detail: Course fee $200, fully refunded if you pass, apply, are hired and start work at a city pool. Pay for pool jobs is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: The page says individuals and groups of all ages can volunteer. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Individuals use the online volunteer calendar and sign-up. Groups submit the Group Volunteer Inquiry form. Email a2parksevents@a2gov.org or call 734.794.6627.
notes: Ask staff whether a teen needs a parent signature. The page does not say.
duration: One-day to long-term. Group projects run April to October.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Rising 9th graders for Counselors in Training. High school students for counselor roles.
how_to_apply: Not stated. Call Peace Neighborhood Center at (734) 662-3564. 1111 N. Maple Rd., Ann Arbor.
notes: Ask whether the job is paid before you apply. The page also lists College and Career Prep for high school students, Monday to Thursday during the school year.
duration: Summer Youth Services runs eight weeks
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for most roles. Survey Squad is 16 and up. Ushers must be 18. The page says 12 and 13 year olds may volunteer with an adult volunteer. Volunteers work under the supervision of festival staff.
how_to_apply: Pick a volunteer role and a night on the A2SF volunteer sign-up page. Questions: call 734-994-5999.
notes: Seasonal: shifts are in the summer festival only. Usher spots for 2026 were closed. Check the page in spring for 2027 sign-up.
duration: Single shifts at the festival
pay_detail: Unpaid. Completed shifts earn perks such as access to special hospitality areas, and select benefits include tickets to some performances and prize giveaways.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 when programming begins (you must turn 16 by June 1 of the program year) AND you live in, or attend school in, Washtenaw County. Participants may take part for up to three years.
how_to_apply: Online application (opens January): your contact info, parent or guardian contact, approximate household income, possible summer conflicts, and one reference who is not a relative. Accepted minors need a parent or guardian signature.
notes: A paid internship is not guaranteed: the site says a subset of participants is selected, though staff aim to match everyone. After acceptance you need I-9 identification documents and a bank account in your name for pay (this is for payroll, not a fee). Professional development is Tuesday or Wednesday evenings online, then Fridays 10am to 2pm in person from June. Michigan requires a work permit for minors under 18 to work; as of Oct 2, 2026 permits are issued through the state's Youth Employment Permit Portal, not schools. Contact: mail@summerworks.info.
duration: Program runs April to August; internship is 10 weeks between June and August
pay_detail: Internships pay $15 or $17 per hour depending on whether you have finished high school or an equivalent (employer FAQ). About 20 to 25 hours a week.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Ann Arbor and Livingston volunteer page (the link goes to the hospital's volunteer system at stjoemercyann.vsysweb.com). Then an interview, paperwork, health screening and a required orientation.
notes: Requirements listed for volunteers: interview, two TB skin tests, proof of varicella and MMR immunity, Tdap, this year's flu shot, health clearance form, one non-relative reference, and orientation; background checks apply to volunteers 18 and over. Also on the same page: The Farm at Trinity Health takes volunteers age 15 and up (no background check under 18). The Apply Now link is http, not https, so it is not in the apply_url field. Volunteer office phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Year-round roles with some seasonal placements (a summer teen cohort exists)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18. The commission has 21 members: 2 from each county district and 3 at-large.
how_to_apply: Email britt@neutral-zone.org. Ask when you can apply.
notes: Pay and meeting schedule are not stated on the page. Neutral Zone is at 310 E Washington St, Ann Arbor, phone (734) 214-9995.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Students in the county school districts that run each program. The page says to contact your district CTE director or high school counselor. Other-district rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor or your district CTE director. The page does not list steps.
notes: Programs differ by school. Ann Arbor, Chelsea, Dexter, Lincoln, Manchester, Milan, Saline, Whitmore Lake and Ypsilanti each list their own. Washtenaw ISD phone: (734) 994-8100.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 enrolled in at least one high school class (or homeschooled) who show college-level skills. Seniors: GPA 2.5 or higher. Grades 10 and 11: SAT 480 or PSAT 460 or higher. Grades 9 to 12: or take the Accuplacer or a writing sample at WCC.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WCC application, set up your NetID, upload proof of academic level and the parent consent and principal or counselor approval forms from the dual enrollment packet, then register for classes. Call 734-973-3682 for help.
notes: The page does not list application deadlines or information night dates. It links to an Academic Dates page. WCC dual enrollment is not a job.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Tuition not stated on the page. Your high school may pay (it sends a billing form), or you pay or use a payment plan.

who_can_apply: Michigan residents. 8th graders (9th Grade Program) need passing grades in English, math, science and social studies. 9th graders (Middle College) need 1 credit each in English, math, science, social studies and electives by the end of the school year. 10th graders (Middle College) need 2 credits each in those subjects. Washtenaw County residents get priority.
how_to_apply: Go to an Admissions Informational Meeting first (6:00 to 7:30 PM on Dec 1, 2026; Jan 19, Feb 1, Feb 10 online, Feb 18 online, 2027). Then use the online application. Placement tests follow if you are admitted.
notes: Admissions office phone: (734) 677-5360. General line: 734-973-3300. This is a school program, not a job.
duration: Several years of high school
pay_detail: The page says graduates finish without paying tuition, fees or books.

who_can_apply: The Youth Volunteer Corps is for teens ages 11 to 17. Ages for the other youth volunteer roles are not stated on the page. Youth sports coaches must be at least 14.
how_to_apply: Use the Begin your application button on the volunteering page. Questions: volunteer@annarborymca.org.
notes: The page's own link to a Youth Volunteer Corps page was a dead link when checked, so details of YVC projects and dates are not confirmed. The Y also lists other volunteer roles that appear aimed at adults. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Varies: one-off service projects or ongoing roles
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Corps form on the page when it opens in late April, then attend a one-hour training. A work permit is provided at orientation. Phone: 734-482-4110.
notes: The library says teens need a work permit even for this volunteer role. Michigan rules cover volunteers under 18. Permits now go through the state Youth Employment Permit Portal (since Oct 2, 2026).
duration: Summer. Hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Create Your Own Project is for grades 10 to 12. The page gives no grade rule for the Teen Advisory Group.
how_to_apply: Use the TAG application, the event volunteer sign-up form or the project proposal form linked on the page. Teen Librarian Assistant spots are full, so that form puts you on a waitlist. Phone: 734-482-4110.
notes: The library says TAG members must fill out a work permit. Pokemon card game helpers meet Thursdays 5 to 6 PM starting October 1.
duration: Teen Librarian Assistant: one hour weekly or every other week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Summer Volunteer Squad is for teens going into grades 7 to 12. You must live in Arlington Heights.
how_to_apply: Use the volunteer application link on the library volunteer page. New Middle School Panel members sign up on the page.
notes: There is also a Tween Advisory Group for grades 4 to 6, which is for younger kids.
duration: Summer for the Squad. The Middle School Volunteer Panel meets monthly during the school year, over snacks. Check the library calendar for dates.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 years old. Students can join one week, all six or any number of weeks.
how_to_apply: Register for classes through the registration link on the Teen Academy page. Questions: Office of Engagement.
notes: Courses change every week. Students agree to the handbook rules when they sign up. The Teen Academy page does not mention scholarships; ask the Office of Engagement.
duration: Six weeks of themed courses (2026: June 1 to July 24)
pay_detail: $185 per one-week course (Week 3 is $148). Morning (9 to 11:30 a.m.) and afternoon (12:30 to 3 p.m.) courses.

who_can_apply: Adults 18 and up. Teens must be at least 16 years old when they apply.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Then go to an interview. You also need a health screening and a criminal background check. You need orientation papers and training on site. Phone: 847-437-5500.
notes: You need at least 50 volunteer hours before you can ask for written proof of hours (for school or court). Uniform and ID badge are required whenever you volunteer.
duration: One 4 hour shift a week (minimum 4 hours of service each week)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Adults 18 and up. Teens must be at least 16 years old when they apply.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Then go to an interview. You also need a health screening and a criminal background check. You need orientation papers and training on site. Phone: 847-755-8708.
notes: You need at least 100 volunteer hours before you can ask for written proof of hours (for school or court). Uniform and ID badge are required whenever you volunteer.
duration: 4 hours a week, at least 100 hours over 6 continuous months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Aurora residents ages 14 to 18 who are in high school.
how_to_apply: Check that you meet the rules, then fill out the BEO Interest Form (Google form).
notes: The page does not name the employers or say if internships pay. For city help, call 311 or 630-256-4636. The City's Summer Youth Programs page said summer 2026 programs are closed and to look for summer 2027.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. As of 2026-10-10, the program page says nothing about pay. Ask the program team.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not give an age or grade range or a residency rule. Ask the teen librarians.
how_to_apply: Write to the Teen Librarians. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is teens@aurorapubliclibrary.org.
notes: The library's teen volunteer page said summer reading volunteers for 2027 apply in the spring. It also lists outside groups that take teen volunteers, with their own age rules.
duration: Meets on the 1st Monday of every month at 6 p.m.
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It does not say if service hours are given.

who_can_apply: Aurora residents ages 15 to 24. The page lists separate planning sessions. They are for Aurora high school students, college students and nonprofits.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form. Staff office hours are Tuesdays 2 to 4 p.m. (630-256-3416) and Wednesdays 10 a.m. to noon (630-256-3402) during the window. Email youthservdiv@aurora.il.us.
notes: The page says about 10 to 40 projects will be funded. Co-design sessions were September 8 and 10, 2026, so they have passed. Ages up to 24 are allowed, so high school students compete with older applicants.
duration: Application window Aug 24 to Oct 16, 2026
pay_detail: You do not get paid. Each project can receive a microgrant of $1,000 to $5,000 to carry it out. The money pays for the project, not a wage to you.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 17 who are in good standing at school and live in Aurora or North Aurora. A signed waiver is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and the waiver using the link at the top of the Youth Court page. Print and sign the waiver and bring it to your first session. Contacts on the page: rodriguezs@aurora.il.us or sarmientos@aurora.il.us.
notes: Training dates are not listed on the page. The page says Youth Court is for youth who committed first time offenses. Teens serve as jurors.
duration: Meets the third Tuesday of each month, 6 to 8 p.m.
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not say which clubhouse hosts each Industry Club or whether you must be a member first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Industry Clubs interest form on the page, or email membership@bgcncil.org or call the South Elgin office at (847) 608-5017. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free and signs up through MyClubHub (bgcncil.org/join/).
notes: The organization runs Elgin and South Elgin clubhouses (administrative office at 735 Martin Dr, South Elgin) plus Aurora, Batavia and a Schaumburg Teen Center, but the Industry Clubs page does not say where each session meets. Ask before you sign up. Elgin clubhouses follow the School District U-46 calendar.
duration: 8 to 10 week sessions
pay_detail: Described as paid; the amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Keystone Club is for ages 14 to 18. Youth of the Year is for ages 10 to 18. You must be a Club member. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free, and you must meet the local residency or school district rules.
how_to_apply: Create an account in MyClubHub, pick your clubhouse and fill out the membership application. Staff will email next steps and a start date. Contact for Youth of the Year: cmaxwell@bgcelgin.org.
notes: Age limits can differ by clubhouse. The Industry Clubs (paid career programs for teens) are a separate listing. A Schaumburg Teen Center page exists but only shows a calendar.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Teen membership is free. Winners of Youth of the Year are eligible for Club scholarships.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 must be with a legal guardian at all times. Ages 16 and older can volunteer on their own. Everyone must pass screening.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist through the Bloomington Volunteer Network. Use the green button on the page. That is not the application. The volunteer director will email you a link to it later.
notes: Book Buddies (K to 6th grade, all ages welcome with an adult) needs no application. Shelter hours for Book Buddies are listed on the page.
duration: 2-hour weekly shift for a minimum of 6 months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older who can do hard physical work. That means digging, carrying mulch buckets and pulling water tanks. You must show up on time. Grant rules also ask that you treat all people fairly, no matter their gender, who they love or their race.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form linked from the job page. Questions: hello@canopybloomington.org.
notes: The page does not say which year the March and May dates belong to, but the weekday dates match 2026. Check the page again in early 2027. Work permit rules for Indiana minors were not checked.
duration: Part time, Monday to Friday 9am to 1pm (20 hours a week). Two 4-week sessions: June and July (2026 dates).
pay_detail: $15 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a class. Use the events calendar at the Eskenazi Museum.
notes: The 2026 camp was full. Younger weeks are for ages 7 to 12. Contact the museum for cost.
duration: 1 week, noon to 3 p.m. Monday to Friday (July 27 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. You must be 18 to use power tools. Student chapters exist at Bloomington High School North and South.
how_to_apply: Email ec@monroecountyhabitat.org to sign up for a build day. You can also use the contact form on the volunteer page.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and clothes you do not mind getting dirty. Groups such as schools can sign up together. ReStore roles are listed but the page does not state a separate age for them.
duration: Ongoing; many volunteers come weekly, monthly or for special events
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Lunch is provided for construction site volunteers.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not state exact grades or ages. Highly selective, about 15 to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Record a monologue of up to 90 seconds. Upload it to YouTube or Vimeo as unlisted. Then fill out the online application with the video link. The program can give you a monologue if you need one.
notes: You must live on campus. The application page is at cinemaacademy.indiana.edu/summer-sessions/afc.html. Check the exact age rules there.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: $950, which includes lodging, meals, instruction, equipment use and supplies (2026 price).

who_can_apply: Gifted high school students, such as singers, players and spoken word artists. Students are picked. Age and grade limits are not listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the camp page (an online form). Students are selected.
notes: Contact campsoul@iu.edu or the director, Ignoisco Miles. His email is imiles@iu.edu and his phone is 812-855-0816. Ask about cost and how to audition before you apply.
duration: 6 days (June 13 to 18, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18. The page has a star by this, so check the session page for exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill in the form. It is on the Cinema Academy summer sessions page.
notes: There is also a one-week Online Filmmaking Bootcamp. The Media School also holds a free one-day teen workshop on Saturday Nov 14, 2026 (Cinema, Game Dev and Journalism tracks).

pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. Three kinds of scholarships are offered.

who_can_apply: Current Indiana high school juniors on a college-prep path. That means the Indiana GPS Diploma or GPS Diploma Plus. You need a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA. You should like teaching, counseling or student services.

notes: The page does not state the exact day it opens or closes. Only people who live in Indiana can join.
duration: 1 week (July 11 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: Free. Food and lodging are covered.

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 18. The minimum age varies by camp, so check the page for each session. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the camp website. The scholarship form is separate.
notes: Overnight tuition includes dorm lodging. Day camp is an option for local students. Tuition includes meals, a t-shirt, a thumb drive and a water bottle. Media School also lists June and July 2027 weeks.
duration: 5 days
pay_detail: Overnight $850, day camp $500. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school students. Beginners and experienced students are both welcome. Age limits are not stated.

notes: Run since 1946. Check the site for cost and dorm details before you plan.
duration: 5 days per session (Session 1: July 12 to 16, 2027. Session 2: July 18 to 22, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school juniors with a GPA of at least 3.2, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math. You want a science career. Students from the other Holland programs go first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 8, 9 or 10. You need a GPA of at least 3.0, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. Contact Kody Beaver, holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.
duration: About 1 week (July 19 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: $125 non-refundable registration fee, charged only to accepted students

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9, 10 or 11. You need a GPA of at least 3.2, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math. You want a science career.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. You contact your assigned mentor before the program. Expect to work some evenings. Contact Kody Beaver, holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.
duration: About 1 week (July 12 to 19 in 2026)
pay_detail: $125 non-refundable registration fee for accepted students

who_can_apply: Students of all backgrounds and experience levels. The IU O'Neill School page says middle and high school students. Exact ages are not stated.

notes: Labs may be cancelled if too few students sign up, and you would be offered another lab. Camp size is limited. The camp says it is cheaper than many other university camps.
duration: About 1 week (check-in July 5, check-out July 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: housing and meals $950 ($150 deposit plus $800 tuition); commuter with meals $750; commuter without meals $500. Scholarships awarded on a rolling basis after May 15.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 18. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form on the workshop page. A liability form and details are emailed before the workshop.
notes: Drop-off and pick-up are at the Franklin Hall commons atrium (601 E Kirkwood Ave). This is separate from the summer HSJI program.
duration: 1 day, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. Lunch is provided.

who_can_apply: Ballet intensive: ages 13 to 18, admitted by a filmed prescreen of a classical variation. Contemporary intensive: ages 14 to 18, must have completed grade 8, no screening.
how_to_apply: Online registration form and $100 fee; ballet applicants upload a private YouTube link to a classical variation. Do not pay tuition until accepted. Then submit the Participant Agreement Form.
notes: Intense schedule (Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM). The student pays; this is not a job.
duration: 1 to 3 weeks: June 6-12, June 13-19 (ballet) and June 20-26 (contemporary), 2027
pay_detail: Tuition $1,000 per one-week session ($2,000 for two, $3,000 for three) plus $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals $550 per session; commuter meal plan $115 per session.

who_can_apply: High school age (pre-college) and undergraduate brass players. The page gives no exact age range. You send a placement recording for ensemble placement.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Also upload a placement recording to the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Confirm 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 27 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $750 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional youth housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 on brass, woodwinds, voice, strings or rhythm instruments. No audition to get in, but you send a placement recording.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Then upload a placement recording that has not been edited. YouTube links are fine. Use the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Check the 2027 dates and prices before you plan.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: Tuition $775 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices). Need-based aid and merit awards exist.

who_can_apply: Students currently in grades 8 to 12 who play in band or orchestra. Jazz band requires an audition on the first day.
how_to_apply: Online registration form plus the $100 registration fee, tuition by the payment deadline, then a Participant Agreement Form. Contact: musicsp@iu.edu.
notes: Costs and dates are from the 2026 session page. The student pays; this is not a job. The Jacobs Academy also lists other pre-college summer programs.
duration: One week (June 14 to 20 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026: residential tuition $1,120 (housing and meals); commuter tuition $815 (lunch and dinner); $100 non-refundable registration fee credited to tuition. Need-based financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Serious pianists ages 12 to 19. You must be able to practice several hours a day. You should play music that is early advanced to advanced. The director can admit exceptional students under 12. You must audition with a recording.
how_to_apply: Pay the $100 fee in the online sign-up form. Then upload a list of the music you play and two different pieces you play from memory. Send them as recordings to the Jacobs audition portal. Pay tuition only after you are accepted.
notes: The director is Dr. Elizabeth Yao (elizyao@iu.edu). Check the 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 2 weeks (June 27 to July 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $2,400 plus a $100 deposit credited to tuition (2026 prices). Housing and meal plans cost extra. Financial aid and scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18. You send a placement recording so you can be placed in studios and groups.
how_to_apply: Finish the online sign-up and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Then upload a recording for placement in the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Confirm 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 1 week (July 5 to 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $900 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices). Need-based aid exists.

who_can_apply: Serious string players ages 12 to 18. You must audition by recording.
how_to_apply: Pay the $100 fee in the online sign-up form. Then upload two different pieces as recordings to the Jacobs audition portal. YouTube links are fine. Pay tuition only after you are accepted.
notes: Directed by Prof. Mimi Zweig (zweig@iu.edu). Confirm 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 4 weeks (June 20 to July 18 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $3,200 plus a $100 audition fee credited to tuition (2026 prices). Housing and meal plans cost extra. Need-based aid and merit scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Any high school student. Only 50 team spots are available.
how_to_apply: Apply online. It is first come, first served.
notes: The page shows the August 28 and October 3 dates without a year; the date has already passed this fall. Travel costs are not discussed on the page. Expect it to repeat in fall 2027 but confirm.
duration: One day (Saturday)
pay_detail: No cost to apply or attend

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 who want to explore cybersecurity. Students with little or no technical background are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. Contact the summer camp team at luddycmp@iu.edu or Joshua Streiff at jostre@iu.edu.
notes: Costs money. It is a camp, not a job. The page does not say whether it is residential or a day camp. Ask the summer camp team.
duration: 1 week, June 2027 (exact dates not set)
pay_detail: Program fee $300.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Applications open in January 2027 through the Luddy high school programs page. Contact the summer camp team at luddycmp@iu.edu or Joshua Streiff at jostre@iu.edu.
notes: Costs money. It is a camp, not a job. The same page lists the Luddy Cybersecurity Immersion Camp, which has its own card.
duration: Residential camp, July 2027 (exact dates not set)
pay_detail: Program fee $950. It covers on-campus lodging, meals and activities.

who_can_apply: High school students completing grades 9 to 12. Only 20 students are accepted from around the country.
how_to_apply: Email Program Director Ansley Valentine (arvalent@iu.edu). Send a photo and a resume of your stage and backstage theatre work. Then you get audition materials.
notes: Costs a lot, so ask about aid. Run with Stages Bloomington. Confirm 2027 dates and cost with the program before applying.
duration: 3 weeks
pay_detail: Tuition is $4,575 with housing and meals. A $500 non-refundable deposit is due on acceptance and the other $4,075 is due June 5 (2026 terms).

who_can_apply: High school students finishing junior year with a GPA of at least 3.0 out of 4.0. You like leading and community work. Clubs and your application essays count too.
how_to_apply: Apply online with an application and essays. Check the box on the form if you want a travel scholarship. Questions: iurlp@iu.edu.
notes: Check the page in the fall for 2027 dates. The page does not say if housing is on campus.
duration: 5 days (June 21 to 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free if accepted. You pay your own travel to Bloomington and spending money. Travel scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors with a GPA of at least 3.0, recommended by a principal or guidance counselor, living with a parent or guardian within commuting distance of campus. IU GPA of at least 2.5 is also required once enrolled.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, then email openprgm@iu.edu for the form and instructions.
notes: Only for students who live close enough to commute to Bloomington. Costs are real college credit fees. Not a job.
duration: One or more courses per term (fall, spring or summer)
pay_detail: Students pay the regular IU undergraduate credit-hour and mandatory fees (student health fee waived). Dollar amounts are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students. Most come with a teacher or school group, but the page says exceptions can be made. Email essi@iu.edu to ask.
how_to_apply: Email the ESSI team at essi@iu.edu to ask about attending. Registration opens in fall 2026.
notes: Most students attend with a teacher or school group. The page says exceptions can be made if you email essi@iu.edu.
duration: 1 day (9:30 AM to 2:30 PM in the sample schedule)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 3 to 12 can enroll in regular 4-H. You must enroll every year.
how_to_apply: Enroll online in 4HOnline (the 'Click here to enroll' link on the county page). Call Purdue Extension Monroe County at 812-349-2575 for help.
notes: County 4-H camp is for grades 3 to 8, so older teens do not use it. The Extension office is at 3400 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47401. This is a youth club, not a paid job.
duration: Program year starts Oct 1
pay_detail: $20 enrollment fee per member for grades 3 to 12 ($5 for Mini 4-H, grades K to 2).

who_can_apply: The city says it connects volunteers of all ages. Each posting sets its own rules, so check the listing for age limits.

notes: You need an account on the volunteer network site. Parks volunteer pages on the city site list events, camps and clean-ups but do not state ages.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer opportunities

who_can_apply: Teens entering at least 7th grade in the fall of the next school year. Teens apply with the Teen Volunteer Application; adults 18 and over use a separate form.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application (online form linked on the Become a Volunteer page), then register for a volunteer orientation. Contact: Volunteer Manager, 812-337-1337 ext. 221.
notes: Middle and high school volunteers work alongside college students and adults. Some roles (parties, outreach) need prior museum experience and training. Outreach events require your own transportation.
duration: Ongoing; flexible hours
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Perks: free admission, 20 percent off in the gift store

who_can_apply: The Become a Volunteer page says WonderCamp applicants must be entering grade 9 in the fall of the next school year. The internships page says entering grades 9-12 or home-school equivalent, and graduating seniors may also apply. Required training is held at University Elementary School.
how_to_apply: Apply with the Teen Volunteer Application on WonderLab's Become a Volunteer page, choosing the WonderCamp internship; special training sessions are listed on the application form. Contact: 812-337-1337 ext. 221.
notes: Unpaid. The Become a Volunteer page says WonderCamp interns must be entering grade 9 in the fall of the next school year, while the internship page says entering grades 9 to 12; use the stricter reading (grade 9 or older) unless WonderLab says otherwise.
duration: Summer camp weeks; training also required the Saturday before each camp week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer internship (the page describes it as volunteering your time)

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8. Letters of recommendation are not needed but are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out the yearly application during an open window. You share your interests and recent wins. You also share your goals for college and a career.
notes: For younger teens. Eighth graders are encouraged to apply to King Scholars at the high school level. Cost is not stated on the page.
duration: Saturdays in October and November (fall) or April and May (spring)
pay_detail: Not stated. No cost is listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grade 9, 10, 11 or 12 when they apply. Spring applicants must be in grades 9 to 11. A parent or guardian must attend onboarding.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the fall or spring window. Check the King Scholars page for the application and how to prepare.
notes: The Brookfield Zoo volunteer page says its regular volunteer forms are for adults. It says this program is its chance for high school students. Grade 8 graduates can join KCLA Transitions. Grade 12 students are not accepted in spring. Scholars who take part a lot can apply for seasonal jobs.
duration: Year-round. At least 80 engagement hours each year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include zoo access like a basic membership, ten free admission passes, and discounts. Scholars commit to at least 80 hours a year.

who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors (grades 10 to 12) interested in art and design.
how_to_apply: Register online and pay the $250 registration fee. Scholarship applicants submit a form, a 300 to 500 word personal statement, three artwork samples and a NACAC fee waiver.
notes: Fees shown are the 2026 prices. Meals are included on weekdays. Refunds: tuition balance less the registration fee is refunded in full if withdrawn by June 15, 2026 and half by June 29, 2026.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to 25)
pay_detail: Commuter $3,000 total ($2,750 tuition and fees plus a $250 registration fee). Residential $3,600 total (adds $600 room and board). Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Junior counselors are 16 to 17 years old. Applicants need three written references from people who are not close relatives.
how_to_apply: Complete the camp job application (opens in December) and have three references fill out the reference form. Contact Andy Davis, Camp Director, at (217) 333-3955 or ardavis1@illinois.edu.
notes: Staff live on site during camp weeks. Program staff and senior counselors must be 18 or older. Illinois work permit rules were not checked.
duration: 2026 plan: paid training May 26 to June 1, then counselor sessions June 2 to July 30 (Camp Corral July 5 to 10)
pay_detail: Salary plus room and board. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The page says PRE-CE adds research spots for students with strong interest and promise. That includes students from rural or under-served communities. It runs next to researcHStart (a separate card).
how_to_apply: Application materials come out each fall. For PRE-CE, contact Stephanie Dietrich. She is the Senior Manager for Education. Her email is sdrich@illinois.edu.
notes: PRE-CE runs at the same time as researcHStart. The Cancer Center at Illinois is a host site for it. For researcHStart you must be 16 or older. You apply online with two recommendations and then have an in-person interview. The stipend is taxable. Dates for 2027 are not posted. Past summers ran from the second full week of June to the first week of August.
duration: About 8 weeks, 40 hours a week, from the second full week of June to the first week of August
pay_detail: $4,000 taxable stipend

who_can_apply: High school volunteers must be 14 or older. Students must provide up-to-date immunization records.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button under 'Students (college/teen)' on the Carle Foundation Hospital volunteer page (opens an online application) and send immunization records.
notes: The next listed deadline is the spring term deadline of November 15; confirm the year and current rules with Carle Volunteer Services. Other Carle sites list their own teen age ranges.
duration: By term (fall, spring, summer)
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who meet at least one condition, such as low family income, a disability, being a school dropout, homeless or foster youth, or needing extra help to finish school or get a job.
how_to_apply: The page gives no workNet address or walk-in hours. General CCRPC office: 1776 E Washington St, Urbana, IL 61802, (217) 328-3313.
notes: Eligibility rules apply, so not every teen qualifies. Call to ask about summer paid placements. The workforce site may be updated separately at eciwork.net. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated for youth. A separate Work Experience page says qualified interns can have up to 240 hours of wages covered.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 and up, with basic computer knowledge. A 9 year old who turns 10 by September 1 can ask for an exception.
how_to_apply: Register one camper per camp online when registration opens, with a $20 non-refundable deposit. Call 217-265-5342 with questions.
notes: The 2026 page says registration is closed. 2027 dates are not posted.
duration: 1 week per camp (2026 camps June 8 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Price not stated on the page. The page says free or reduced price camps may be offered to qualifying families (scholarship waiver page).

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 17. Candidates are picked through an application and interview.
how_to_apply: Email or call Stacey Clementz at the Homer Lake Interpretive Center, (217) 896-2455, or use the online volunteer application on the page.
notes: Youth program volunteers (school programs, September to May) and public program volunteers are also listed on the page; age rules for those are not stated. The District also has public volunteer events that need no application.
duration: Summer day camps (June to July per the volunteer page); weekly hours not stated
pay_detail: Volunteer position.

who_can_apply: Ages 10 to 15. Pre-registration is required.
how_to_apply: Call 217-344-7297 or visit the shelter to enroll. Payment is due when you enroll.
notes: The page does not mention volunteer age minimums. Ask the shelter about teen volunteering.
duration: Meets the 2nd Tuesday of each month, 4:00 to 5:30 pm. Four sessions a year (spring, summer, fall, winter)
pay_detail: $35 for a 3 month membership (includes a T-shirt).

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list an age range or require 4-H membership.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through ZSuite (Illinois 4-H event sign-up) when it opens. Ask for the Trailblazer scholarship in the same sign-up.
notes: Stay at Bousfield Hall, 1214 S. First St., Champaign. Refunds in 2026 had to be requested in writing by May 15. Questions: illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
duration: About 4 days, Sunday to Thursday (2026: June 21 to 25). June 2027 dates are expected.
pay_detail: 2026 price was $500 base fee plus a fee for each academy ($550 base if registered late). 2027 prices are not posted. Campus parking was $60 for the week. Need-based Trailblazer scholarships were offered.

who_can_apply: High school students with little or no Arabic. The page lists no grade or age rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and pay the $25 fee. Send a high school transcript, a note from a teacher and a scholarship form. Counselors email transcripts to silmw-uiuc@illinois.edu.
notes: The page says an early admission date gives a better chance at the largest scholarship. Dates and deadlines may change by spring. Contact: linguistics@illinois.edu, (217) 244-0661.
duration: 2 weeks, June 13 to 26, 2027 (residential)
pay_detail: Tuition is not listed on the program pages. There is a $25 application fee and a $250 deposit after admission. Scholarships are awarded based on financial need and/or academic merit. The page says its 2026 program was funded by a Qatar Foundation International grant.

who_can_apply: High school students who are rising sophomores through seniors. Students come from around the country.
how_to_apply: Register on the page starting Nov 1, 2026. For the scholarship, also submit a one-page essay on why you want to be an architect by the deadline.
notes: Contact: Elizabeth Abosch, eabosch2@illinois.edu. There are no refunds if you cancel, miss days or come for part of it. Sign up early, because spots fill.
duration: One week, July 11 to 17, 2027 (residential, on campus)
pay_detail: Program fee $1,300 (includes lodging and meals). The page also mentions a $100 non-refundable fee. A partial-tuition scholarship for two students is offered (apply with a one-page essay).

who_can_apply: Each camp lists its own ages. In 2026 camps were for ages 10 and up (some 10 to 17, some 12 and up). Check the age before registering.
how_to_apply: Registration opens when 2027 details are posted on the MakerLab summer page. A $20 non-refundable deposit applies.
notes: 2026 camps ran June 1 to July 31. Lunch supervision and late pickup were $10 a day each.
duration: 1 week, 3 hours a day (morning or afternoon sessions)
pay_detail: $250 a week in 2026. Optional lunch hour supervision and late pickup were $10 a day each.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors at Champaign-Urbana high schools (per the College of LAS page). You should be curious about science and health.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Email uiuc-spheres@illinois.edu.
notes: The LAS page lists neuroscience, molecular and integrative physiology and sociology as research areas. Ask about the exact eligibility because the two pages describe it differently.
duration: 6 weeks in summer (exact dates not posted)
pay_detail: $2,400 summer stipend for successful participation

who_can_apply: Junior high and senior high music students. The 2026 senior band page said students completing grades 8 to 12. Students bring their own instruments. Some ensembles need an audition video.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the ISYM site when it opens. Questions: music@illinois.edu or 217-333-2620. Students must provide their own instruments.
notes: Prices were checked for the senior band only. The 2026 senior session was July 6 to 11. Read each ensemble page for its cost and rules.
duration: 1 week per ensemble
pay_detail: 2026 Senior Band cost: $775 resident (housing and meals) or $575 commuter. Other ensembles may differ.

who_can_apply: Anyone age 16 or older who meets the health requirements and passes a background check. The page has no separate teen program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application. Show your shot records. Finish a background check. To reach Volunteer Services, call (217) 443-5279. Or write to SHMC.VolunteerServices@osfhealthcare.org.
notes: The hospital page now uses the name OSF Sacred Heart Medical Center - Urbana. The page does not say if the application is open right now, so call first. The page does not show an application link.
duration: 3 to 4 hours a week for at least 6 months (encouraged)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: The page says 15 year olds can apply for lifeguard and swim instructor. Minimum ages for other jobs are not stated; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the District's job listings (linked from the Employment Opportunities page). Aquatics questions: Ryan Hays, ryan.hays@champaignparks.org. HR: hr@champaignparks.org.
notes: Lifeguard classes are run by the District in Champaign-Urbana. Concession workers get a paid-for Food Handler's certification. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).

pay_detail: Paid job. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages. Lifeguard certification is covered 100% by the Park District.

who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 years old who are enthusiastic, hardworking and willing to learn. Teen volunteers may work at most 25 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal, then view opportunities. Questions: volunteer@champaignparks.org.
notes: Some roles (for example Prairie Farm) run only part of the year.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid. Hours can count toward high school volunteer requirements.

who_can_apply: At least 15 years old, attending an area high school or home-schooled, with course prerequisites and assessment requirements met. For high school credit you also need your school's approval and good standing.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply page under Dual Credit. Early College Services: 217-353-2663, earlycollege@parkland.edu (office U214).
notes: Early College students do not qualify for financial aid. Credit and grades go on a permanent Parkland transcript. The Early College page also lists an Early College and Career Academy with programs such as Automotive Technology, Certified Nurse Assistant and EMS.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Tuition is not stated on this page. It says courses are affordable and in some cases reduced or tuition-free.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 18. Each camp sets its own age range, and the student must meet it by the first day of camp.
how_to_apply: Register online at parkland.edu/ceRegister, by phone at 217-351-2235, or in person at Community Education, 1315 North Mattis Ave, Champaign. Ask about scholarships on the page.
notes: Camps cost money. Check each camp page for its price and ages. Scholarships are for families with financial need and are first-come, first-served.
duration: Varies by camp
pay_detail: Fee varies by camp. The page says scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Any junior or senior in the Parkland College district. Home school and private school students can apply through the ECCA office.
how_to_apply: Ask your high school counselor for the ECCA application, apply to Parkland as an Early College student if needed, and return the ECCA form with a parent signature to your counselor. Call 217-355-1382 or email nelder@efe.k12.il.us.
notes: Students need their own ride to Parkland and to off-campus clinical or job-site visits. ECCA follows the Parkland calendar, not the high school calendar.
duration: Mostly a full school year; classes 7:30 to 9:30 am on Parkland days
pay_detail: Not a job. Many high schools pay the cost, but it varies. The FAQ says financial aid is not available for dual credit students. Textbooks are loaned.

who_can_apply: High school and homeschooled students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2026 who live in the Unit 4, Urbana or Rantoul school districts.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Summer Start link on the Parkland page. A student and parent orientation is required. Contact summerstart@parkland.edu or 217-353-2346.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted yet. MTD bus vouchers were offered to students in Champaign, Urbana and Savoy who needed a ride to campus.
duration: 2026: June 1 to June 11, Monday to Thursday, 3 hours a day
pay_detail: Up to $250, paid at the end for attendance. Each missed day lowers the total.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20. Members must keep a passing GPA and complete community service.
how_to_apply: Download the application on the city page, sign it, and mail or drop it off to Champaign Police Department, ATTN: Youth Police Explorer Post 258, 82 E. University Ave., Champaign, IL 61820. Questions: Detective Michael Talbott, 217-403-6900.

duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 17 years old who can give four hours a week, Monday to Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., for at least six months in a row. Needs TB test and MMR and chickenpox records.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the page. Rush replies by email in 5 to 7 business days. The email has steps for orientation and a health screening. Contact: volunteer_services@rush.edu, (312) 942-5574.
notes: No summer-only volunteering. No weekend or evening shifts. Volunteer Services does not offer internships or externships. Under 17 does not qualify here. The page lists general hospital numbers for Rush Copley (630-978-6200) and Rush Oak Park (708-383-9300). These are not volunteer lines. Contact Volunteer Services at (312) 942-5574.
duration: At least 6 months, 4 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 100 hours you can ask a staff member for a reference letter.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18. The 1.0 college-credit option is for juniors and seniors ages 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses on the Early College Program page. For the Smith Scholarship, fill out the scholarship form. Upload your household 1040 and send in three pieces of art to SlideRoom. For need-based aid, say yes at sign-up and upload the 1040 in DocuSign.
notes: Costs money unless you win the Smith Scholarship or aid. Aid is first come, first served.
duration: 10-week courses in fall and spring; the page does not state a summer course length
pay_detail: Noncredit 10-week course $661; 1.0 college credit course $1,982; supplies about $50 to $200 extra. The Smith Scholarship covers 100% of noncredit course tuition for Illinois students. Limited need-based aid.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed their sophomore year by the time of the program. Merit scholarships are open to all students; need-based aid is for US residents.
how_to_apply: Register online when sign-up opens November 1. When you sign up, you can also apply for a merit scholarship or need-based aid.
notes: The page says registration opens November 1 but gives no year. It probably means this coming November for summer 2027, so confirm. The site menu also lists an online version (ECPOSI). Its details were not on the page.
duration: 1, 2 or 4 weeks. 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31.
pay_detail: Tuition is $1,908 for 1 week, $3,816 for 2 weeks and $7,632 for 4 weeks. The page also lists housing and meal plan costs, supplies and personal spending. A $100 non-refundable tuition deposit applies to students who apply for aid or scholarships. Merit scholarships and limited need-based aid (US residents) are offered.

who_can_apply: High school students from the Chicago area. The page lists no age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the Young Adult Council page for the next application. Questions: teenprograms@steppenwolf.org.
notes: Members see Steppenwolf plays and many Chicago plays for free. Steppenwolf also runs free Step In theatre workshops and Teen Takeover nights, which have cheap tickets to shows. Join the teen email list on the Teen Programs page for updates.
duration: Weekly Wednesday meetings at Steppenwolf
pay_detail: Weekly meetings appear unpaid; the page says community engagement and extra leadership work is paid. Rates not stated.

who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents who are sophomores, juniors or seniors in 2026-27. You need a B or 3.0 average and a household income under $80,000 a year. You must be able to keep the daily schedule.
how_to_apply: Sign up at the apply portal. Upload your transcript, resume, essay and an income form signed by a parent or guardian. Name two people who will recommend you. Contact: info@chicagobusinessinstitute.org or (312) 545-7855.
notes: The site shows two email endings, org and com; use the org address on the apply page. The apply page does not state pay or job sites. The home page says the program was founded to provide paid summer internships and mentions placements (one student interned with the City of Chicago), but no pay amount is given, so ask the office. Two recommendation letters are needed, so ask early. Illinois work permit rule not checked.
duration: Six weeks
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. Ask the office.

who_can_apply: You must have been in CPS this year and last year. You will be a junior or senior. You have a strong record in the hardest courses you can take. You are ready for college work.
how_to_apply: Fill out an online application. It has short essays, a graded work sample, a teacher recommendation and transcripts. It also has an online interview in mid-August. For the $0 tuition option, you need financial aid papers.
notes: UChicago classes do not follow the CPS calendar, so you attend even when your high school is on break. Many students stop after Winter Quarter.
duration: Autumn, Winter and Spring Quarters; one course per quarter
pay_detail: $800 tuition plus $75 lifetime transcript fee (books not included) if household income is over $60,000. $0 tuition, with books and fees covered, if under $60,000.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors or seniors who are at least 16 by June 14, 2027 and live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana. College freshmen and sophomores can also apply. Must commit to both summers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in recommendations. At least one must be a teacher or professor. Up to 12 applicants are accepted.
notes: You must find your own housing and ride to UChicago. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. One application covers all the UChicago cancer pathway programs that fit you.
duration: Two summers of 8 weeks (2027: June 14 to Aug 6, 35 to 40 hours a week) plus monthly 2 to 4 hour online sessions from Feb 2027 to Dec 2028
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $5,000 per year

who_can_apply: Full-time high school students who live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, and can attend every weekday, 4 hours a day. Up to 20 students per year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: Virtual program run with Kentucky, Michigan, Penn and UT Austin. No minimum age is listed. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for the stipend.
duration: 2 weeks, July 12 to 23, 2027, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to noon CT, online
pay_detail: $500 taxable stipend

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old (some roles need 18+). Applicants for the Summer Volunteer Program must be at least 18 at the time the application is submitted. Must interview, pass health screening, a drug screen and a background check, and not hold certain visas (B-1, B-2, H-1B, H-4).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Volunteer application. Do it when a recruiting window is open. The form is in Volgistics. Then you talk with Volunteer Services in an interview. For questions, write to vservices@uchicagomedicine.org. You can also call 773-702-4421.
notes: The page says student volunteers must be at least 16, and some opportunities need 18 or older. The summer program opens in early March 2027. One summer block says applicants must be 18 at submission, while the FAQ says the summer rules match the others (16). Confirm the summer age rule.
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for at least 6 months or one school year; 100 hours within a year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, are at least 16 by June 14, 2027, and can commit to all 8 weeks. Max 30 students across all sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Pick your site: UChicago, UIC, UIUC, Northwestern downtown or Rush. Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: No housing or ride is provided, so pick only sites you can reach. The application asks for your GPA and a transcript. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027, 35 to 40 hours a week
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $4,000

who_can_apply: High school students. The application shows which programs you are eligible for based on your current grade. Chicagoland students can choose to commute for Career Insight and Immersion.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a profile, transcript, writing sample, supplement and one recommendation letter. It also needs a parent okay and the $75 fee. Test scores are not required. You may rank up to four program choices but can be admitted to one.
notes: Expensive, not a job. Apply by the priority deadline if you need financial aid. Aid is limited and first come, first served.
duration: Varies by program. Online courses run 3 to 5 weeks and the language institute runs 6 to 8 weeks; the page does not state a length for enrichment.
pay_detail: Costs in 2026: Enrichment $3,000; Career Insight $5,890 ($4,100 commuting); Immersion $9,300 ($6,100 commuting); Practicum $15,200; online 3 to 5 weeks $4,980. Need-based partial aid is offered (not full), and Enrichment fees can be waived for income under $125,000. $75 application fee.

who_can_apply: For the Tech and AI day in 2026: students entering grade 10, 11 or 12 with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA, interested in business and in UIC for fall 2027. Rules for the other days were not posted.
how_to_apply: Email bizsummer@uic.edu or call 312-996-2700 to ask about 2027. The 2026 events used an online registration form on the UIC events site.
notes: Seats were limited and filled. Grade and GPA rules above are from only one of the four days, so confirm before applying.
duration: One series of four days, June 23 to 26, 2026 (each day run by a different department)
pay_detail: The Tech and AI day was free with breakfast and lunch. Cost for other days was not stated.

who_can_apply: The page says the program includes 25 neighborhood high school teens, run with After School Matters. The page does not list an age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply link on the Youth Farm page (an online form). Questions: Aurea France, Manager of Education and Wellness, per the page.
notes: Run in partnership with After School Matters. Confirm ages, dates and pay before relying on this. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.
duration: Spring, summer and fall growing seasons
pay_detail: Stipend: 4 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 hours a week in summer. Rate not stated.

who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job. The youngest age in the whole program is 14, but most summer jobs are for 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.
notes: The FAQ says youth 16 and older do not need a work permit. Some pages on the site are leftovers from old years, so trust the FAQ and the City press release for 2026. Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 and 15 who live in Chicago. At least half of participants come from priority groups (for example youth with disabilities, English learners, youth in foster care or experiencing homelessness).
how_to_apply: Apply through the online Chicago Youth Works application. Youth under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form if offered a position. Partner agencies contact applicants directly.
notes: The Chicago Youth Works FAQ says youth under 16 may be required to have a work permit; Illinois law requires one for most under-16 jobs, issued through the school district or ISBE. Ask the program whether a stipend program needs one. The FAQ says the Chicago Housing Authority, After School Matters and DFSS each also have a limited number of slots for 14 and 15 year olds.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Volunteer Application, submit a school recommendation form from a teacher, counselor or administrator, interview, finish health screenings, pass the orientation quiz and attend the mandatory orientation.
notes: The hospital's general volunteer program is age 16 and up. Perks listed include free parking, a food voucher, a free uniform and a free TB test. The next cycle should be the December 30 spring deadline, but the page gives no year, so confirm.
duration: Summer: first week of June to first week of August, 40 hours minimum. Fall and spring: 60 hours minimum. One 4 hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Volunteer team applicants should be in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer team form linked on the 10x10 Teen Art Expo page when applications open. Teen artists (age and grade rules for artists are not stated) can submit art when submissions open in mid November 2026. Museum phone: 513-721-2787.
notes: The museum has other volunteer groups. They are docents, visitor service aides, REC volunteers and CAM Cruiser volunteers. The main volunteer page does not state ages for them. Ask the museum before applying to those.
duration: The team meets 4 to 6 p.m. on the first Thursday of each month plus extra dates as needed, and must be free for the opening on Saturday April 10, 2027. The exhibition runs April 6 to 11, 2027.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer team

who_can_apply: The Clubs are open to youth ages 5 to 18 across Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. All youth are welcome, with no income rules. The page does not give an age range for the teen Workforce Development program itself.
how_to_apply: Click Enroll Today on the Join the Clubs page (it goes to the Club portal), or contact your preferred Club for help with the application. After acceptance, families get any extra forms. Phone: 513-421-8909. Email: info@bgcgc.org. Main office: 1205 Dewey Ave., Cincinnati, OH 45205.
notes: Confirm first. The pages do not list teen ages, teen hours, or any teen jobs. No Junior Staff program is mentioned. Clubs are at Price Hill, Avondale, Eastgate and East Westwood in Ohio. They are at Newport and Covington in Kentucky. There is also a Western & Southern Workforce Development Center.
duration: Summer: June 1 to July 31, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. School year: August 17 to May 14, Monday to Friday, 2:30 to 7:30 p.m. (hours vary by Club).
pay_detail: Free. The summer and school year programs are listed as completely free. The page does not say that teens are paid.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in high school or home-schooled, ages 14 to 18. It is a select group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the C-YA Teen Council application form on the page.
notes: The CAC teen page also lists a free Young Adult Lab on Thursdays 4 to 6 pm (open to all teens) and a Teen Art Show for ages 13 to 19. The page says enrollment for the 26-27 school year has begun and does not post a 2027-28 date. Call 513-345-8400 to confirm the current schedule.
duration: September to May, one meeting a month
pay_detail: Free to join. Dinner is provided at meetings. Perks: free admission, discounted tickets, field trips to museums and universities in another city.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Advanced dancers who have at least two full years on pointe. No audition.
how_to_apply: Sign up online when it opens. Use the Learn more link for the Ballet Intensive on the CCM Prep teen programs page.
notes: The opening date is only given as January 2027, so no day is stored. Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu.
duration: June 5 to 13, 2027 (housing check-in June 4)
pay_detail: Tuition $750. Housing is an extra $1,000.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders with a strong interest in musical theatre. An audition (video) is required.
how_to_apply: Audition through Acceptd. Choose CCM Prep: Musical Theatre Intensive. Get ready a headshot and a resume. Prepare a 60 to 90 second speech and two different songs. Send a 30 to 60 second video of you dancing alone.
notes: Housing is optional and costs extra. Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu. Tuition assistance may exist; ask CCM Prep.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks. 2027 sessions: June 14 to 20 or July 12 to 18 (1 week); June 14 to 26 or July 12 to 24 (2 weeks)
pay_detail: Tuition: $1,000 per 1-week session or $2,000 per 2-week session. Housing is an extra fee ($1,000 for a week, $1,800 for two weeks). $35 audition fee; email ccmsummer@ucmail.uc.edu about fee waivers.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12 who play a string instrument. You need to audition. You also need one letter of support.
