how_to_apply: Audition through Acceptd. Choose CCM Prep: Strings Intensive. Send a headshot and two different pieces, 8 to 10 minutes in all. Send a letter from a teacher or pro.
notes: Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu.
duration: June 5 to 12, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition $900. $35 audition fee; email ccmsummer@ucmail.uc.edu about fee waivers.

who_can_apply: High school seniors who are about to graduate, from the Cincinnati area.
how_to_apply: Apply online between Nov 1 and Feb 1. Questions: hssummerinternship@cchmc.org.
notes: The page does not give the year for Nov 1 and Feb 1; the year is inferred from the line that the new program starts in summer 2027. More details are to be posted. Pay and exact dates are not posted yet.
duration: One month, starting summer 2027
pay_detail: Not stated for the new program. The program page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. The old program was a paid, part-time position.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade. Seniors still in high school in spring must use the high school application.
how_to_apply: Submit the application packet by the posted due date, then attend a parent information session, an in-person interview and an orientation. Medical screening and a background check are required.
notes: Competitive: only the highest scoring applicants are accepted. Volunteers must complete at least 80 percent of their scheduled shifts. The hospital does not arrange job shadowing or senior capstone hours through Volunteer Services.
duration: Weekly 2 to 3 hour shift; Summer 2026 session
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Cincinnati Public Schools juniors and seniors with good grades. You show you are responsible. A counselor must say yes.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor. The page says counselor approval is required.
notes: Only for students at Cincinnati Public Schools. The source is a district news story, so ask your counselor for the current rules, pay and dates.
duration: 6 to 8 weeks
pay_detail: Not stated. The district news story, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Ask your counselor.

who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 15 or older, hold current American Red Cross Lifeguard Training/First Aid and CPR for the Professional Rescuer/AED certifications, and pass a water skills test. The page does not give an age for gate or pool monitors.
how_to_apply: Register for the required lifeguard course screening on the page, then apply to the open positions. Questions: CRC Aquatics, 513-357-7665.
notes: Lifeguards also attend pre-season and on-site pool training and pass an annual water skills review. Check the page for current screening dates. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Seasonal and part-time; dates not stated
pay_detail: Paid; rate not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Live in the City of Cincinnati or a surrounding community and be 14 to 24. A limited number of positions are for ages 14 and 15. Under 18, a parent or guardian signs the hiring forms; under 16 you need a work permit.
how_to_apply: Create a free account at governmentjobs.com, then apply to the Y2WK job at agency.governmentjobs.com/cincinnati. Only online applications are accepted. Applicants are contacted by phone or email for an interview.
notes: Very competitive: WVXU reported more than 1,000 teens applied last year and about 6 percent were hired. The CRC page says ages 14 to 24 and residents of the city or surrounding communities; an older City HR FAQ says only City residents ages 14 to 18, so confirm. The CRC FAQ still lists 2019 start dates, so ignore those. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Summer; roughly June to early August, dates vary by partner
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Adults can volunteer too. Groups of 10 or more can volunteer together. Great Parks supports Eagle Scout, Gold Award and senior capstone projects.
how_to_apply: Watch the Great Parks volunteer page for the March 2027 information sessions and use the Email Volunteer Engagement link on that page to ask about the teen steps. The page does not show a teen application link. Group projects use the Request a Project Match form.
notes: Confirm first: the page gives no teen application steps or time commitment. Great Parks also lists one day volunteer projects; the page did not state a minimum age for them.
duration: Long term volunteering. Time commitment is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Hamilton County residents ages 14 to 21. You can join if your family income is low or if something makes it hard for you to get a job.
how_to_apply: Use the Youth Apply Here link on the county page. Phone 513-946-0400, email Hamil_yep@jfs.ohio.gov, daily 9 am to 4 pm.
notes: The county page says Harbor helps run the program. The Eligibility and Application tabs could not be read in the text copy. Check the income rules and the form on the page. Ohio work permit rules are not on the page.
duration: Year-round; summer jobs are a main part
pay_detail: $13 per hour

who_can_apply: Age 12 or older, able to commit to an ongoing schedule of 2 to 6 hours a week for three months or longer. A background check applies at age 18 and older. Court-mandated volunteers are not accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill in an application in the library's online volunteer system and pick a listing. Questions: 513-369-6968.
notes: Each branch listing sets its own details, so check the age on the listing you choose. The page also mentions meal-service and tutoring roles. It lists a separate Friends of the Library volunteer line at 513-369-6035.
duration: 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, from public, private, parochial, charter and homeschool backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Use the youth application link on the Youth Programs page when recruitment opens. Email youthprograms@cincymuseum.org to be notified.
notes: The program started in 1989. In the first summer teens shadow the Museum of Natural History and Science, The Children's Museum and the Cincinnati History Museum.
duration: Year-round through high school; first summer needs at least six shadowing sessions
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer; perks include free museum admission and parking

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18. The page says the program helps students meet service hour requirements for high school graduation and honor societies. Leader in Training is for ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application linked on the Youth Volunteer Opportunities page when recruiting reopens. Questions: volunteer@cincynature.org or (513) 965-3348. The youth opportunities page lists the main phone as (513) 831-1711.
notes: The pages checked do not give the street address. Check the Nature Center site for the location. Group service days, including for local high schools, remove invasive plants. The youth opportunities page says ages 13 to 18 may apply. It did not repeat the closed for 2026 wording. Check the status before you plan around it.
duration: Seasonal work tied to maple season and early spring. The time commitment is not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Groundwork ORV Green Team page. Contact info@groundworkorv.org or 513-301-0310.
notes: Work sites named by the City include Mt. Echo Park, Mt. Airy Forest, Mt. Storm, Caldwell Nature Preserve and Kennedy Heights Park. Pay, hours and the application window are not on the pages, so ask Groundwork ORV. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Summer; length not stated
pay_detail: Paid summer job; rate not stated

who_can_apply: Showcases are for campers entering grades 6 to 12. The page also lists academies for grades 1 to 6 or 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register online through the camp listings on the Playhouse website.
notes: Camps are at the Playhouse in Eden Park and at Mason Community Center. Before and after care cost extra. Ask the Playhouse about financial aid.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks, June 1 to July 31 in 2026
pay_detail: 2026 early bird tuition: $350 for one-week showcases, $750 for two-week Academies at the Playhouse ($720 for the 9-day week of June 15). Prices rose on March 1. 2027 prices are not posted.

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 through 18. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: The Youth Services page gives no link or dates for the Summer Cadet Program. Check that page or its Facebook page for news.
notes: The Summer Cadet Program section gives ages 16 to 18 and part-time summer work. It gives no pay, hours, dates or application link. The separate Public Safety Cadet program on the same page is for young adults. Confirm with the department.
duration: Part time over the summer; exact weeks not stated
pay_detail: Described as part-time summer work for the department. The wage is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school and college students ages 15 and older. The page does not list grade levels.
how_to_apply: Email one message to job_shadows@trihealth.com. Include these items. The Job Shadow Instructions. Your Application. The Risk and Release form. The Authorization to Treat Minors form. Your immunization records. The team does not match you to a department. Look at TriHealth's services and locations first.
notes: The TriHealth volunteer page says Good Samaritan and Bethesda North hospitals use adult and teen volunteers. It does not give a teen age or steps. Email volunteer@trihealth.com or call 513-862-2368 to ask. The job shadowing page does not mention a background check.
duration: Typically about 8 to 16 hours (varies by department or unit)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Camps are organized by age and interest level. Grade rules and fees are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list on the UC summer camps page. Then apply when 2027 sign up opens. Email CEASSummerCamps@ucmail.uc.edu.
notes: Confirm grade levels, cost and dates when the 2027 page is posted. Another UC camp, the Early IT Summer Camp, has its own card in this guide.
duration: Day camps; length not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: A fee applies; the amount is not stated on the program pages. Scholarships may be available for students who need financial help.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th graders through rising 12th graders who like technology. The camp FAQ page gives this grade range.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Here link on the Early IT Summer Camp page. Tell them in your application if cost or lack of resources could keep you from taking part. Questions: ucearlyit@ucmail.uc.edu. There is a parent or guardian orientation on Zoom.
notes: The camp page has a Registration is Now Open notice, but it gives no closing date and no year for the June 1 to 18 dates, so the status stays closed-expect-reopen until the year is confirmed. The camp FAQ page gives the grade range (rising 9th through rising 12th graders) and says the camp is free. Check the dates and status before sending a teen.
duration: June 1 to June 18, Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. The page does not state a year and calls it a one three-week day camp.
pay_detail: Free to attend. A light breakfast and lunch are provided each day. No pay.

who_can_apply: Eligible local high school students. Space is limited. Exact age and grade rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the page. Questions: UCH-HighSchools@UCHealth.com.
notes: Offered only at UC Medical Center, 3188 Bellevue Ave. The page says joining depends on space and on who qualifies. Age and grade rules are not stated.
duration: September to March, twice a month, 6 to 8 p.m., in person
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. For the UC Medical Center summer program you must be 16 by June 1. You need a TB test, MMR and varicella proof, and a yearly flu shot.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form for your site. Then go to an orientation and do a 20 minute phone interview. Email UCHVolunteerServices@UCHealth.com.
notes: Short term or one time volunteering is not offered. West Chester Hospital is at 7700 University Drive, West Chester, OH. Volunteers are unpaid, so no work permit is needed.
duration: UC Medical Center summer: June to mid-August. West Chester: fall (Oct to Dec), spring (Feb to May) and summer (June to July) sessions.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are 16 or older by August 1 of the program year (in 2026 that date was August 1, 2026). Previous research experience is not required.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application form. You also upload a 1 page resume style summary of your school work and activities. You upload a 1 page personal statement. You rank the session you prefer. Contact: Michele Glassmeyer, Michele.Glassmeyer@uc.edu, (513) 558-6351.
notes: Costs money. The price, session dates and age cutoff above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.
duration: One week per session, Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. In 2026 there were four sessions between June 1 and June 26.
pay_detail: $1,100 (2026 price). A limited number of scholarships and financial aid awards are available.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 19. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Youth page. Call the league if the form is closed.
notes: The Youth page also tells about a yearly city wide Youth Summit led by youth for youth. Its ages, cost and dates are not stated. Check the current summer dates and stipend with the league before you plan.
duration: 160 hours total, 20 hours per week (about 8 weeks)
pay_detail: A financial stipend; the amount is not stated. Work is 20 hours per week for 160 hours total.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. The page words the age rule as 13 to 17 on May 1, 2026, which looks like a leftover date for a 2027 season, so confirm.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application with essays, attend one group interview and two orientations, and set up an online profile to log hours.
notes: Orientation 1 is an online course with a guardian plus a session on April 24 or 25, 2027; Orientation 2 is all day at the Zoo on May 22 or 23, 2027. The Zoo says to contact them if the fee is a hardship. Third-year and older ZooTeens have a lower 70 hour requirement.
duration: Starts May 31, 2027; 100 hours for first and second year ZooTeens, including a 40 hour camp week
pay_detail: $60 non-refundable program fee on acceptance (volunteering is unpaid)

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 13 years old or in grades 7 to 12 during the 2026-2027 school year. The page says the teen program is currently full.
how_to_apply: Email teen@bexleylibrary.org to join the teen volunteer email list. That is how you hear about openings. The summer application opens April 1.
notes: The page says the library is postponing adult volunteering for now. Call the youth department with questions.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 12 who live in the Columbus area can join.
how_to_apply: Download the member form from the page. Email it to youthcouncil@cmafohio.org. You can also mail it to the Youth Advisory Council Coordinator at 1390 Dublin Road, Columbus, OH 43215.
notes: Time can count toward the community service hours you need to graduate. Ask the foundation if seats are open for 2026-2027. Email youthcouncil@cmafohio.org or call 614-240-7410.
duration: Not stated on the page.
pay_detail: No pay stated. Time can count toward community service hours needed to graduate.

who_can_apply: Ohio residents in grades 7 to 12. New students need a 3.0 unweighted GPA, or ACT or SAT scores that qualify, or Columbus State placement test scores that qualify. Middle schoolers must take the reading and writing placement tests. They must reach the needed score in at least one area.
how_to_apply: Give your school a Letter of Intent. Apply to Columbus State. There is no fee or essay. Finish online onboarding. Show that you meet one of the eligibility rules. Then sign up for classes with your counselor.
notes: The college application asks you to have your Social Security number ready. Use a personal email, not a school email. Send your unofficial high school transcripts or ACT/SAT scores to your CCP advisor.
duration: Semester courses
pay_detail: Courses and textbooks are free for public school students. Transportation and other costs are the student's.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21 in Franklin County. In general, families must meet the income rules for TANF cash help. Ages 14 to 15, 16 to 18 and 18 to 21 have their own tracks.
how_to_apply: Apply through one of the partner groups on the county page. They are Columbus Urban League, Godman Guild, Lead the Way Learning Academy, Nationwide Children's Hospital and Saint Stephen's Community House. Each lists its own phone and email.
notes: Check the partner pages in winter. The county page says nothing about work permits. Nationwide Children's and Columbus Urban League already have their own cards in this guide. Godman Guild and Lead the Way phone numbers are on the county page: 614-294-5476 and 614-915-0434.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Ages 14 to 15: $1,500 stipend plus up to $300 in incentives for finishing the 6 weeks. Ages 16 to 18: wages up to $15 per hour.

who_can_apply: The page says the program serves young adults in grades 9-12 and after high school graduation. Exact age rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth and Young Adult Workforce Program interest form on the Godman Guild page.
notes: Events listed: Entrepreneur Night Nov 18, Community Service Dec 3, Resume Building Jan 27, Public Speaking Feb 24, Money Skills Apr 7, Showcase May 6. Phone 614-294-5476. The Godman Guild site has an older Ready 2 Earn link that gives a 404. Use the teen page.
duration: Monthly sessions Nov 2026 to May 2027. Summer 2026 Ready 2 Earn ran 5 weeks and 60 hours.
pay_detail: Not stated on the Godman Guild pages. The Franklin County Ready 2 Earn page lists a stipend for ages 14 to 15 and wages for ages 16 to 18 through its partners.

who_can_apply: Teens 16 and 17 can volunteer on their own. A guardian must sign a Junior and Teen Volunteer Waiver and Release. Ages 12 to 15 can join only as junior volunteers, with an adult volunteer partner over the age of 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the New Volunteer Registration form. Then use the emailed link to book an in-person STEPS orientation in Hilliard. Next, finish species training and mentoring. Then start to book shifts.
notes: The FAQ lists a junior option for ages 12 to 15. It needs an adult volunteer partner over 21. Email volunteer@columbushumane.org with questions.
duration: 4 hours a month minimum
pay_detail: Unpaid. New volunteers pay a one-time $50 mission investment.

who_can_apply: Youth in or entering grades 6 to 12 who are at least 12 years old. High school students 18 or older must be returning to a traditional high school and may need a background check.
how_to_apply: Online VolunTeen application, first come first served by branch. If your branch is missing from the drop-down, it is full.
notes: Openings vary by branch. Current or recent youth volunteers should talk to the Summer Reading coordinator at their branch. The library also has School Help, Reading Buddies and Creation Station volunteer roles; the page lists the age rule only for the summer VolunTeen role. Ohio's work permit rules for unpaid public library volunteering are not stated on the page.
duration: June 1 to July 31 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Most assignments are for ages 16 and up. Ages 11 to 15 can help only at Inniswood Metro Gardens, as Junior Volunteers. The Inniswood training is in March.
how_to_apply: Attend a Volunteer Information session and complete the volunteer application. A background check including fingerprints is part of the process.
notes: Slate Run Living Historical Farm lets children volunteer with a parent or supervising adult. Scouts can set up group service days by email. For Inniswood contact the volunteer coordinator at 614-895-6226.
duration: Flexible schedule by assignment and park
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Sort and pack and the Kitchen are for ages 13 and up. Markets and kids' meals are 16 and up. The garden is 16 and up, or 14 and up with a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Click Find an Opportunity on the volunteer page and pick a shift on the volunteer sign-up site. Groups use the group button on the same page.
notes: Sort and pack is in Grove City (3960 Brookham Drive). Other sites have no address on the page. Call 614-277-3663 with questions.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. A parent or guardian must take part in the TB test step.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online part of the Teen Program form. Mail or hand in the paper part to Volunteer Services. Then you interview and take a TB test. You go to a volunteer orientation and a unit orientation.
notes: Sites listed: Mount Carmel Dublin, East, Grove City, St. Ann's and New Albany. Phones: East 614-234-6658, Grove City 614-663-6700, St. Ann's 380-898-4097, New Albany 614-663-6334. Completing the application does not guarantee a spot.
duration: One shift (about 4 hours) a week. Summer: weekdays 8 am to 4 pm. School year: weekday evenings 4 to 7 pm or weekends 8 am to 8 pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: "Arts-interested youth." The page gives no age or grade rule. Selected teens join a cohort.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. Call the museum at 614-221-6801 or watch the page for the next call.
notes: Meetings are at CMA Short North, CMA at The Pizzuti and the Broad Street location (480 East Broad Street). Ages are not stated, so confirm with the museum before you plan on it.
duration: Select Saturdays, Sept 26, 2026 to May 30, 2027
pay_detail: $1,250 stipend, paid in two installments

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19. Free registration; drop-ins are welcome.
how_to_apply: Register for free on the museum events listings, or drop in.
notes: Teens 13 and older can also visit the museum on their own at any time, per the page.
duration: Every second Thursday, 5 to 7 pm. Teen Studio: Unwind is quarterly, 5 to 7 pm.
pay_detail: Free; includes museum admission

who_can_apply: Teens who are 15 by June 1 and currently in high school. Competitive, with limited spots.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Get references who are not family to fill out an electronic form. Go to a group interview. Sign a commitment form. Send your shot record, including flu. No waivers are allowed. Then finish an online orientation and training for your job.
notes: You can miss no more than 2 shifts. You need to be there 80 percent of the time. Contact Family and Volunteer Services at 614-722-3635 or Volunteering@NationwideChildrens.org. The page has no direct application link.
duration: 10 weeks, June to mid-August, one 2 to 3 hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Ohio residents in their freshman, sophomore or junior year of high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online STEM Institute application when it opens. Email si-contact@osc.edu.
notes: Two phone numbers appear on OSC pages, so email is the safer contact. The page does not mention financial aid. It was formerly called the Summer Institute.
duration: 2 weeks, June 6 to 17, 2027
pay_detail: $600 per student ($60 per day) for housing, meals, tuition, trips and insurance. OSC says the real cost is about four times that.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 in fall 2027 can take high school courses.
how_to_apply: Make a free account in the online application system. Then apply. Sign up for updates on the page to learn when applications open.
notes: Questions: ExploreASC@osu.edu or 614-292-6390. The page says some need-based aid may be available. Ask for it on the program application. Other department camps are on the department summer page. They cover philosophy, language science, humanities and mind science.
duration: 1 week per course
pay_detail: The 2026 fee was $550 per one-week course, with lunch and snacks. The 2027 fee is not posted.

who_can_apply: All high school students interested in a career in healthcare. The page gives no grade, age or residency rule. A parent or guardian must attend the required orientation.
how_to_apply: Online application (Apply Now form on the camp page). Use the Contact Us link on the camp page for questions.
notes: Free and short, so a good first health-career step. Watch the page for 2027 dates.
duration: 3 days, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
pay_detail: Free for students. Breakfast and lunch are provided.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10, 11 or 12. A student who just finished freshman year can also apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send a high school transcript, a personal statement and a note from a teacher.
notes: The page has a few date mix-ups (one spot says 2025), so confirm the 2027 dates and cost with ccbs@osu.edu.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page. It says financial aid, including partial and full scholarships, is available.

who_can_apply: Ohio residents who will be high school sophomores, juniors or seniors and want a health career. The page suggests a 3.0 GPA overall and 3.3 in math and science. You also need two letters of support. One must be from a math or science teacher.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks about school and other activities, essays and a transcript. You also need two signed letters of support. They are sent through a separate form.
notes: You must find your own housing and rides. The page only covers 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Tuition is $325. Full and partial scholarships are given based on need and application quality.

who_can_apply: Ohio residents in 8th grade at Columbus City Schools, Cincinnati Public Schools or seven other listed city districts. You must be the first in your family to go to college. Family income must be under the limit. You must earn mostly A grades.
how_to_apply: Apply in 8th grade through the Young Scholars Program page. Questions: YSP@osu.edu.
notes: Only 8th graders can start. The page says there are no costs for the pre-college portion.Other districts on the list: Akron, Canton, Cleveland, Dayton, Lorain, Toledo and Youngstown. Check the page for the income table and the current deadline.
duration: Grades 8 through 12
pay_detail: No cost stated for the program. Ohio State financial aid is offered after graduation if requirements are met.

who_can_apply: Student volunteers must be at least 12 years old or in grades 7 to 12. You must have a Pickerington Public Library card and go to an orientation. You must keep a steady schedule of 2 to 6 hours a week for about 3 months or longer.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply to Volunteer link on the volunteer page. Then go to an orientation. The Volunteer Coordinator runs it.
notes: Two locations: Pickerington Main Library and Sycamore Plaza Library. Homework Help is open Monday to Thursday, 3 to 6 pm, in the school year. The VolunTeen Scholarship form is open December 1 to January 30.
duration: On-going, 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. A VolunTeen Scholarship is open to high school students with outstanding volunteer service.

who_can_apply: Columbus residents (or people who pay Columbus taxes) ages 14 to 23. Must pass a drug test; a background check applies at 18 and older. Required documents: birth certificate and/or Social Security card, plus a state or school photo ID.
how_to_apply: Apply during the winter window listed on the program page. If you have questions, email AJRP@columbus.gov or call 614-724-2038.
notes: Work experiences vary and are matched to career interests where possible. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. The page does not say how to submit the application beyond the schedule, so confirm the method with the program.
duration: Mostly summer; some participants may continue in fall and winter
pay_detail: $15 an hour, up to 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: City of Columbus residents (getting City trash and recycling service counts) entering grades 6 to 10 in Fall 2026 who keep a 2.8 GPA. Selected applicants interview with the program directors.
how_to_apply: Email the application, last school year's report card and a letter from a teacher, administrator or community leader to CBMcGhee@columbus.gov, or drop it at Blackburn Community Center (263 Carpenter St.). Selected applicants interview.
notes: Includes middle schoolers (grades 6 to 10). There is a mandatory guardian and youth orientation on Sept 19, 2026. You can miss no more than three meet-ups without an excuse. The page says applications began May 1, 2025. That looks like a typo for 2026.
duration: Sept orientation, then 12 monthly meet-ups Oct 2026 to May 2027; ceremony May 15, 2027
pay_detail: No pay; cost not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older with the swimming skills needed. Must finish the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course (the City waives the course fee if you are hired). Completing the course does not guarantee a job.
how_to_apply: Submit the Lifeguard Interest Form, take the pre-course swimming skills test, finish the Red Cross course, then submit the employment application.
notes: The City also offers Red Cross lifeguard training for ages 15 and older. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) says school-age minors need an age and schooling certificate (work permit). In the summer, 16 and 17 year olds can show the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead.
duration: Summer season; dates not stated
pay_detail: $20 an hour (seasonal)

who_can_apply: Pre-college students who are passionate about mathematics. First-year students range in age from 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Ross Program website when the window opens. Email ross@rossprogram.org with questions.
notes: The page lists two sites. One is Otterbein University in Columbus, OH. The other is Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology in Terre Haute, Indiana. The 2026 dates were June 14 to July 24. Ask about 2027 dates when they are posted.
duration: 6 weeks (summer 2026: June 14 to July 24)
pay_detail: $7,500, covering tuition, housing and meals. Financial aid is offered for students who need it.

who_can_apply: 9th and 10th graders. The county page says IT On Ramp+ is for TANF-eligible Franklin County 9th and 10th graders.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the TECH CORPS Work-Based Learning page. Phone 614-583-9211, email info@techcorps.org.
notes: The county page lists a 6-week length and $15 per hour for IT On Ramp+; the TECH CORPS page lists 4 weeks. Ask TECH CORPS which is right for the next session. Ages are not stated, only grades 9 and 10. The TECH CORPS page gives no pay.
duration: IT On Ramp+ is 4 weeks, full day. Computing Career Corps meets weekdays 9 am to 3 pm.
pay_detail: $15 per hour for IT On Ramp+ (6 weeks), per the Franklin County page. Pay for Computing Career Corps is not stated, but students earn Work Based Learning hours.

who_can_apply: High school and college students. The page does not state a minimum age or grade.
how_to_apply: Email Meg Brown. She is the Director of Children's Education. Her address is megbrown@thurberhouse.org.
notes: The page says counselors must be 21 or older and gives no minimum age for interns. Confirm the age limit by email.
duration: Monday to Friday, at least 1 week (camp runs 8 weeks)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Thurber House can sign off on service hours. Interns provide their own transportation and lunch.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th grade through rising college freshmen.
how_to_apply: Register online. For a scholarship, click "applying for a scholarship" in the online registration. Questions go to Meg Brown (megbrown@thurberhouse.org).
notes: Bring a sack lunch.
duration: 2 weeks, Monday to Friday (July 20 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: $825 (includes all fees, snacks, a journal and a t-shirt). Payment plans on request. A very limited number of scholarships are given by lottery (you pay a $25 registration fee to enter).

who_can_apply: Any student in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Young Writers' Studio page. For help paying, email Meg Brown (megbrown@thurberhouse.org).
notes: Fall 2026 dates are listed. The page does not list later sessions.
duration: 6 evening sessions, 6:30 to 8:30 p.m.
pay_detail: $17 per session, with a discount for the whole season. A limited number of scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Tremont Road Branch or Lane Road Branch link on the volunteer page. Contact the teen volunteer staff listed for each branch with questions.
notes: Branches are Lane Road, Miller Park and Tremont Road. The page lists two different branch application links, so use the one for your branch.
duration: Shifts for the whole 2026-2027 school year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service hours, and teen volunteers enter a quarterly prize raffle.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 19, per the age range listed for WRTU on the Urban League Career Connect page. Other eligibility rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The Youth Leadership Team is at 3443 Agler Rd., Columbus, phone 614-257-6300.
notes: Supported by the Franklin County Board of Commissioners and employer partners. A 2024 WRTU Fellows program began with 27 youth. The Urban League's other youth programs (for example I Am My Brother's Keeper, ages 14 to 18, and VLOG, ages 14 to 19) are listed on its Career Connect page. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Summer; length not stated
pay_detail: Paid for summer involvement; rate not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 18. Lead Volunteers are ages 16 to 18. Requirements vary and spaces are limited.
how_to_apply: Read the teen volunteer rules page. Fill out an application, even if you have volunteered before. Go to an orientation before your first shift. Use the phone number in the notes for questions.
notes: Phone 614-882-7277, option 5. No direct application link was on the page. Lead volunteers need at least 4 to 6 hours a month and summer volunteers at least 2 hours a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 12 or entering grades 7 to 12 in the fall.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Volunteens application. The library will contact you if you are approved.
notes: The page lists no orientation or hours requirement. Email the library with questions.
duration: School year (September to June) and summer (June to August)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work

who_can_apply: Anyone in grade 6 and above. You do not need to be a YMCA member.
how_to_apply: Click Start Your Application on the Hilliard Teen Leaders Club page. You can also email Taylor Stillion. His email is taylor.stillion@ymcacolumbus.org.
notes: This card is for the Hilliard branch. Other YMCA of Central Ohio branches may have their own clubs; ask the Y.
duration: Weekly meetings, Wednesdays 6 to 7 pm
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors or seniors who like marine science. You must go to an info session and fill out a form.
how_to_apply: Go to an info session. Fill out the interest form. Then fill out the Apply for the Program form linked on the page.
notes: The page does not say what travel papers are needed, so ask the Zoo. The trip is 3 days on land and 3 on the water, weather permitting. Field station is on Andros Island, Bahamas.
duration: 8 days (June 19 to 26, 2027)
pay_detail: $3,500 per person. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school teams of 4 to 7 students with one faculty advisor from the school. Only 2 teams per school are accepted.
how_to_apply: Your team captain fills out the online team application on the Teen Eco Summit page. A school faculty advisor must be on the team.
notes: You need a school faculty advisor on the team, so ask one first. Only 2 teams per school are accepted. Each team needs its own project and application.
duration: Kickoff Oct. 28 or 29, 2026 (9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.), projects through the year, celebration at the end of April
pay_detail: Free to take part

who_can_apply: Teens entering grades 8 to 12 who show leadership, animal knowledge, professionalism and emotional maturity.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the Teen Volunteers page in early 2027.
notes: The page does not state the months, hours or any fee, so confirm with the Zoo. Season is listed as summer as a best fit but is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Cook County residents ages 14 to 19.
how_to_apply: The Cook County page points to fpdcc.com/nature/conservation-corps-programs for how to apply. That page was not available.
notes: Confirm age rules, pay and deadline on the Forest Preserves site, because it blocked my reader. Ask about working papers if you are under 16.
duration: 4 to 6 weeks
pay_detail: Paid. The amount is not stated on the Cook County page. Transportation and service clothing are provided.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in suburban Cook County who are not working or in school. It aims at the south and west suburbs but is open to all of suburban Cook County.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Chicago Cook Workforce Partnership Opportunity Works page. The Cook County page links to it. That page was not available.
notes: The page does not say how to enroll or the pay, so call or check chicookworks.org. For teens 16 to 18 who have left school.
pay_detail: Subsidized internships. Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in the grades listed for each role.
how_to_apply: Click Apply for the role you want on the volunteer page. Questions about youth roles: Kevin, kwonch@cooklib.org. Questions about high school roles: Leah, lhotchkiss@cooklib.org.
notes: You need a library card for the adult volunteer jobs.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer work counts toward service hours.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 and up. Accepted volunteers must attend three weekend training sessions.
how_to_apply: Online youth volunteer application during the August window, then an in-person interview (5:30 to 7:30 p.m.) at COSI.
notes: Candidates who cannot attend all three trainings are told to reapply later. COSI also lists one-day Quick Impact volunteer shifts; check each listing for its age rule.
duration: Three weekend trainings (Oct to Dec in 2026), then ongoing volunteering; hours not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Chicago residents attending a Chicago high school or equivalent (graduating seniors can apply), ages 16 to 19 on the first day (June 22 in 2026), with a Social Security number or ITIN.
how_to_apply: Log in to Chicago Youth Works, finish that application, choose After School Matters under Opportunities, then search library positions (program name CPL or your branch) in the ASM application. Branch staff interview in May.
notes: Positions were offered at every Chicago Public Library location. You can apply to many branches but be hired for one. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age here is 16. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org.
duration: 6 weeks (June 22 to Aug 1 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026: $17.05 per hour, 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Ages 14 to 19 on the start date of Jan 9, 2027. Teen Best Reads and Teen Media Lab are open to current 9th, 10th and 11th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Chicago Public Library application form (not the After School Matters site). Answer the open-ended questions carefully; they decide who is interviewed. Virtual interview in Microsoft Teams for each program. Apply to as many as you like but accept one.
notes: You enroll with After School Matters during the first month, which needs a Social Security Number and parent or guardian information. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org. Gamer's Guild sub-guilds meet at different library branches.
duration: Starts Jan 9, 2027. Gamer's Guild to June 10; Media Lab Jan to June 22 and Sept 7 to Dec 14; Best Reads to Dec 14.
pay_detail: These are stipend assistantships. The amounts are not stated on the program page, so ask the library.

who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students. 8th graders apply through GoCPS when they apply to high school; freshmen and 10th graders ask their school counselor.
how_to_apply: Rank CTE programs on your GoCPS high school application (8th grade), or talk to your counselor (9th and 10th grade). Email CTE@cps.edu for questions.
notes: Which pathways are offered differs by school; the CTE Matrix and Guide to CTE Programs on the page list them. CPS Work-Based Learning (internships, co-op) builds on these pathways. Contact: 773-553-2108.
duration: Multi-year pathway
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Current 10th and 11th graders at a district-run CPS school; priority goes to 10th graders. Must attend an information session and submit a recommendation from a trusted adult who is not a family member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google application form, a signed Student and Parent Expectations and Consent Contract and a Recommendation Form, then email everything to ChicagoBuilds@cps.edu.
notes: It is an Illinois Works Pre-Apprenticeship site and offers the Master Builder program with City Colleges of Chicago. Classes meet during the school day in an AM or PM cohort. Contact: 773-534-0909.
duration: Two school years, 2 hours a day at Dunbar High School campus (3000 S. King Drive)
pay_detail: Earn 2.5 high school credits per year of the program. Pay for senior-year internships is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school seniors at least 16 years old with a 2.0 GPA, excellent attendance and a counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply in 11th grade through your school; contact the citywide Cooperative Education coordinator (773-553-2108) for the process.
notes: Placement and training partners listed on the page include Genesys Works and Urban Alliance. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age is 16. Cutting school or work can cost credit.
duration: One school year, at least 180 hours a semester (about 10 hours a week); 3 elective credits
pay_detail: Students earn wages; the rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled at a Chicago Public Schools high school, including home-schooled students per City Colleges. A 2.5 GPA and strong attendance are typical requirements. If your GPA is lower, the page says recommendation letters are accepted. Under 16 needs a principal recommendation and approval from the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, get approval from the dual enrollment coordinator at your City Colleges campus, complete the City Colleges application and pick classes. Do not pay for or enroll in a class before talking to the Early College team.
notes: Undocumented students are eligible (CPS page). Some courses need ACT, SAT or City Colleges placement scores; many courses have no prerequisites. Jumpstart Pathways and Runway 606 are related CPS options. Seven campuses; each has a dual enrollment coordinator.
duration: Per semester; dual enrollment is one course per semester at a City Colleges campus
pay_detail: Free college credit. The page says you earn college credit for free.

who_can_apply: Sophomores who live in the city of Chicago. A 2.3 GPA and 90% attendance are recommended. Needs 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and a background check.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Sophomores apply online each year beginning in February. Provide 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and pass a background check. Questions: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.
notes: Takes up to 125 students each year. Contact: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.
duration: Two years; Tuesday and Wednesday 4:30 to 7:30 p.m., September to May
pay_detail: Free: uniforms, materials, snacks and transportation help provided; scholarships possible. A paid summer internship between junior and senior year is possible (pay not stated).

who_can_apply: Camp volunteers and general program volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Other roles do not list an age on the page. Everyone fills out a volunteer waiver. The page says teens to seniors can volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lyman Woods application for the role you want. Also fill out the volunteer waiver. Program and camp volunteers send in an application and go to an interview and training. A criminal background check is only for program volunteers 18 or older.
notes: REAP restoration workdays need an RSVP. The park district also runs Counselor in Training (C.I.T.) camps for teens. The teen camps page lists no CIT sign-up fee; it lists only a $5 or $10 per-camp withdrawal service fee. Ages for most teen camps are not listed.
duration: Camp volunteers help during the summer. Other roles are ongoing.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Teen and adult volunteers: age 14 or entering high school. Junior volunteers: junior high school students.
how_to_apply: Junior volunteers fill out the online application, permission form and photo release. Teen and adult volunteers check openings on the museum volunteer page. You can also call or email Jessica Greenlaw.
notes: Experience with kids is helpful but not required. Summer teen volunteering is not mentioned on the page, so ask. The minimum age for the junior program is not given, only junior high.
duration: Teen shifts start at 2 hours. Junior: one weekend day (Friday to Sunday) each week for 3 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: One-time community events: ages 8 and up with an adult. Long-term roles are generally 18 and up, with limited openings for ages 13 to 17. Family roles are ages 10 and up with an adult.
how_to_apply: For long-term roles, apply online through the volunteer portal. Then meet with program staff for an interview. After that, go to orientation and training. For one-time restoration workdays, find a date on the events calendar and register.
notes: Getting started for a long-term role takes about 2 to 3 months. The FAQ page says background checks apply to people 16 and older in one place and 18 and older in another. Ask the Volunteer Services office what applies to you. Call 630-933-7233 or write to volunteer@dupageforest.org. The page does not list which long-term roles take people under 18.
duration: One-time workdays or long-term roles with a yearly minimum of hours
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Students at participating schools: U-46 (Bartlett, Elgin, Larkin, South Elgin, Streamwood), District 300 (Dundee-Crown, Hampshire, Jacobs), District 301 (Burlington Central), District 303 (St. Charles East, St. Charles North, Compass Academy), Cambridge Lakes Charter and St. Edward Central Catholic. The tracks are for juniors, seniors, or juniors and seniors, depending on the track. Talk with your counselor.
how_to_apply: Talk with your parents and your high school counselor first, then use the online Dual Credit application (Apply Now). Independent enrollment also needs approval from the ECC Dual Credit office. Contact: DualCredit@elgin.edu or 847-214-7887.
notes: Accelerate College students may need to qualify for college-level courses and testing may be required. Each district publishes a Dual Credit Guide listing what its schools support. The ECC page also lists Upward Bound, Educational Talent Search and College and Career Readiness workshops.
duration: Per semester
pay_detail: Accelerate College: no tuition for district-approved courses. Independent enrollment and Dual Enrollment: students are usually billed tuition. Career tech courses the district does not approve require tuition.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 at certain schools. The middle schools are Abbott, Ellis, Kimball, Larsen, Carpentersville, Canton and Tefft. The high schools are Elgin, Larkin, Streamwood and Dundee-Crown. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident. You must show money need or be a possible first-generation college student.
how_to_apply: Send in the Talent Search application with your papers. You can do this online, by email to talentsearchtransition@elgin.edu, by mail or by fax. You can also get a paper copy from your school counselor. A guardian helps if you are under 18.
notes: Contact: 847-214-7764, Building K Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin. Only the schools named above are served. The page does not state a cost or federal funding; the pay_detail wording is not confirmed by the page.
duration: Ongoing through high school
pay_detail: A federally funded TRIO program. The page does not state a cost, pay or stipend.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Dundee-Crown, Larkin or Streamwood High School who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and are either potential first-generation college students or from a low-income household (U.S. Department of Education rules). If unsure, apply and staff will tell you if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Student and parent or guardian complete the online Upward Bound application. Counselors and teachers can fill out the Student Recommendation Form. Contact: upwardbound@elgin.edu, 847-214-7253, Building K, Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin.
notes: Only for students at the three listed high schools. The page does not mention a summer part or a start date, so ask staff. A web search snippet suggested Elgin High School is also served, but the ECC page itself lists only the three above.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth interested in the fire service. The page does not list an age range or other rules. Ask the coordinator.
how_to_apply: Go to any meeting on the schedule. Or ask the coordinator for an application. You can write to efdexplorers439@cityofelgin.org. You can also call 847-931-6175.
notes: The page lists no age range and no fees. Equipment provided: uniform, bunker gear, SCBA, mask, gloves, boots and hood. Meetings are on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday at 6:00 p.m. The page now lives at elginil.gov (the old cityofelgin.org address redirects). The page does not say members become CPR certified; it lists CPR and first aid as topics. Call before you go to confirm age rules.
duration: Meetings twice a month, 1st and 3rd Wednesday at 6:00 p.m.
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. Uniform and gear are provided, and members become CPR and first aid certified.

who_can_apply: Individuals, families and groups, including school and youth groups. No minimum age is listed. Volunteers 18 and younger need a parent or guardian to sign the waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer preferences form and sign the waiver (a parent signs if you are 18 or younger). Questions: david.schoenknecht@elginil.gov or 847-531-7055.
notes: Wear long pants and closed toe shoes. Because no minimum age is listed, call to ask if there is one for your role.
duration: Ongoing, flexible
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Tools are provided.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 up to under 21. You live in Elgin or a nearby town and go to a local school. You have a C average or better. You have no past arrests or felony convictions. Special cases are reviewed one at a time. Boys and girls are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the application packet. It has the application, terms and a liability waiver. Then pass a background check and an oral interview.
notes: The program is linked to Boy Scouts of America. Boys and girls are welcome. The page says it serves youth in Elgin and nearby towns.
duration: Weekly meetings on Wednesdays at 6:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. Explorers are expected to give 96 volunteer hours a year.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Watch the event calendar and social media for each month's plan, then show up.
notes: Short page. It does not say how to sign up, where events happen or if there is a cost.
duration: One event each month
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 6 and up can ask to volunteer or do community service hours. The Junior Teen Advisory Group is for grades 6 to 8.
how_to_apply: Contact Adelaide Rowe, arowe@egvpl.org, (847) 439-0447 ext. 252 about volunteering. For Jr. TAG, use the Apply Online link on the page or contact Tammy Wulf, twulf@egvpl.org, ext. 248.
notes: The page does not describe a program for older teens. It only lists volunteering and the Reading Program.
duration: Jr. TAG meets monthly, year round, with snacks
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students. Endeavor Health says most roles are for age 16 and up, but age 14 and up at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals. Health screening and orientation are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Student application. The hospital will contact the people it picks about next steps. If you have questions, call Volunteer Services at 630-527-3034.
notes: Hours per week and the length of service are not on the pages. Ask Volunteer Services. Background checks are only for ages 18 and up. Age 14 applies at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals; most roles are for 16 and up.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school students. Endeavor Health says most roles are for age 16 and up, but age 14 and up at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals. Health screening and orientation are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. If the site has problems, call 331-221-3282.
notes: The Elmhurst application page had no hours or length details, so ask the volunteer office. Background checks are only for ages 18 and up. Age 14 applies at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals; most roles are for 16 and up.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.
duration: Minimum 4 hours a week and 100 hours for the year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens offer their service without pay.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.
duration: Minimum 4 hours a week and 100 hours for the year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens offer their service without pay.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.
duration: Minimum 4 hours a week and 100 hours for the year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens offer their service without pay.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online High School Volunteer application. Plan on one 30 minute sitting. Then you do an interest interview and a volunteer orientation. You may need a background check. You must also meet the health rules.
notes: The form cannot be saved and finished later.
duration: At least 6 months, 3 to 4 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers offer their service without pay.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.
duration: Minimum 4 hours a week and 100 hours for the year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens offer their service without pay.

who_can_apply: Evanston or Chicago-area high school students who love art. You can come to meetings on Wednesdays from 5:00 to 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Apply. Then do a short interview, take a tour of the art center and meet current members. To ask about the current application, contact Catie Bryant at cbryant@evanstonartcenter.org.
notes: The page has no closing date, and its board photo is captioned 2023-24. Email before you plan around it.
duration: School year. About 8 to 12 meetings per semester.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members volunteer at least 25 hours a year and earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Mainly under-resourced high school students and community members. The city workforce page says ages 17 and older. The ASPIRE page does not list exact rules, so email to ask.
how_to_apply: Write to aspire@cityofevanston.org and ask how to join. The workforce page also has a Workforce Division Engagement Form.
notes: The city workforce page says ASPIRE works with NorthShore HealthSystem. It serves ages 17 and older. Email aspire@cityofevanston.org to ask about high school students. Also ask your school counselor.
duration: Summer internship. Length not stated.
pay_detail: Summer internships are described as paid. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students at Evanston Township High School. The page is written for ETHS students.
how_to_apply: Talk to the Early College and Career Experiences office in Room W220. Contact Abronia Young. Call 847-424-7735 or write to younga@eths202.org. You can also call the post-secondary counselor, Michelle Vazquez, at 847-424-7163.
notes: ETHS also has a Work Permits page. It says Illinois law requires minors under 16 to get a work permit before working. Permits are by appointment only, and students aged 14 to 15 in school-approved work-based learning programs do not need one.
duration: A few weeks to a semester or a year
pay_detail: Internships may be paid or unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who live inside Evanston Township High School District 202.
how_to_apply: Register online ahead of time for the winter job fair, then meet employers there. Employers use a separate job request form.
notes: Illinois law says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate), per the Evanston Township High School work permit page. The page says the program began in 1992 and last year over 40 employers offered over 300 jobs. Pay and exact summer dates are not on the page. The registration link is the 2026 form; look for a 2027 form around winter.
duration: Up to 9 weeks
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rate is not stated on the page. Confirm with the city.

who_can_apply: Illinois high school students who will be seniors in 2027-28 or who graduate in 2027. Must be a U.S. citizen and have proof of medical insurance. No STEM prerequisites. Age and GPA are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal, a supplemental questionnaire, a PDF list of your STEM courses uploaded in the Resume section, and one letter from a STEM teacher or STEM club advisor. You cannot upload missing items after you submit.
notes: The apply link only works during the application window. Recommenders get an email upload link. It is sent only on weekdays during business hours, so line up your letter writer early. A walkthrough video is on the page.
duration: 4 weeks, July 12 to Aug 6, 2027
pay_detail: $500 per week stipend. Housing is not provided; transportation assistance is available.

who_can_apply: High school students in public, private or parochial schools, and home-schooled students with high school standing. Students attend in person. A physics course and two years of algebra help but are not required. A unique email address is required.
how_to_apply: Watch for the news in November. Then fill out the online application. If you have questions, write to saturdaymorningphysics@fnal.gov.
notes: Lectures are at Wilson Hall in Batavia. Some lectures may be off-site. Spring 2027 dates are not posted yet.
duration: 11 Saturdays, 9 a.m. to noon. Fall 2026 ran Sept 12 to Nov 21.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Open to all high school students across Illinois. No science prerequisite. You must attend at least 8 sessions, with no excused absences.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the application. It opens in late fall 2026. If you have questions, write to Saturdaymorningquantum@fnal.gov.
notes: Classes are held at the Olive Harvey Learning Center, 3055 East 92nd Street, Chicago. The page gives no exact open or close date for applications.
duration: Saturdays 1 to 4 p.m., February 6 to April 24, 2027 (no sessions March 20 and 27)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Enrolled in an Illinois high school JROTC program, and an Illinois high school junior, senior or recent graduate when you apply. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal with an unofficial transcript, a resume and three short essay answers (under 200 words each). Then give contact info for one recommendation writer; the letter is due by the close date. Questions: Internships@fnal.gov.
notes: Only for cadets in an Illinois JROTC program. You cannot upload missing items after you submit, so gather everything first. Reference emails go out only on weekdays during business hours.
duration: 6 weeks, June 28 to Aug 6, 2027
pay_detail: $18 per hour. No onsite housing or transportation reimbursement.

who_can_apply: The employment page says positions run from teens seeking a first job to skilled professionals. Minimum age is not stated on the page, so check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the job you want from the Join Our Team page. Applications are kept on file for one year. A background check is required if you get an offer.
notes: The district says it has about 1,200 part-time and seasonal workers at times of the year. Job fair dates are from old press releases, so confirm the next one. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.
duration: Seasonal and part-time
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay is listed on each posting. It is not on the main employment page.

who_can_apply: Students and school groups. The page does not list a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Use the link on the volunteer page to reserve a spot for an event. To adopt a park or trail, email Ivan Chambers at ichambers@fvpd.net.
notes: The district provides trash bags, gloves and a few litter grabbers for Adopt-A-Park groups. Ask the district if a parent form is needed for under 18.
duration: One-day projects or monthly clean-ups (Adopt-A-Park runs April to September, or May to October)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Eligible local teens. The page does not state the age range or other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Teen Corps page when it reopens. Contact the Teen Corps Coordinator through the page.
notes: Run on a community garden and the Conservatory's Farmers Market. Ages, stipend amount and dates are not on the page, so ask the coordinator. Ohio needs a working permit for paid work at ages 14 to 17, but 16 and 17 year olds do not need one for nonagricultural, nonhazardous work during summer vacation. See permit.html?state=oh for the steps.
duration: Summer program; length not stated
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old and complete an application, a background check and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application, then complete the background check and orientation.
notes: Some outdoor roles run March to November and the Children's Garden runs April to October.
duration: No minimum hours; weekly, monthly or seasonal
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. Bring an ID (school ID, driver's license or library card).
how_to_apply: 1) Fill out the online teen volunteer application. 2) Register for a one-time Teen Volunteer Orientation. 3) Sign up for open sessions on the teen volunteer calendar. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead.
notes: Grade 6 is under 13, so younger readers should ask about their grade. The library's Elgin Teens page also describes Studio 270, a high school teen space at 270 N. Grove Ave. (homework help, college readiness, job hunting help; phone 847-695-7577), but parts of that page look out of date, so call first. The volunteer page lists a contact email that is hidden in the page text; use the library's Contact Us page.
duration: Short sessions, about 1 hour each; you pick the ones you want
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Geneva Public Library patrons in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register as a Volunteen using the sign-up form on the page. Contact: geneva.library@gpld.org or (630) 232-0780, 227 S. Seventh St., Geneva.
notes: Service hours are flexible and are not listed as a set number. The page does not describe the registration steps beyond the sign-up form.
duration: Fall 2026 session: Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in grades 6 to 12. They live in Glenview or go to a school the library serves. Teen Advisory Board applicants must be in grades 7 to 11 and follow the same rule. Innovation Center volunteers must be in high school at a school the library serves.
how_to_apply: Fill out the youth volunteer application when it opens. The Teen Advisory Board form comes out in November. For the Innovation Center, write to innovationdesk@glenviewpl.org. For other questions, write to youthdesk@glenviewpl.org or call 847-729-7500.
notes: Returning volunteers do not need to apply again. Court ordered community service for teens must be 16 and older. It uses a separate form.
duration: Teen Advisory Board: monthly meetings and 3 to 5 programs in a one year term
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. The page says interns are ages 16 to 18 in one place and 16 to 19 in another.
how_to_apply: Watch Hennepin County job listings (sign up for email notifications from the page). Libraries hiring interns: Brookdale, Brooklyn Park, Franklin, Hosmer, North Regional, Roosevelt, and Cedar Riverside Opportunity Center.
notes: Training includes hands-on learning, group reflection and an adult mentor. Hiring dates and pay are not on the page. Confirm with the library before relying on it.
duration: Year-round (summer and school year), about 6 hours a week after school and weekends
pay_detail: Described as a hired position; the pay rate is not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Only a limited number of teen volunteer spots exist at some libraries.
how_to_apply: Ask your local Hennepin County library about teen openings. If there is one, fill out the teen volunteer application (PDF). Bring it to the library. A staff member will contact you. Questions: Volunteer Services, 612-543-8633.
notes: Adult volunteers have a different process. The phone line is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Enrolled 4-H members ages 14 to 18 as of September 1 of the 4-H year, with strong visual or performing arts skills.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page. Contact Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Must attend at least 75 percent of the monthly Zoom calls.
duration: One-year term; Zoom meetings the last Tuesday of each month
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 13 or older, enrolled in or past their first year of high school, with some community service. Needs a reference from an Extension staff member, school staff member or youth worker.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Illinois 4-H Ambassador Application (the Apply for the Illinois 4-H Food Advocacy Team button, which opens form.jotform.com) and get a reference. Questions: Mark Becker, mbbecker@illinois.edu.
notes: Cost to attend in-person meetings is not stated.
duration: One Zoom meeting a month (Sunday, 7 pm) and 1 to 2 in-person meetings a year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 when applying. Must be committed to 4-H values and passionate about healthy living.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page. Contact Illinois 4-H at Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Members must attend at least one day of the Illinois State Fair. Whether you must be a 4-H member is not stated.
duration: Virtual meeting once a month for 1 to 2 hours, plus a 1 to 2 day retreat each year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 as of September 1 of the application year.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page (an application tip sheet is linked). Contact Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Whether you must be a 4-H member is not stated on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings (recording available)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: 4-H members who are at least 14 years old.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the page for the next training.
notes: Teens must attend one training to be on the state roster and join a spring update call to stay on it.
duration: 6-hour training, offered about three times a year; a spring update call each year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 join a 4-H Club. Your age on September 1, the start of the 4-H year, decides how you join. Teen teams: Creative Collective Art Ambassadors is ages 14 to 18, and Illinois 4-H Influencers is for high school age youth. Other teams do not list ages on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the Join 4-H page with a parent or guardian. Your local Extension office then contacts you with next steps to register. Returning members renew in Zsuite.
notes: This is club membership and volunteer leadership, not a paid job. Cost, grades and teen team application steps are not stated on the pages. Call Illinois 4-H at (217) 333-0910 or email Illinois4H@illinois.edu.
duration: 4-H year starts September 1. Teen team terms are about one year (stated for the Art Ambassadors).
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the page. Ask your local Extension office.

who_can_apply: Boys who have completed one semester of 11th grade and have at least one semester left after Boys State. Those who finished junior year get preference. A boy may attend only once as a citizen. Many are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form; your local American Legion post will then contact you. Parents can also register eligible sons. Questions: info@illinoisboysstate.org or 309-663-0361.
notes: Boys only. Delegates must stay all week and may not drive or leave campus. The Samsung Scholarship application must be finished before arriving.
duration: Session starts June 12, 2027, at 4:00 PM (90th annual session). The registration page lists no end date.
pay_detail: $400 registration fee covering program, up to 10 scholarship contests, housing and meals. Most delegates are sponsored by a local American Legion post.

who_can_apply: Youth who meet one of these: DCFS has legal guardianship, you aged out of care at 18 or older, or you were adopted or placed with a guardian from care at 16 or older. Use it at any U.S. accredited school, in state or out of state.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Illinois Education and Training Voucher Funds on the Kaleidoscope site. File a FAFSA each year. Finish any forms your school asks for. Questions: DCFS.ETVCoordinator@illinois.gov.
notes: This is for college or training after high school, so it matters most for teens 16 to 18 who are planning ahead. It is money for school, not a job. Ask your caseworker.
pay_detail: Up to $5,000 a year for school costs. Good for five years (in a row or not) or until age 26, whichever comes first, with satisfactory academic progress.

who_can_apply: Youth in DCFS care ages 17 to 20 who work 20 hours a week or 80 hours a month. Youth in job training or an approved apprenticeship can also apply. Older former foster youth have a separate apprenticeship rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out form CFS 449-2. Then email it to the DCFS Office of Education and Transition Services, or fax it to 217-524-2101. Ask your caseworker for help.
notes: Only for youth in DCFS care (or certain former foster youth). Call 312-814-6800 or 217-785-2509 for help. DCFS Advocacy Office: 800-232-3798.
pay_detail: The page says it gives financial services but does not list the amount.

who_can_apply: Members must have an interest in marketing, management, entrepreneurship, hospitality and tourism or finance. A chapter needs a certified local educator as advisor. Grades and ages are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA chapter and advisor. If your school has none, the Illinois DECA site has a Start a Chapter page. Membership runs through the DECA membership portal linked on ildeca.org.
notes: Not a paid job. Dues and conference dates come from the DECA Inc. page for Illinois. The state site ildeca.org did not repeat them. Mailing address on the state site: 2460 Dundee Road, Box 1001, Northbrook, IL 60065.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $17 per member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local fees (not stated).

who_can_apply: Students at a school with an FBLA chapter. The page lists high school, middle level and college chapters. How to join is not explained on the program pages.
how_to_apply: Ask a business teacher about a chapter at your school. The chapters page lists active chapters by region. Use the Contact page on ilfbla.org to ask how to join or start a chapter.
notes: Dues and how to start a chapter are not on the program pages. The national FBLA site blocked automated reading, so national rules were not checked.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school girls who are current juniors. A principal, guidance counselor or home school administrator must certify leadership qualities, good character and U.S. residency. You must secure sponsorship from an American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form (name, school email, counselor name and email, school, hometown), get approval from your school official, find a sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation. Call 309-663-9366 or email info@alaigs.org.
notes: Girls only. The program is physically active with long walks; the registration page asks you to check with a doctor if you have limits. After the program you share your experience with your sponsoring Unit.
duration: One week, June 20 to 26, 2027
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages checked for this card. Ask the Illinois Girls State office and your local American Legion Auxiliary unit.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are Illinois residents. You need earlier research experience (a research program, course or science fair). If you do not have it, you must finish an online Research Fundamentals course first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the IMSA page when the portal opens. Questions go to Dr. Anita White at awhite@imsa.edu or 630-907-5949.
notes: Residential students live in IMSA halls and get all meals. Commuters get breakfast and lunch but must drive to the Aurora campus. Topics change each year.
duration: Two weeks. In 2026 the sessions ran June 1 to 12, June 15 to 26 and July 6 to 17.
pay_detail: No pay and no program cost are stated. The Research Fundamentals course has a fee that is refunded when you finish the course and program. A need-based scholarship exists for that course.

who_can_apply: Students who are a sophomore, junior or senior at a charter or public high school in Illinois. You must be in that grade during the year you apply.
how_to_apply: Make a Submittable account with a personal email, not a school email. Then send in the online application. Finalists do a video interview. Returning members apply again. They skip the interview.
notes: The ISBE page is marked archived, so watch the page for the next call for applications. Next year's dates are not posted; the June 30 date is from the last cycle.
duration: One school year. Members meet several times a month, online and in person.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Open to volunteers who apply. The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Download the Information Booth Volunteer Application PDF from the volunteer page. Call the Special Events Office at 217-782-0777. There is an optional one-hour training workshop.
notes: Ask the Special Events Office if volunteers under 18 are allowed. The page also lists paid seasonal jobs. They are in the grandstand, customer service, grounds and security. It gives no minimum age or pay, so they are not listed here.
duration: 3 to 10 days, 15 hours minimum (2026 fair Aug 13 to 23)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free fair T-shirt, admission and parking

who_can_apply: You must be at least 12 years old and not yet 19. Members under 18 join a cadet or composite squadron, not a senior squadron.
