how_to_apply: Find your local squadron with the unit locator or the Illinois Wing units page. Contact the unit to confirm a meeting. You usually go to about three meetings. Then you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. The national page says ages 12 to 18; the Illinois page says at least 12 and not yet 19. Illinois Wing HQ: 630-524-4400 or wa@ilwg.cap.gov.
duration: Weekly meetings all year
pay_detail: Dues and uniform costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask the squadron.

who_can_apply: High school students. Legislative Assistant and Press Team are open to freshmen through seniors. Lobbyist and Attorney are for sophomores to seniors. Legislator is for juniors and seniors. Anyone can be a Clerk-Bailiff.
how_to_apply: Get the registration link from your local Delegation Advisor. A student and a parent or guardian both sign the code of conduct. You pick a preferred role and give your State Senator and State Representative. Contact the state office if you have no delegation.
notes: Not a job. State office: 1315 Butterfield Rd, Suite 218, Downers Grove, IL 60515, (630) 833-9622, ilyag@ilymcayg.org.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
pay_detail: $455 program fee. Your delegation decides how it is collected (full payment, deposit, or register first). Scholarships are available through the registration application.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. No prerequisite courses.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up link on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. To ask about cost and openings, email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: Asynchronous course with weekly office hours. Only the September 2026 cohort is listed for sign-up.
duration: September 28 to December 18, 2026
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list grades for this course. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a need-based scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: IMSA does not provide a mentor or lab space in this course. Students must complete all assignments by the deadlines to earn the certificate and refund.
duration: 2026 session: March 9 to May 29, 2026
pay_detail: $200. Scholarships are based on financial need. Students who get an SRELO mentor and finish the course get the fee reimbursed.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. You must find your own research mentor and lab space if needed. IMSA cannot provide them.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a scholarship instead. Do not pay if you apply for a scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: It is a hard program. Daily work is expected and you must meet firm deadlines. Failing three deadlines means removal without a refund. IJAS fair entries must be made as an IMSA RISE student for Region 5. Program is non-credit.
duration: September 7, 2026 to May 31, 2027
pay_detail: $1,200. Scholarships based on financial need (free or reduced lunch or SNAP) require a $150 fee, with $100 refunded if you finish.

who_can_apply: Open to all youth in grades 9 to 12. Register through your local Purdue Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Purdue Extension office if you need help signing up.
notes: The page says "contact your local Extension office for registration assistance". Confirm cost and the sign-up steps with Extension.
duration: 3 days (June 10 to 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Indiana 4-H youth in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register through 4-H Online by the deadline.
notes: The flyer was marked coming soon, so start time and details were not posted when read.
pay_detail: $25 per person, or $50 with overnight stay

who_can_apply: Youth who have completed grades 7 and 8 (so they are entering 9th grade).
how_to_apply: Sign up through 4-H Online. Contact your local Purdue Extension office if you need help signing up.
notes: Aimed at incoming 9th graders, so it fits the early end of the guide age range.
duration: 3 days (June 10 to 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: Registration fee was $250 by May 8, $275 for May 9 to 15 and $300 for May 16 to 22 (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Current 4-H members in grades 9 to 11 with strong leadership and 4-H advocacy. You must have been a member for at least 2 years before applying.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has a short questionnaire. It also has a video about why you want to be an ambassador. Use the Apply Now link on the page. Then you have an interview.
notes: You need to be in 4-H first. Find a local club through the Indiana 4-H page.
duration: Not stated on the page. Training is July 30 to August 1.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older; college-age young adults can also work. Workers are expected to live in the reserved dorm space during the job.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the page. Read the schedule for shows with no animals. Email Megan Skiba, skiba0@purdue.edu.
notes: Indiana work permit rules were not checked. Housing is required to be on site.
duration: About 4 weeks (July 31 to Aug 25, 2026)
pay_detail: Minimum wage

who_can_apply: Indiana youth in grades 3 to 12 (Mini 4-H is K to 2 in most counties).
how_to_apply: Start with the club membership page or contact your county or district 4-H office.
notes: Fees are not listed on the page.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Members must be in a business or marketing class now or have been before. The Indiana Department of Education must recognize chapters. They must have business courses. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher. Ask about joining or starting a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Indiana DECA advisor. Use indianadeca@gmail.com.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is indianadeca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Indiana.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $15 per member: $7 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Open to adults and youth. If you are younger than 18, a guardian fills out the Youth Volunteer Service Agreement. The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Create a Volunteer Profile and send the signed Youth Volunteer Service Agreement (guardian signs) to dnrvolunteer@dnr.IN.gov. Check CERVIS for current projects or contact a property near you. Phone 463-203-6562.
notes: Ask the park or property near you what age it takes. The list of tasks on the page is general and not every property offers every task.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. The page also lists unpaid internships for school credit.

who_can_apply: The state page says in-school young adults ages 14 to 21 and out-of-school young adults ages 16 to 24 may be eligible. Eligibility rules beyond age are not stated.
how_to_apply: Connect with your local WorkOne Career Center (Lafayette office serves Tippecanoe County; schedule by appointment through the WorkOne West Central site). Ask about the young adult program.
notes: This is the state workforce agency's WIOA-style youth help, not a single job. The WorkOne West Central about page (older) says a youth program for ages 16 to 24 is offered; the newer state page says 14 to 21 in school. The Bloomington (South Central) WorkOne regional page was not read, so confirm locally. Call before going. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the state page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask the program before you count on either.

who_can_apply: To join FFA, you must be enrolled in an agriculture course at your school. The page does not list grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher about enrolling in an agricultural education class. The Indiana Agricultural Education site explains how to start a program if your school has none.
notes: Not a job. Your school needs an ag class and an FFA chapter. The page links the Indiana Agricultural Education program for how to start one.
duration: School year
pay_detail: State dues are $14 per active member per year (includes national, state and district dues). Local chapters set their own local dues.

who_can_apply: Boys going into their senior year of high school. No age limit is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Registration opens January 11, 2027 on the Hoosier Boys State site. The application steps are not on the pages. Email info@hoosierboysstate.org or call 317-630-1301.
notes: The FAQ on the About page says the cost to attend is $400. The About page says a $50 non-refundable application fee is due, and the remaining $350 sponsorship fee is paid by a local American Legion Post or other community partner. Drop-off and pickup is at the MTI Center, 1215 Thunder Ave, Angola, IN. Not a job. The page links to a separate Girls State site (alahgs.org) that returned a 404, so no Hoosier Girls State card was written.
duration: One week
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. The About page lists scholarships for college. Bring no more than $30 spending money.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). Cadets can stay in until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Indiana Wing office: 4760 Andrews St, Columbus, IN 47203, 877-350-8643, info@inwg.cap.gov.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the program pages. The application lists payment options.

who_can_apply: The page says anyone seeking a work-based learning experience, and lists high schools among its partners. It does not state a minimum age. Learners can create an account on the site.
how_to_apply: Make a free learner account on the site. Search for chances by region. Then apply to each one you like.
notes: The site has a Create Your Account link for learners. The page does not state age rules for postings, so check each posting. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The site moved from indianaintern.net to workandlearnindiana.com.
pay_detail: Varies by employer. Each posting sets its own pay.

who_can_apply: Indiana high school students with an adult mentor. Grades and ages are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Not posted yet. Contact Anna Egan (williaak@purdue.edu) for questions.
notes: Check back for registration dates. A research paper is part of taking part.
duration: One event
pay_detail: Free event

who_can_apply: Hoosier students in 6th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Contact Shelby Lashbrook. Use shelby@indianaymcas.org or (317) 715-2145. Do this to join, start a delegation, volunteer or sponsor.
notes: Not a job. Office: 6610 N Shadeland Ave, Indianapolis, IN 46220, open Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
pay_detail: Program fees are not listed on the program page. Ask the program contact.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages do not explain parent consent for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Fill out the application. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Examples are proof of income and proof of citizenship or residency. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Address: 1480 Snelling Ave N, St. Paul, MN 55108. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. After applying, the national site says the review includes a background check (1 to 2 weeks) and a campus review (about 30 days).
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Workdays are described as for all ages, individuals and families. No sign up needed unless you come with a group of 10 or more. Age rules for the longer volunteer roles are not on the pages.
how_to_apply: For workdays, just show up 5 to 10 minutes early and sign in with the leader. For longer roles, fill out the volunteer application on the site. Volunteer Office: 630-762-2741, volunteer@kaneforest.com.
notes: Bring boots or sturdy shoes, a water bottle and gloves. Info on Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects is in the Resources section of the volunteer page. Questions about workdays: Stewardship Specialist, 630-200-1290.
duration: Workdays are monthly. Cancelled when it is below zero.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Kane, DeKalb or Kendall County. The page lists no income or other rules (federal workforce funding rules may apply, so ask the provider).
how_to_apply: Pick a provider on the page and contact them directly. Providers in Kane County include Elgin Community College and Business & Career Services Inc. Waubonsee Community College covers Kane and Kendall. Not sure where to start? Call 630-762-2085.
notes: Starts at age 16, so it fits older high schoolers. The page names one contact person but lists an email that does not match that name, so phone first. Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor grant per the page. Elgin Community College's own Future Workforce Leaders program is one of the providers.
duration: Varies by provider
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one of the services; pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Current students in grades 9 to 11 in the Naperville area. The page does not give a school or residency rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. For questions, contact the KidsMatter Director of Programs. Call 630-864-3960 or write to sherilyn@kidsmatter2us.org.
notes: The page still showed the 2025-26 call when read. Check back in spring for the next one.
duration: One school year, with monthly meetings
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It is a leadership role.

who_can_apply: The page does not state an age rule. Call the museum to ask if teens can volunteer.
how_to_apply: Click Sign Up to Volunteer on the volunteer page (a Google Form). Phone 765-742-1128.
notes: No teen rules are posted, so confirm your age is allowed before you sign up. Museum is at 102 S. 10th Street, Lafayette. Admission is free.
duration: Event by event
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours verification papers provided.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 to 17 years old on June 1 of the year they apply. Teens interested in any career field may apply. A parent or guardian must co-sign the online application. A teacher or mentor recommendation form is part of the process.
how_to_apply: Read the Zoo Teen Information Packet, apply online through the zoo's volunteer form (applicant and parent both e-sign), and submit the teacher or mentor recommendation form. Contact: zooteen@lafayette.in.gov, 765-807-1543.
notes: Opening date for 2027 is not posted; the page only says check back in January 2027. The page mentions sponsors that keep costs low for participants but does not state a fee amount. The information packet was not read, so shift length and total hours are not stated here.
duration: Summer; shift details are in the 2026 Zoo Teen Information Packet (not read)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 9. Everyone under 18 needs a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. Ages 9 to 15 need an adult chaperone (1 adult for every 5 youths). Individual 16 and 17 year olds can volunteer without a chaperone. Groups of 16 and 17 year olds need chaperones (1 adult for every 10 youths). You must be at least 14 to volunteer at the Fresh Market.
how_to_apply: Create a VolunteerHub account (a parent or guardian creates the profile for a child), pick a shift on the volunteer calendar, and bring the signed waiver to your first shift. Questions: call 765-471-0062.
notes: Some shifts have their own age rules. A parent or guardian needs to make the account for anyone under 18. Court ordered community service hours need separate approval before you start.
duration: Single shifts you pick on the calendar
pay_detail: Unpaid. Training is given at the start of your first shift.

who_can_apply: The Franciscan Health page says volunteers include men, women and teens. Minimum age for Lafayette East is not stated; the system page says each hospital sets its own age rules. Ask the volunteer manager.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer form on the Lafayette page. You can also call Lisa Green at 765-502-4249. She is the Volunteer Services Manager.
notes: Call to check the minimum age before you apply. The hospice program has its own form. It was not checked for teen rules.
duration: Usually once or twice a week for 3 to 4 hours, plus orientation and at least 2 days of training
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Grade 11 and 12 students at Harrison, Jefferson, Lafayette Virtual Academy, McCutcheon, Tippecanoe Online Academy or West Lafayette high schools. Home school and private school students who live in those districts can also apply. Other students may get leftover seats if their superintendent signs an agreement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Harrison, Jefferson, McCutcheon and West Lafayette students get the enrollment form link from their counselor. Everyone else fills out the online Enrollment Form on the Next Steps page.
notes: Competitive. Seats are ranked on attendance, behavior, credits, GPA and past courses, and GLCA makes the final call. Each program has its own prerequisites on its page. The pages do not say how long the day is, how transportation works, or what it costs.
duration: School-year program for grades 11 and 12; schedule not stated
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. The academics page says students can earn college credit.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors from partner regional high schools. The page does not say how a student signs up, so ask your school counselor.
how_to_apply: Not stated. Students take part through their partner high school.
notes: Check with your high school counselor to see if your school takes part.
duration: One day
pay_detail: Free event

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 15 who can pass a swim test (20-yard swim, 7 to 10 foot brick dive and carry, 2 minute tread, 300-yard swim). Limited to the first 20 applicants.
how_to_apply: Fill in the form online. You can also drop it off at the Parks Office, 1915 Scott Street in Columbian Park. Or sign up in the parks online catalog under the LIFEGUARD CERTIFICATION tab.
notes: Classes meet at the Lafayette Jefferson High School pool. The page does not name the year; the weekday dates match 2026. Pay for the lifeguard job is not on this page.
duration: Four class days in March and April (2026 dates were March 12 pre-test, then April 10 to 12) plus some online Red Cross work
pay_detail: $250 course fee covers the course, materials and Red Cross certification. $200 is refunded if you pass, get hired by Lafayette Parks and finish a full season. Job pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Kids and teens ages 7 to 17. A parent must sign the registration form.
how_to_apply: Get the registration form from the Parks Office in Columbian Park, or download it. A parent signs it. Hand it to the Workreation Coordinator on your first day. Call 765-807-1500.
notes: Good first volunteer step for younger teens. Not a paid job.
duration: 1 hour a day at Tropicanoe Cove, Vinton Pool or Castaway Bay (June 1 to July 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn one Kids Can Pass for each hour worked (good for city pool admission and Columbian Park rides).

who_can_apply: High school students who are current freshmen, sophomores or juniors. Apply through Purdue Summer College for High School Students.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Purdue Summer College for High School Students application and pick it as a short-term course choice. Questions go to Anna Egan (williaak@purdue.edu).
notes: Residential. Admission is not guaranteed and you list up to three course choices on the application. Prices are 2026 and may change.
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 Summer College prices for a 1-week, 1-credit program: Indiana resident $725.80 (tuition plus room and board), out-of-state $1,326.25, plus a $60 non-refundable application fee. Scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Students entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade for Senior Camp. The page says the minimum age for camp is 12. Past campers cannot repeat the same camp.
how_to_apply: Online camper application on the Boiler Vet Camp page (not open yet). Ask for a scholarship inside the same application.
notes: Call the College of Veterinary Medicine at 765-494-7607 with questions. Camp fees are all-inclusive for the hands-on in-residence camps.
duration: 7 days (Senior Camp June 20 to 26, 2027)
pay_detail: Senior Camp is $1,600 and Junior Camp is $1,300. Partial scholarships are available and requested in the application.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. No other rule is stated on the camp page.
how_to_apply: Apply through Purdue's Summer College for High School Students (the camp page says the 2026 application was there). Questions: purdueag@purdue.edu.
notes: This is a camp, not a job, and it costs money. The Purdue ag summer programs index page describes the high school camp as a two-week experience. The camp page itself says one week. Confirm the length with purdueag@purdue.edu.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the camp page. Summer College for High School Students sets the price (see the Purdue Summer College card).

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 (the Pulsar level). New students send an essay or other media about their interest. They also send two of these. One is a transcript with a 3.5 GPA in the talent area. Others are a test score of 120 or higher on an intelligence test and a 90th percentile achievement or aptitude test. A teacher or mentor letter counts. So does proof of involvement such as awards.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application through the Purdue conferences site (the Register Now link on the page). Upload your essay or media and two supporting documents. Questions: geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. Checked against the GER2I summer residential page on 2026-10-10: the 2026 dates, the $2,990 Pulsar rate, the $100 application fee and the required application materials match. The page says registration for Summer 2026 is open and also says it opens February 2, 2026, so it is inconsistent. 2027 dates are not posted. Confirm with geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210 before you plan. The page also lists other prices ($1,250 commuter and $1,495 residential per session). They may be for the younger levels.
duration: 2 week sessions
pay_detail: 2026 listing: $2,990 per session for Star or Pulsar, plus a $100 application fee (refunded only if not accepted). Optional $100 Saturday field trip. A 5% early bird discount applied by Feb 17. A limited number of partial scholarships exist for students with financial need, first come, first served.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th, 10th and 11th graders. The 2025 page says the camp has a focus on high school female students. Age limit not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has an Apply Now link to the Summer College application page, but it shows no year. Contact techrecruit@purdue.edu or 765-494-4935.
notes: This page looks old (2025 dates). Check Purdue Polytechnic and the Summer College site for current dates and cost before planning. Offered with Purdue Summer College for High School Students. The 2025 page lists $350 per person, including activities, lodging, meals and a camp t-shirt.
duration: 1 week, 1 college credit (page lists June 23 to 27, 2025)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page checked for this card

who_can_apply: Rising 10th and 11th graders. Age limit not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has a Register Now button linking to the Summer College registration site, but it shows no year. Contact techrecruit@purdue.edu or 765-494-4935.
notes: This page looks old (2025 dates). Check Purdue Polytechnic and the Summer College site for current dates and cost before planning. The 2025 page lists $350 per person, including activities, lodging, meals and a camp t-shirt.
duration: 1 week, 1 college credit (page lists June 23 to 27, 2025)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page checked for this card

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Grade 8-12 Students Sign up for SMAP button on the page (a form). You are then notified about upcoming sessions.
notes: The SMAP page says the program is live on Zoom. The page does not mention cost. Check the sign-up form for the current format.
duration: About 1 session a month, third Saturdays at 11:00 a.m. Eastern
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering 7th or 8th grade in fall 2027. Selected through a competitive review.
how_to_apply: Submit a student application with a Statement of Interest essay, plus a teacher recommendation (a science teacher is preferred).
notes: For younger teens. Questions: Connie Kaspar, 765-496-6095, ScienceWISP@purdue.edu.
duration: June 20 to 24, 2027, residential
pay_detail: $600 registration fee covers residence hall, meals, snacks, labs and activities. Full payment due within two weeks of acceptance.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors (Class of 2027 for the 2026 camp). Purdue recommends three years of high school math and one year of chemistry or physics by summer.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A complete application needs your PSAT, SAT or ACT scores and a transcript. Applications are taken until spots are full, then a waiting list. Questions: step@purdue.edu or 765-494-7217.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. Only for students going into their senior year. The page gives 2026 information, so check it for the 2027 cycle.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: Attendance fee $2,500 for 2026. It covers activities, housing, meals and local transportation. You pay your own travel to Purdue. Need-based scholarships are available after you are accepted.

who_can_apply: High school students. Main page says ages 15 to 17. Application page: priority for GPA 3.30 or higher and at least 16 who have finished sophomore year, younger students may apply. Residential courses require being under 18 for the whole program. Course-specific rules apply.
how_to_apply: Online Summer College application: essay, high school transcript, up to three short-term course choices, $60 non-refundable fee. Admitted students first get one course; more are offered as space allows in late March to early April.
notes: Costs are summer 2026 and may change. Some courses were full for 2026 and some were canceled. The listed short courses include PREFACE and MITE, which are pre-college engineering workshops, with their own eligibility. The student pays; this is not a job.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks, residential, June and July
pay_detail: Summer 2026 prices: $60 application fee. Tuition and fees $347.85 per credit hour for Indiana residents ($948.30 nonresident). Room and board $377.95 for a 1-week program, $907.08 for 2 weeks. Some courses add $60 or $200 program fees. Scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Battlefield Museum, Genealogy Center and Collections roles say volunteers must be 18 or older. The Fort Ouiatenon, History on Tour and Feast pages do not state an age rule, so ask before you apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out a volunteer application and attend an interview. Every role needs on-site training, and no experience is required. Call 765-476-8411 or email info@tippecanoehistory.org.
notes: Ask the museum whether 14 to 17 year olds can take the Fort Ouiatenon or History on Tour roles.

notes: The page still shows the Summer 2026 schedule, so the 2027 dates are a guess based on last year. The page's email link points to volunteer@henryvilaszoo.gov while the text says education@henryvilaszoo.gov, so check both. Phone on the page: 608-266-4732. Not a paid job.
duration: 8 weeks, two days a week (June 22 to Aug 21 in 2026)
pay_detail: $200 per teen for the summer. Scholarships are available. Applying is free and payment is due only after you are invited.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 can volunteer on their own in many roles. Ages 10 to 14 can only volunteer with a parent or guardian, and only in some roles (gate greeters, goat yard, events, wildlife champions). The youngest age for any role is 10, with a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Pick a role on the zoo's Volunteer Roles page and fill out the application at the bottom of that role's page. Join the volunteer email list through the Volunteer Inquiry Form to hear about openings and information sessions.
notes: If you need school-required hours, check with your school counselor first. The zoo does not currently support court-ordered community service hours.
duration: Seasonal; commitment varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid. The zoo does not do last-minute school hour confirmations.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from the Madison area who care about the arts.
how_to_apply: Not described on the page. Call MMoCA at (608) 257-0158 to ask when the next application opens.
notes: The page may be out of date (it mentions the 2025 group), so confirm by phone before planning around it. Small group.
duration: 6 to 8 hours per month, in person at MMoCA, through the year
pay_detail: Members are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Juniors at an MMSD high school at the time of application.
how_to_apply: Send the online student application. You also need a note from a science teacher, a second note and a parent consent form. Questions: Kristen Riddle, sriprogram@madison.k12.wi.us.
notes: You must attend a March orientation with a parent or guardian and all seminars. Only for MMSD students.
duration: 9 weeks, 20 to 25 hours a week
pay_detail: The page does not say if it is paid. Students earn one UW-Madison college credit and high school science and experiential learning credit.

who_can_apply: MMSD juniors and seniors. You must pass an interview with an employer to get a placement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your Youth Apprenticeship coordinator or school counselor, join the Google Classroom, go to Workplace Success Workshops, do an intake screening, then interview with employers. Coordinator: Annie Johnston, ajohnston2@madison.k12.wi.us.
notes: The page does not name a year for February 13, so confirm the date. Related cards cover the Dane County and state youth apprenticeship programs.
duration: Program length not stated on the page. Explore runs October to December; interviews run March to July.
pay_detail: At least the state minimum wage. The page says students typically earn about $15 an hour on average.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 in the Dane County area. Juniors and seniors need a referral from their home school. MMSD applicants must be entering the fourth quarter of junior year before applying.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Legacy page (opens a Google Form). Seniors and juniors also need a referral from their home school.
notes: Free program. Staff mentor graduates for one year after completion. Phone (608) 244-4721, info@operationfreshstart.org, 2670 Milwaukee St, Madison. The program starts at 16, so the Wisconsin permit rule for 14 and 15 year olds does not apply to it.
duration: At least 1,000 program hours (total length not stated)
pay_detail: Bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated). Finishers may earn an AmeriCorps Education Award of about $2,800 for college.

who_can_apply: The form has an age category of '17 and under', and the page says teens can volunteer to complete school hours. A minimum age is not stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form (area of interest, availability, branch). Staff reply by email. A background check is required under City of Madison APM 2-44.
notes: On Oct 9, 2026 the page said Central Library had no openings and asked high school students needing hours (for example National Honor Society) to check back in fall 2026. Alicia Ashman, Hawthorne, Lakeview and Meadowridge listed no openings or a waitlist. Ask a branch before counting on hours.
duration: Varies by branch
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 17. Ages 12 to 15 must have an adult chaperone (21 or older) for the whole shift. Ages 16 and 17 can volunteer without a chaperone.
how_to_apply: Register in the Second Harvest volunteer portal and sign up for a Food Sort/Repack shift. Bring a youth waiver signed by a parent or guardian to each shift. Questions: volunteers@secondharvestsw.org or 608-216-7214.
notes: Groups with youth should add (YOUTH) to the group name when signing up.
duration: Per shift; length not stated on the page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: The page says adults and teens interested in nature education can serve as assistant naturalists. No exact age is stated.
how_to_apply: Contact volunteer program manager Judy Kingsbury at (608) 262-5604 or judith.kingsbury@wisc.edu.
notes: Drop-in restoration work parties run most Saturday mornings from mid-February through mid-December. Check the Arboretum events calendar for times. The page does not state a minimum age for them.
duration: Camp sessions; schedule not posted
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Badger Dairy Camp registration form when it opens. Questions: badgerdairycamp@ansci.wisc.edu.
notes: Students stay in the Dejope Residence Hall, two to a room.
duration: 4 days (2026: July 8 to 11)
pay_detail: $175 non-refundable registration fee covers housing and dining. Grants and sponsors cover the rest.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay when you sign up. Send scholarship forms to info@precollege.wisc.edu.
notes: The page shows 2025 dates, so confirm the next session.
duration: 4 weeks, Tuesdays and Thursdays 6 to 8 pm (Oct 21 to Nov 13 in 2025)
pay_detail: $480. Full and partial scholarships available; Wisconsin students on free or reduced lunch can apply for a full scholarship.

who_can_apply: Eligibility is not stated on the web page. It points to separate Program Details and FAQ files. Check them before applying.
how_to_apply: Apply online with unofficial transcripts, two essays and a letter of recommendation. Questions: Mary Headington, education@cancer.wisc.edu.
notes: Pay and who can apply are in linked PDF files that were not checked for this card. This is a different program from HERO.
duration: 2026: June 15 to Aug 7
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin high school students going into freshman, sophomore or junior year. You must be a full time student. You need a strong interest in research or cancer jobs. Students from rural school districts get priority. Past SHE participants are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has two personal statements of up to 250 words each. Someone who is not family must fill out a reference survey for you.
notes: You need a reliable computer and internet. Some money for tech is offered.
duration: 2 weeks (July 20 to 31 in 2026), weekdays 9 am to 1 pm
pay_detail: $500 taxable stipend for full participation. No fee is mentioned and lab materials are provided.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 and up who can commit to at least one full semester.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Wisconsin volunteer application on the UW Health volunteer page when it opens. Onboarding takes several weeks: online trainings, health assessment, placement interview, caregiver background check.
notes: Health clearance is required: seasonal flu shot, MMR, varicella, Tdap and a TB blood test. The page says waivers and exemptions are not accepted. Volunteer Services: (608) 263-6046, volunteer.services@uwhealth.org. The same page also covers Illinois locations; this card is for the Wisconsin application.
duration: At least one full semester
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Students enter in 8th grade and plan to attend a participating school. The page says Madison Metropolitan School District students need at least a 2.75 GPA and must submit an application.
how_to_apply: Submit a PEOPLE Precollege application through the program site.
notes: Entry is at 8th grade, so most teens who find this are already past the usual start. Ask about joining later. A separate PEOPLE Milwaukee track starts in 9th grade.
duration: 8th grade through high school graduation
pay_detail: Cost and any internship pay are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores or juniors with a 3.0 GPA or higher.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add a PDF transcript and two short answers of 150 to 300 words each on why you like pharmacy. Contact PharmD@pharmacy.wisc.edu or 608-262-6234.
notes: Check the PharmD events page for the PSP 2027 announcement.
duration: 5 days (July 12 to 16 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students who are finishing grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Sign up online. For questions, write to summerartsclinic@precollege.wisc.edu or call 608-263-2242.
notes: You can stay on campus or come each day as a commuter.
duration: 1 week (July 12 to 18 in 2026)
pay_detail: Residential $1,275; daily commuter $875; plus a $75 nonrefundable fee. Need-based scholarships are limited.

who_can_apply: Students who are finishing grades 9 to 12. At sign-up, everyone picks a placement audition or a talk with staff.
how_to_apply: Register online. Questions: smc@wisc.edu or 608-263-2242.
notes: The Violin Institute has room for only 12 students. It needs a recorded audition. The date was April 1 in 2026.
duration: 1 week (June 28 to July 4 in 2026)
pay_detail: Residential $1,275; daily commuter $875; Violin Institute $1,500; plus a $75 nonrefundable registration fee. Financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th and 10th grade students interested in business. Preference goes to first-generation college students and students who get free or reduced lunch, but others can apply and may be waitlisted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the precollege page. If accepted, a parent signs waivers and pays the fee.
notes: Not residential: families arrange their own housing and transportation. Apply by the end of April, but programs can close when full.
duration: 4 days, June 14 to 17, 2027, 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: Nonrefundable enrollment fee; the amount is not posted. Email wsbprecollege@wsb.wisc.edu about fees and financial help.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in business. Preference goes to first-generation college and low-income students.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the precollege page.
notes: There is also a one-day workshop on April 10, 2027 called Her View, Her Voice (applications Dec 1, 2026 to Mar 26, 2027).
duration: 1 day, Nov 14, 2026, 9:30 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: Enrollment fee amount is not posted (lunch is provided). Email wsbprecollege@wsb.wisc.edu.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students interested in business. Preference goes to first-generation college students and students who get free or reduced lunch, but others can apply and may be waitlisted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the precollege page. If accepted, a parent signs waivers and pays the fee.
notes: Past field trip sites named on the page include Trek Bikes and Epic. Not residential.
duration: 4 days, 9 am to 4 pm. Session 1: June 21 to 24, 2027. Session 2: June 28 to July 1, 2027
pay_detail: Nonrefundable enrollment fee; the amount is not posted. Email wsbprecollege@wsb.wisc.edu about fees and financial help.

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 14 years old when they apply. They must live in the City of Madison limits or attend a Madison Metropolitan School.
how_to_apply: The library page does not list application steps. Call Madison Public Library at 608-266-6300 or Common Wealth Development at (608) 256-3527.
notes: The library page says the program has mandatory pre-internship training and weekly professional development during the internship. The Common Wealth Development website was under construction when checked, so confirm details with them before applying. The library page does not state the age 14 minimum, the Madison residency rule, the pay rate or the hours; confirm these with Common Wealth Development before applying.
duration: 8-week summer internship. The library page does not give dates.
pay_detail: Wages start at $15.50 an hour, about 20 hours a week (2026).

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in south central Wisconsin (job centers in Dane, Sauk and Jefferson counties). Whether in-school youth qualify is not stated.
how_to_apply: Go to a free info session. It is listed on Eventbrite from the page. Or visit a Job Center, or call 608-249-9001.
notes: Eligibility rules (such as income) are not on the page, so call before you count on a paid placement.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Free. The page says all WorkSmart Network services are free of charge and does not say anyone is paid.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in participating Dane and Jefferson county school districts. Employers choose and hire apprentices.
how_to_apply: Contact your school district's School to Career Coordinator (the page lists a name and phone for each district, for example Madison Metropolitan: Annie Johnston, 608-663-5384). Register for an information night on the program page.
notes: The page lists the Jan 20, 2027 information night, but its registration link address ends in Jan202026, so confirm the date with the program. Students interested in UW Health need the Feb 17 session. Main office 608-249-9001. Ask the coordinator whether your age needs a Wisconsin work permit.
duration: 1 or 2 years
pay_detail: Paid while working; wage not stated.

who_can_apply: Female high school students who will finish their junior year in spring 2027. You must have at least one more semester before graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online delegate application. The link is on the Michigan Girls State page and the 2027 flyer. Questions go to the Girls State chairman, Beryl Robbins, at berylrobbins1980@gmail.com or (313) 318-6845.
notes: Not a job. A closing date was not on the page or flyer, so apply early. The page also lists a Samsung scholarship and a government manual to read before attending.
duration: One week, June 13 to 19, 2027
pay_detail: Cost to the student is not stated on the program pages. The page asks people to donate to send a young woman to Girls State.

who_can_apply: Males who have finished junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You should like government and show leadership, character and school or community service. You must be a U.S. citizen. You cannot attend Boys State twice.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on michiganboysstate.org (the 2026 brochure says to visit the website to apply). Pay the $25 application fee and find a sponsor for the $400 program fee. Office: (517) 371-4720 ext. 123 (site) or 517-220-2754 (brochure), legion@michiganlegion.org.
notes: Not a job. Dates, fees and the deadline above are from the 2026 brochure and flyer, so confirm the 2027 details with the office. The resources page still showed a May 1, 2024 deadline, so it is out of date. Office address: 212 N. Verlinden Ave., Lansing, MI 48915.
duration: One week (2026: June 21 to 27)
pay_detail: $25 application fee paid by the student. The $400 program fee is paid by a sponsor such as a local American Legion Post or other community group (2026 brochure).

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 26 with a visual impairment. The school can refer you at your IEP meeting.
how_to_apply: Contact your local BSBP office or your school special education office. You can also fill out the form at the IEP meeting.
notes: Programs may target a certain age group, interest or skill.
duration: Programs run throughout the year
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: People 16 or older. The form has a box for ages 16 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form on the page, sign up for an open house, or contact the Volunteer Coordinator at 248-341-2756 or CIS_volunteer@cranbrook.edu. Required paperwork is needed.
notes: Special Events Volunteer is a good short option for community service hours. Nature Zone shifts are weekends and select holidays.
duration: A regular schedule is welcome but not required. Special event shifts are short.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a marketing, management, finance, hospitality or entrepreneurship course. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Michigan DECA advisor, Dave Wait. His email is dwait@emich.edu.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is mideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Michigan.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $17 per student member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Must live in Detroit and be 14 to 24. You must show papers that prove age, residency and eligibility. Some programs also take Highland Park and Hamtramck residents.
how_to_apply: Call 313-962-WORK (9675) or visit a Detroit at Work career center (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.). Bring documents that prove age and where you live.
notes: Summer jobs are a separate track (Grow Detroit's Young Talent). Pay rates and the work permit rule for this program are not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Free to join. Offers paid and unpaid work experiences, plus stipends for training and career exploration. Amounts not stated.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Detroit. Ages 14 to 24. You can apply at 13 if you turn 14 by July 1.
how_to_apply: Express interest at GDYT.org. Picks are made by random lottery. If chosen, finish enrollment forms and upload documents (including a work permit for ages 14 to 17), then attend orientation.
notes: The FAQ lists a work permit for ages 14 to 17 as a required document. Up to 8,000 spots in 2026, so a lottery decides. Next year's window is likely spring 2027.
duration: About 6 weeks, up to 120 hours, usually early July through August
pay_detail: Wage jobs pay $12.50 to $15 per hour, paid every two weeks. Stipend jobs pay $1,500 to $2,000.

who_can_apply: First-time participants who go to high school or live in metro Detroit, in 10th or 11th grade, age 16 or older by program start, GPA 2.5 or higher, and allowed to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Email HAPE@hfhs.org with questions.
notes: The page says students under 18 must get a work permit. Teens must also join at least one year-round track.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 28 to Aug 7, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) plus monthly meetings September to May
pay_detail: The page says stipends or wages may be available for high school students but are not guaranteed. The program is free.

who_can_apply: Detroit-area high school students who are curious about health care. No medical experience needed. Grades and school districts are not listed.
how_to_apply: Submit the online internship application form linked on the summer internship page. For the program, email iokerek1@hfhs.org or call 313-916-2698.
notes: Very competitive: the page says 331 applied and 25 were chosen in 2025. The application link may be the 2026 form, so check the page for the next one.
duration: 7-week summer internship. Saturday sessions during the school year.
pay_detail: Program is free. Summer interns get a $1,000 stipend for 7 weeks.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors (going into 12th grade) and college freshmen, sophomores and juniors.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the program site. A 2-day orientation comes first. Students finish assignments and weekly classes.
notes: Rising seniors and college students apply to the same program. Contact: medicalmentorspipeline@gmail.com. Cost was not stated, so ask before applying.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 24 to August 6)
pay_detail: Pay and cost not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who passes a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application, then wait for an interview to find the best fit.
notes: The page does not list specific roles or hours. Ask the volunteer team (volunteers@mi-sci.org) about teen roles.
duration: Time commitment not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students from Metro Detroit with little or no investing knowledge.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application packet. Add two letters of recommendation and the signed forms. Email it to edwarddj1@udmercy.edu.
notes: Held on the McNichols Campus, 4001 West McNichols Rd. The camp page still says applications are open, but the 2026 camp dates have passed. Ask the camp director before you apply.
duration: One week. In 2026 it ran June 22 to 26, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily.
pay_detail: Free. Materials, breakfast, snacks, lunch, a T-shirt and a backpack are included.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who want to explore health careers. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: The 2026 camp is full, so you cannot apply now. The program page does not post 2027 sign-up dates. Questions can go to Nina Favor at favornf@udmercy.edu.
notes: Held at the STAR Center on the McNichols Campus. The middle school week was July 20 to 24, 2026. The high school week was July 27 to 31, 2026.
duration: One week. In 2026 the high school week was July 27 to 31, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. Breakfast, lunch and snacks are included. Campers also get a lab jacket and a blood pressure cuff.

who_can_apply: High school students in 10th, 11th or 12th grade with a GPA of 2.75 or higher. Priority goes to Wayne County residents, Detroit Public Schools Community District students, and students from disadvantaged backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and write a 300 to 400 word personal statement. An official transcript is needed if you are accepted.
notes: Program dates may change. Contact: BCAPstudentgroup@gmail.com or (313) 577-1584.
duration: 6 weeks. Monday to Thursday up to 5 hours a day, plus Friday events 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: Students who finish may get a monetary award. It depends on funding and is not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. Choose camp I or II of a topic, not both.
how_to_apply: Register through the Summer Academy pages. Use the question link to reach the Director of Community Engagement.
notes: Cost was not stated on the pages. Ask about the scholarship page before you decide.
duration: 1 week per camp. You can mix topics across weeks.
pay_detail: Price not on the program pages. A scholarships page is listed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 by June 1. You need your own ride to the zoo.
how_to_apply: Send the application and documents on the zoo page. A parent and teen must do a phone or video interview. Go to one mandatory virtual meeting, then a full training week (9 a.m. to 4 p.m.) in late June or early July.
notes: Work is outdoors in all weather. Training hours count toward the 60. A separate Counselor in Training program is listed but the page gave no details. Questions go to the zoo education department.
duration: Summer track: 60 hours June to August. Year-round track adds shifts September to May.
pay_detail: Cost not listed

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 21 who are enrolled in a state-approved agricultural education course. The page does not list grades.
how_to_apply: Use the chapters and regions page to find a chapter near you, then ask that school about its agriculture class. Questions can go to the state office.
notes: Not a job. The homepage says there are over 10,000 members in 137 chapters. State office: association@michiganffa.org or (517) 353-9221.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teams of high school students. The page does not give an age or grade rule. It links to Start a Team and Run a Team.
how_to_apply: Join an existing school or community team or use the Start a Team link on the FIRST in Michigan site. Contact on the page: Gail Alpert, 248.425.4148.
notes: Ask your school if it has a team. FIRST in Michigan also runs FTC and FIRST LEGO League for younger students.
duration: Build and competition season
pay_detail: Registration cost not stated. Scholarships are listed through FIRST.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished at least freshman year. The page recommends age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply on the hospital page when it opens. Spaces are limited and picks are made after an interview. Orientation is required. The application includes a health screening checklist, and a parent must be there for any shots.
notes: Jackson is west of Ann Arbor and south of Lansing, so it may be a drive. Teens must commit to all assigned shifts.
duration: 8 weeks, at least one 4-hour shift a week (2026: June 8 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students interested in health care, through a school chapter. The site also says you can start a chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your school health or CTE teacher about a chapter, or use the Join MI HOSA link on the site. Contact: hosa@mhc.org or (517) 347-8088.
notes: The site lists more than 10,000 Michigan members.
duration: School year. State conference in April 2027 at the Grand Traverse Resort.
pay_detail: Dues and fees not stated on the home page

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Children must come with a registered adult.
how_to_apply: Pick a workday on the volunteering page and register online by noon the day before. For regular volunteering, send the application and waiver to volunteer@metroparks.com.
notes: Dress for dirt: long pants, closed-toe shoes, layers. Poison ivy can be present. Children must come with a registered adult. Volunteers under 14 must have an adult with them for the whole shift, and a parent or guardian must sign the waiver for volunteers under 18. The volunteering page does not mention seasonal paid jobs.
duration: About 2 hours (10 a.m. to noon)
pay_detail: Free, unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in or go to school in Jackson County.
how_to_apply: Use the Youth and Young Adult Application link on the Jump-Start Jackson page.
notes: The Summer Youth Employment page lists it as one of the Michigan Works! Southeast summer programs. Jackson is west of Ann Arbor. Ask about dates and pay.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Paid on-the-job training; rate not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Livingston County. Juniors and seniors in high school, or anyone 24 or younger regardless of graduation.
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us link on the YouthWorks page, or call the Michigan Works! Southeast office.
notes: Livingston County is northwest of Ann Arbor (Howell and Brighton area). The page does not state the work permit rule for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: 2026 program: June 15 to August 14
pay_detail: Paid; the page does not state the hourly rate

who_can_apply: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 26 who are in school or have been accepted at school after high school. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must sign a consent form. Your school fills out a form that shows the disability.
how_to_apply: Use the MRS Online Application. Forms MRS-4.0a (parent consent) and MRS-4.0b (school verification) are on the page. Phone 517-241-5324 or toll-free 800-605-6722.
notes: Work-based learning is one of five services. Ask your school transition coordinator or counselor too.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: MRS pays for services in your employment plan. Not a wage.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students from around the world. The cost page lists no grade rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Now link on the Summer Youth Programs page and pay the $150 deposit at registration. Pathway programs have nothing due at application. Contact syp@mtu.edu or 906-487-2219.
notes: Extra costs can include lab fees, a $20 weekly parking pass and charter bus service. Check the Course Catalog and Scholarships pages on the SYP site for current offerings.
duration: Week-long programs
pay_detail: Exploration programs start at $1,175 live-in (tuition, fees, meals, room and board) or $700 commuter. A $150 non-refundable deposit is due at registration. Pathway program fees vary. Scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in Oakland County. Other rules are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Oakland NEXT application on the Youth page. Or call 248-858-5520 or email oaklandcountymiworks@oaklandcountymi.gov.
notes: The county reported 164 paid work experiences with 60 employers in 2024. The page also lists an IAmPontiac summer internship; details were not read. Ask about the work permit rule for ages 16 and 17.
duration: Not stated. Offers summer and year-round internships.
pay_detail: Internships are typically paid. Pay rate not stated.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Contact it to confirm a meeting. Go to about three meetings before you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Wing HQ mailing address: 43401 N. Jefferson, Bldg. 825, Rm 317, PO Box 450048, Selfridge ANGB, MI 48045-0048. School comes first; the page says school-based squadrons may differ.
duration: Ideally a 2-hour squadron meeting each week plus about one Saturday event a month. A week-long summer encampment is encouraged.
pay_detail: Annual dues are $40 for cadets. The page estimates a fully active cadet could spend $300 to $600 in the first year, minus help for uniforms and overnight fees.

who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low income and have at least one listed barrier (for example basic skills deficient, English language learner, homeless or foster youth, pregnant or parenting, disability). Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with a listed barrier.
how_to_apply: Call Michigan Works! at 1-800-285-WORKS (9675). Or find your local agency by ZIP code at michiganworks.org. Then ask about WIOA Youth eligibility.
notes: Not open to every teen: eligibility depends on income and barriers, so a short call to the local agency is the real first step. The state page does not list a local application form or local youth contacts. Capital Area Michigan Works!' own site (camw.org) mentions WIOA and says 259 youth were served but does not describe its youth program in detail. Work experience for anyone under 18 in Michigan needs a work permit under the state's youth employment law.
duration: Varies by local agency
pay_detail: Not stated. The state page lists both paid and unpaid work experiences, including summer employment, as possible services.

who_can_apply: High school students (a separate middle school program exists). The pages do not list grades. You join through a school or YMCA delegation.
how_to_apply: Check the map on the YMCA page to see if your school or YMCA has a delegation. If not, use the Contact us page to start one. Then register for the conferences your delegation attends.
notes: Not a job. The deadline_iso is the end of regular registration for the February Lansing conference. Fall conference sites include Marquette, Grayling, Allendale, Saginaw, Kalamazoo and Detroit. Lansing conference registration does not open until November 10, 2026, so as of October 10, 2026 the February and April Lansing windows are not yet open.
duration: Fall district conference, then a Lansing conference of about four days
pay_detail: The base fee is not stated on the program page. A $25 late fee applies to late Lansing registration. A financial aid application is linked on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 1/2 to 18 on day one (15 1/2 means you turn 16 during the cycle). Must be a Michigan resident and a U.S. citizen or legally present, not yet have a high school diploma, not be on reporting probation, and have no felonies. Ages 15 1/2 can only do credit recovery and return to their high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Inquiry Form on the MYCA site. Then follow the steps on the Admissions Process list.
notes: It has a military style setup, but the page says you do not have to join the military. The page calls it a program for at risk youth who want to finish high school.
duration: 5.5 months residential plus 12 months after. Cycles start mid-January and mid-July.
pay_detail: Free to parents. No obligation to join the military.

who_can_apply: Minneapolis residents ages 14 to 21 who are not enrolled in college. The Foundations level is for ages 14 to 21; the Pro level is for ages 16 to 21 with previous work or volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the January window. Accepted students (notified by about Mar 10) complete a required in-person orientation in March and April, then are matched with an internship.
notes: Step Up Director phone 612-673-5041; program phone 612-673-5118. The page does not mention work permits. Not every applicant is matched with a paid internship.
duration: About 2 months (June 22 to August 21 in 2026)
pay_detail: Paid by the City of Minneapolis (Foundations level); hourly rate and weekly hours not stated on the page. Teens not matched can do a 5-week online Career Exploration Program and earn up to $599 plus elective credit.

who_can_apply: Anyone from kindergarten through one year past high school. Independent membership means you are not in a club. It needs 6th grade or older and at least two years of 4-H club experience. It also needs an adult 4-H volunteer as your mentor.
how_to_apply: Get in touch with local 4-H staff near you, or fill out the interest form. Then complete your enrollment online or with a paper form.
notes: Clubs and costs can differ by county, so contact your county 4-H staff first. This is a youth club and learning program, not a paid job.
duration: One 4-H year runs Oct. 1 through Sept. 30. You re-enroll each year.
pay_detail: Minnesota 4-H does not charge a state membership fee. Some local clubs or programs charge dues, and help may be available.

who_can_apply: Young men who have just finished their junior year of high school. The Legion says picks are based on merit and ability. A sponsor, usually a local American Legion Post, chooses from students your school recommends.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Post. Forms and delegate information are on mnboysstate.org. For questions, call 651-291-1800 or email jkelley@mnlegion.org.
notes: Boys State is for boys. The 2026 session was June 14 to 20 at Saint John's University. Girls State is a separate program run by the American Legion Auxiliary. The Boys State pages give no age number, only the junior-year rule.
duration: One week. 2027 session: check in Sunday June 13, check out Saturday June 19, 2027.
pay_detail: Fees are paid by the sponsoring American Legion Post or other community group. No dollar amount is listed. Spending money for the camp store is optional.

who_can_apply: Students at a Minnesota high school with a DECA chapter. Chapters must have business and marketing courses and an advisor employed by the school. The official pages list no grade or age rule, so ask your advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, usually a business or marketing teacher. The advisor registers members online. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Jacklyn (Jackie) Schiller.
notes: DECA's page lists 86 chapters in Minnesota (high school and college counts are not split). The state site mndeca.org lists phone 218-847-5355 and posts role play and judging information. It does not explain joining, so start with your advisor.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student dues are $13 total: $5 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapters may add costs.

who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in an agriculture, food and natural resources (AFNR) course at a school with an agricultural education program. The page lists no age or grade rule. If your school has no program, the site links to how to start one.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher and sign up for an agriculture course. Joining FFA goes through that class.
notes: The home page reports 218 agricultural education programs in Minnesota. Ask your counselor whether your school has one.
duration: School year, tied to your ag class
pay_detail: National FFA dues are $7 a year. Minnesota State FFA dues are $11 starting in 2026. That is $18 for both. Local chapters and regions may charge more.

who_can_apply: Any Minnesota high school junior. Public, private and homeschooled students can apply. Each fall the program picks students from the applications. You send a 500 word essay and one letter from a teacher, counselor or advisor.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 Page Application PDF from the House Sergeant at Arms site. Email it to EducationalPrograms@house.mn.gov. You also need a 500-word essay. You need one letter of recommendation. It can come from a teacher, counselor or academic advisor.
notes: Participants stay together as a group each evening at the program-designated hotel. Questions: Sergeant at Arms office, 651-296-4860.
duration: One week (Monday to Friday) in Saint Paul. 2027 weeks run from Jan 25 to May 14, 2027.
pay_detail: Small meal stipend. The program pays for the hotel. You pay your other personal costs.

who_can_apply: The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Sign up online or at the Employment Center (1640 Como Ave, St. Paul). Then confirm your sign-up in person. You do a 5 minute screening. Then you may be sent to interviews. Email employment@mnstatefair.org or call 651-288-4475.
notes: The FAQ dates and the page header disagree on the year, so confirm the dates. Jobs are not guaranteed. The pages do not mention work permits, so check Minnesota rules for under 18.
duration: 12 fair days (2027 fair: Aug 26 to Sept 6)
pay_detail: State Fair department jobs start at $11.50 per hour; vendors set their own pay

who_can_apply: At least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first. Cadets can stay until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the Civil Air Patrol unit locator or the Minnesota Wing Locations page. Visit a meeting with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. Ask whether you can apply online.
notes: Example squadrons: Duluth (MN-016), St. Paul (MN-042), Alexandria (MN-135). Wing office: 6275 Crossman Lane, Inver Grove Heights, MN 55076. This is a youth program, not a paid job.
duration: Ideally a 2 hour squadron meeting each week, one Saturday event a month, and one week-long encampment in summer. School-based squadrons may differ.
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.

who_can_apply: Minnesota residents ages 13 to 19 who attend a middle or high school in Minnesota. Four representatives come from each of the eight congressional districts, plus at-large seats. Applicants should be active in their community and know the three branches of Minnesota government.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview in spring. Selected applicants meet the Council director with a trusted adult in May and are sworn in. You may get a follow-up call or text.
notes: The apply page has a caption with an older appointment date from the last round, so trust the Feb 28 and Mar 31 dates above. Full Council meetings are usually one Sunday afternoon a month. Check the apply page again in January 2027.
duration: Two-year term. You travel to the Twin Cities area at least five times a year for retreats, Youth Day at the Capitol and hearings.
pay_detail: The Council pages do not mention pay or a stipend.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 who live in Minnesota.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the online form. Pick a topic and write the paper. Send it in with the permission form.
notes: Participants get Borlaug Scholar recognition.
duration: Paper due early April; event on one day in May
pay_detail: Free. Participants are eligible for a $1,000 CFANS scholarship.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. (Zoo Ambassador volunteers must be 18 or older.)
how_to_apply: Watch the Minnesota Zoo volunteer page in 2027 for the application. Questions go to the volunteer services email on the page.
notes: ZooTeens do not handle or care for animals; they work with campers.
duration: Summer camp season (details not stated)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits include free admission for you and your immediate family and shop discounts.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th, 8th or 9th grade in the fall. Volunteers can return each summer through high school. After one year, you can move to Science Camp or Tree Monitor.
how_to_apply: Write to youthvolunteers@mortonarb.org and ask about the application. Ask about the deadline too.
notes: Weekday daytime shifts at most branches. Shift hours, fees and training are not listed on the page. The Arboretum's paid science fellowships are for college students, so they are not in the guide. Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects are taken by emailing volunteer@mortonarb.org.
duration: June through August, with some optional fall weekends
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Job seekers from high school students (ages 15 and up) to older adults. Free.
how_to_apply: Walk in. KidsMatter says no registration is necessary. You can try a mock interview, work on a resume and talk about financial literacy there. Questions: sherilyn@kidsmatter2us.org or 630-864-3960.
notes: The Park District says students can use the January fair to plan summer jobs. KidsMatter's 2027 page lists mock interviews, resume help and money skills. Last year's fair also had panels on the 7 Illinois career paths. Confirm what is offered in 2027. A news post from March 2025 also described a spring job fair for summer jobs. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.
duration: One day, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
pay_detail: The fair itself is free. Employers there hire for paid jobs.

who_can_apply: Groups of 2 to 5 teens in grades 7 through 12 when the application is sent in.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application during the August 1 to September 30 window. The top three to five teams give a short in-person pitch, and one team is chosen to run its program.
notes: Programs cannot sell products. They cannot be about politics, medicine or religion. The idea has to be new to the library calendar.
duration: Application in fall. Event runs 30 to 90 minutes in June, July or August 2027
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library pays for the program supplies.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be in 9th grade or above. You do not need a Naperville library card. TAG is open to teens in grades 6 through 12.
how_to_apply: Volunteers fill out the online volunteer application. For TAG, write to the teen librarians and ask how to attend. The email is teenlibrarians@naperville-lib.org.
notes: The volunteer coordinator's phone on the page is 630-637-2226.
duration: TAG meets once a month for two hours at rotating library locations
pay_detail: Unpaid. TAG members earn community service hours for each meeting.

who_can_apply: Up to 8 sophomores and juniors who live in Naperville. You must live inside the city limits. Freshmen and seniors cannot apply. Students who served on a board or commission cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button on any board or commission page of the city site. Answer yes to the Mayor's Chief of Staff question. Upload a resume or a note about your interest. Say that you are free all year.
notes: The news post does not say whether it is paid. Ask Rachel Pruneda (prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018). A full job description is on the city boards page.
duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term
pay_detail: Not stated. The city news post and the boards page were checked on 2026-10-10. Neither says anything about pay. Ask the city.

who_can_apply: Minimum age differs for each job. Check the age listed on the posting.
how_to_apply: Find a posting on the district job board and fill out the online application for that job. Mail, email or fax is not accepted. Apply for each job separately.
notes: Only applicants chosen for an interview are contacted. The page has a table of when each job is usually posted. Ages and pay are on each posting, so check them before you apply. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.
duration: Seasonal. Summer jobs include Centennial Beach and the Paddleboat Quarry.
pay_detail: Pay is listed on each job posting, not on the main employment page.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Volunteers 13 and under may volunteer alongside a parent or guardian. BINGO volunteers must be at least 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Application (17 and under) and approve a DCFS background check, at least two weeks ahead. Then email Becca (address on the Programs volunteer page) to sign up for a program. You cannot just show up, except at Nature Champion days.
notes: Volunteer hours can be confirmed by email, a signed letter or a school form.
duration: Dates listed this fall (no year printed; the weekdays match 2026): Kids' Night Out on Fridays, Nov 20 to Dec 18, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m. Santa's Workshop on Dec 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17 and 20.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The district can sign off on volunteer hours for school.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old, finished 8th grade, and not older than 21. Needs a C average or better, and no serious arrests or convictions.
how_to_apply: Download the cadet application and turn it in at the front desk, 1350 Aurora Ave. A committee checks references and does a background check and an interview. Questions: NPDCadets@naperville.il.us.
notes: The police internship on the same site is for college students, so it is not listed. The department points younger people to the cadet program.
duration: Ongoing, two meetings a month
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. Cadets help with security and traffic control at events.

who_can_apply: Students in high school or going into high school in fall 2026. You live in Naperville or go to high school there. You need parent permission and your own ride. You need good standing at school and no criminal contacts.
how_to_apply: Print and fill out the application and waiver at naperville.il.us/youthacademy. Send the signed forms to Sergeant Greg Rink at rinkg@naperville.il.us. Or drop them off at 1350 Aurora Ave.
notes: First come, first served and space is limited.
duration: 6 weeks, Thursday nights 6 to 8 p.m.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students who live inside Naperville city limits. You are a sophomore, junior or senior. Freshmen cannot apply. If you already served on a board or commission, you cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Click Apply on any board's page on the city Boards and Commissions site. Fill in the profile and the student rep questions. Upload a resume or a short statement. You can apply to up to three boards.
notes: 24 positions, two per board. Contact: Rachel Pruneda, prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018. The dates come from an August 2026 city news post.
duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term; most boards meet in the evening
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a volunteer role.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Franklin County and surrounding areas.
how_to_apply: Register when the program reopens; contact HNHFWorkforceDev@nationwidechildrens.org.
notes: The hospital's student opportunities page also lists Project SEARCH (a 9-month internship for students with disabilities) and Upward Bound Math and Science. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: November to April; two evening sessions a month (4:30 to 8 p.m.)
pay_detail: Paid; amount not stated

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 16 to 21. Participants must be at least 16 years old at the time of registration.
how_to_apply: Register online during the registration window. Questions: HNHFWorkforceDev@NationwideChildrens.org.
notes: Popular: the page says there is overwhelming interest, and about 108 young adults took part in 2025. Schedules are Monday to Friday starting at 9 or 10 a.m. All participants are 16 or older, and Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) lets 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer give proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead of a work permit; the hospital may still ask for paperwork, so confirm.
duration: 4 or 8 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 30)
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old. The page does not list a minimum age for the part-time and camp jobs, so check the posting.
how_to_apply: For jobs, apply on NISRA's ADP Workforce Now site from the Employment page. For volunteering, use the Volunteer Opportunities link on the same page. Call NISRA at 815-459-0737.
notes: The City of Elgin is a member of NISRA. The city says NISRA offers programs at Elgin sites. The 15 week internship is for therapeutic recreation college students. Jobs need a reliable ride. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit.
duration: Program seasons are 6 to 8 weeks. Volunteers are asked to commit for the full season.
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Part-time jobs (1 to 20 hours a week) are paid, but pay is not on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. CTD uses levels based on test scores. Or it uses a school record and teacher recommendation. Check the course page and the CTD eligibility page.
how_to_apply: Apply online through MyCTD. For admission, you use test scores or a portfolio. The portfolio is your report card and a teacher recommendation. If you have questions, email ctd-admissions@northwestern.edu.
notes: Costs a lot and is for advanced learners. CTD also has many other summer and weekend courses for grades 6 to 12 that are not listed here.
duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 tuition: $5,530 residential camp or $3,125 day camp. Financial aid for qualified students is given on a rolling basis while funds last.
