who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 years old. For Northwestern Memorial Hospital the age is 18, and it has no summer program. You must pass a health screening and an interview. You must also go to a virtual orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during the window. Then do an interview. Onboarding includes a health screening and an orientation. Ages 18 and up also get a background check.
notes: Volunteer offices: Delnor, 630-938-2180. Central DuPage, 630-933-6207. Lake Forest, 847-535-6851. Call the one near you.
duration: One day a week for 8 weeks between May and August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who will be seniors in fall 2027. The page says no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form, write a 200 to 225 word essay, list your journalism activities and send up to three work samples. Pay the $55 fee. Your counselor emails your transcript, GPA and school profile to Prof. Roger Boye. Add the financial aid form and a parent tax return if you want aid.
notes: Questions: r-boye@northwestern.edu (email is best) or (847) 491-2069.
duration: 4 weeks (June 27 to July 23, 2027)
pay_detail: Tuition $5,000 including room and board. Up to $100,000 in financial aid and scholarships is available. $55 application fee.

who_can_apply: Students rising into grades 9 to 12 the summer they attend. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and experience or interest in policy debate.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials such as a debate record, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. You need a laptop with a webcam, a mic and Microsoft Word.
notes: The 2026 program was online only. Check whether 2027 is online or on campus. Financial aid and scholarship page exists on the NHSI site but was not read.
duration: 4 or 6 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: $3,500 for the 4 week institute, $5,000 for the 6 week institute. $60 application fee.

who_can_apply: Students in their sophomore or junior year who will be rising juniors or seniors. The page asks for a class rank in or near the top 30 percent. It also asks for proof of special skill or strong interest in media arts.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials. These may include two essays, a resume, a letter of recommendation, test scores and your transcript.
notes: Competitive and costly. Travel is not included. Aid is need-based only. Not a paid program.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th or 11th grade who will be rising juniors or seniors. Juniors get priority. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and some theatre experience or strong interest.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send a resume, two essays, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. Test scores are optional. The Musical Theatre track needs a third essay.
notes: Competitive and costs a lot, but the program says need-based aid is given and does not offer merit aid. Travel is not included. Not a paid program.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12, per the page's 2026-2027 application form. The page does not list residency rules.
how_to_apply: Complete the application on the LETAB page. Questions: mhs@oppl.org.
notes: The page has an Apply now button and says questions go to mhs@oppl.org. It does not give dates.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It does not say if service hours are given.

who_can_apply: The page says boys and girls at least 14 years old are invited to learn new skills and gain work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form and waiver on the volunteer page. Volunteers also go through a criminal background check.
notes: The page says the volunteer background check applies to volunteers. Ask whether it applies to under 18.
duration: Event and program based
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get rewards for their hours.

who_can_apply: Open to job seekers. The page does not list minimum ages. Check the age on each job posting.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online job form. You can upload a resume and cover letter. Hiring supervisors review it. The district cannot talk about forms with anyone but the person who applied.
notes: The page does not say when seasonal hiring opens. Check it in winter. Inclusion partner jobs are handled by WSSRA, a partner group. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.
duration: Seasonal, with set start and end dates
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay is listed on the job postings, not on the main jobs page.

who_can_apply: Eligibility is based on age and grade as of January 1 of the project year. Any youth age 9 or older can do a project, whatever the grade. Eligibility ends December 31 of the year you turn 19. You must join an authorized Ohio 4-H club or group.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office to be connected with a club. Go to a first meeting. Pick a project. Then enroll in 4-HOnline with your club volunteer or the county office. Do it before the county deadline.
notes: Club membership, not a paid job. The site menu has a Just for Teens section that was not read. The ohio4h.org home page was down (503) when tried, so only the join page was read.
duration: Project year
pay_detail: Membership fees are not stated on the page. Ask your county Extension office.

who_can_apply: Students who interview in their junior year for the next summer's program. That means incoming seniors from across Ohio. Local American Legion posts sponsor delegates. The pages do not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Ask a counselor, administrator or history teacher if a Legion post is interviewing at your school. If not, use the Apply or Become A Delegate form on the site. The program will match you with a post. Chosen delegates go to an orientation.
notes: Not a job. Office phone is 513-529-3860. The site describes the program as drawing over 1,200 young men a year.
duration: Eight days
pay_detail: No cost to the student or family when a local American Legion post sponsors you (stated on the Parent Information page).

who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a career-technical education program approved by the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's career-technical or business teacher about a DECA chapter. State questions go to the Ohio DECA advisor, Drew Goldfinger, at Drew.Goldfinger@education.ohio.gov.
notes: Not a paid job. Your school must have an approved career-technical program with a DECA chapter. The state website listed on the page is ohiodeca.org.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $16 per student member: $8 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Any Ohio student who is entering 9th grade through 12th grade, or freshman year of college, this fall.
how_to_apply: Pick the camp on the ExploreAg page and fill out its registration form. For questions, use the Contact Us page at ofbf.org/contact/.
notes: The Oct. 11 close date is figured from the "10 days prior" rule on the flyer, so check the Columbus registration page. Sign up on the page for email notices about future ExploreAg camps.
duration: One-day camps in fall (the weeklong camp is over for 2026)
pay_detail: Free to students. A deposit confirms your spot and is returned on the day of the program (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Students at schools with an Ohio FFA chapter. The membership page does not list grades or ages. Ask your chapter advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's FFA chapter advisor to add you. Chapters submit membership through FFA.org. Schools with no program can contact Ohio FFA about starting a chapter.
notes: Not a job. The homepage reports 30,880 members in 345 chapters. State office phone is (614) 387-7575. The September 30 and November 30 dates are chapter deadlines, so a student should ask the advisor early.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $17 per member covers State and National FFA dues. The school is invoiced by Ohio FFA. Local chapter dues are not stated.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders in any United States school can sign up for Science Adventurers or Horizons of Science. A third camp is for rising 5th to 8th graders.
how_to_apply: Online application and payment for each camp (separate forms on the page). Questions go to Tiffiny Rye-McCurdy at rye-mccurdy.1@osu.edu.
notes: This is at the Ohio State Marion campus, not in Columbus. The page mentions no housing or rides, so plan your own.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: $185 per camp, which includes lunch and lab costs (2026 price).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 20 who are now in a youth or career tech group. Examples are 4-H, FFA, DECA, Girl Scouts, Scouting America and Key Club. You need strong leadership and a record of being involved. Members serve one two-year term.
how_to_apply: Send the official Junior Fair Board application in the online portal on the Ohio State Fair page. Do it between January 1 and March 1. Interviews come next. Send questions to the co-coordinators listed on the page.
notes: The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for minors. Ask the coordinators.
duration: About 2 weeks (arrive the Monday before the Wednesday opening)
pay_detail: Flat-rate stipend, higher in the second year. The amount is not stated. Housing and meals are provided in dorms at the fair.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 through 17 who like animals and nature and enjoy talking with visitors. The page asks for at least 40 hours of volunteer service over the summer.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button under Teen Volunteers on the volunteer page. It is an online form.
notes: The page says nothing about housing or rides.
duration: At least 40 hours through the summer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the unit locator. Visit with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ohio Wing office: 6031 E Main Street, PO Box 301, Columbus, OH 43213, phone 614-338-8198.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the page. Payment options are on the last page of the application.

who_can_apply: Middle school (6th to 8th) and high school (9th to 12th) students. You join through a local delegation run by a school or YMCA.
how_to_apply: Join or start a delegation at your school or YMCA in the fall. New delegations can email yg@ohioymcas.org or call (614) 407-4819. Students and advisors register on the State Assembly registration page.
notes: Not a job. The registration page still showed the 2026 assembly dates, so check it for the 2027 dates.
duration: Fall prep, then a 3-day State Assembly in spring
pay_detail: Registration fee amount is not stated on the program pages. A $25 late fee applied last year. Financial aid pages exist for middle and high school.

who_can_apply: Students in the grades listed for each role. You must finish the volunteer application and have it accepted before you can sign up for events.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Now on the volunteer page and finish the form. Then sign up for service projects on the events calendar.
notes: Service projects sign-up opens two weeks before each event.
duration: Member Services needs at least 20 hours. Teen Advisory Board meets monthly in the school year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens earn service hours (for example 2 hours for each accepted book review).

who_can_apply: Volunteers of all ages are welcome. The page says junior and senior high school students are encouraged to take part.
how_to_apply: Call Pleasant Home at (708) 383-2654. The Park District also asks volunteers to use the general Acorns to Oaks volunteer form and waiver.
notes: The same volunteer page lists the Oak Park Conservatory (call 708-725-2451). It also lists Cheney Mansion garden volunteers (call 708-383-2612). It does not give ages for those.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Lake County high school students who like health care, science and research.
how_to_apply: Email campmed@rfums.org to ask how to apply.
notes: In person only. Ask when applications open.
duration: 5 days, the last week of July
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Lake County students. High school students who live near the Rosalind Franklin University campus come first.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for INSPIRE link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026.
notes: Check whether it pays. Students can come back every summer until they finish a bachelor's degree. To reach the program, write to Rachael Lange at rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu or call 224-570-7325.
duration: 8 weeks in summer
pay_detail: Pay or stipend is not stated on the program page. Ask the program.

who_can_apply: Juniors in good standing with a GPA of 2.0 out of 4.0 or higher and an interest in nursing. Applications are for juniors at Cristo Rey St. Martin College Prep, Highland Park, North Chicago, Round Lake and Waukegan High Schools.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More link on the Nursing INSPIRE page to find the form. To reach someone, write to Dr. Mosilda Asanji at mosilda.asanji@rosalindfranklin.edu.
notes: Only students at the five schools named can apply. The page looks about two cycles old (it shows 2024-25 dates), so ask the program for current dates. Parents join a session on financial planning for college.
duration: 8 weeks, four days a week, June to August
pay_detail: Described as a paid educational opportunity. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. The page does not list a school list or grade rule beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Science Saturdays link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026. Contact: Rachael Lange, rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu, 224-570-7325.
notes: Only about 25 students are chosen each year.
duration: 9 Saturdays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., June to August
pay_detail: Free. Lunch and transportation are provided.

who_can_apply: Local high school and college students who like health care or science.
how_to_apply: Use the Register for the Virtual Mentor Program link on the pathway programs page. It opens a Google form (forms.gle). You must attend an orientation before being matched.
notes: Online, so you do not need to travel to North Chicago.
duration: Monthly meetings, October to May
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who live in River Forest. You must attend an orientation, and a parent or guardian must sign the release and waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen/Tween Volunteer form or the Book Buddies form online. Or print it. Email the form to volunteer@riverforestlibrary.org or drop it off at the library.
notes: River Forest residents only. The page says both that Summer 2026 applications are closed and that they are open, so it is out of date. Ask the library when the next call opens.
duration: Teen volunteers: one 1 hour shift a week in summer. Book Buddies: one weekly time slot for all of July (Tuesdays 3 to 5 p.m. or Wednesdays 5 to 7 p.m.).
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page mentions it can help with school community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18. A Minor Volunteer Consent Form is also needed. Volunteers must meet health and vaccine rules. They must do an interview and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and print and complete the Minor Volunteer Consent Form. If your interests match, they will schedule an interview and registration. Call (630) 978-4826.
notes: No shadowing or observation. The page still has older COVID-19 wording (proof of vaccination and a COVID-19 waiver), so ask the office what applies today. A background check is for ages 18 and up.
duration: Summer volunteers commit to 11 weeks in a row. Year-round volunteers commit to 6 months or 100 hours, whichever comes first.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school students can volunteer only during the summer months. Applicants must live within 12 miles of the hospital. The page does not give a minimum age.
how_to_apply: See the list of current chances (PDF). Then fill out the online volunteer application. Questions: volunteerROPH_services@rush.edu or (708) 660-5684.
notes: No shadowing or observation. Applying does not guarantee a spot and does not lead to a job automatically.
duration: Summer months
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include free parking and cafeteria and gift shop discounts.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 years of age or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application (general, or the Reading Together and Homework Center form), pass a background check, and attend volunteer orientation and training. Opportunities are posted on Idealist. Volunteer Services: VolunteerSPPL@ci.stpaul.mn.us or 651-266-7432.
notes: Not a teen-only program; open to anyone 14 and older.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Saint Paul residents who live in a cost-burdened household (for example, they receive SNAP or Section 8) or have a barrier to employment. YJ1: at least 14 by June 1 and no older than 19 by Aug 25. YJ2: at least 16 by June 1 and no older than 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online youth application in February (have your Social Security number, household income, a phone number and an emergency contact email ready; YJ2 needs a resume). Then attend pre-employment training in March, Career Exploration Day and interviews.
notes: Very competitive. About 2,000 people apply for about 500 YJ1 internships (FAQ). Contact (651) 266-6363 or RightTrack@ci.stpaul.mn.us. The overview text says ages 14 to 24 across all Right Track programs. The summer teen programs are 14 to 21. Unplaced teens can join an online professional development program.
duration: 6 to 9 weeks, starting in June
pay_detail: YJ1: at least $13.50 per hour, about 15 hours a week. YJ2: at least $16.37 per hour, 15 to 40 hours a week (as stated on the program page).

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 who live within the Schaumburg Township District Library service area. Grade level is not stated.
how_to_apply: The page invites eligible teens to apply but does not describe the method. Watch the library's Student Trustees page or ask the Teen Department.
notes: Board meetings are the third Monday of each month at 6:00 p.m., plus monthly meetings with the Teen Department. The next-cycle timing is a guess from this year's August 9 deadline.
duration: One year: October 2026 to September 2027
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: The page says the Volunteer Squad is open to students entering grades 8 to 12 in fall 2026. No age or residency rule is listed.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. Check the volunteer page in spring or ask the library.
notes: The contact email on the page was a blank placeholder. Call or visit the library.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Unpaid. Students can earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Minimum ages are not stated on the pages. Check each job posting.
how_to_apply: Go to a job fair. Or apply on the district's online job board (BambooHR). Questions: Alex Khodan, Supervisor of Aquatics, alkhodan@parkfun.com.
notes: Pay figures for lifeguards are from the 2025 post, so check the current rate. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.
duration: Seasonal, May through September, per the district's aquatics job fair post.
pay_detail: In the aquatics job fair post (dated Feb 18, 2025): lifeguards $18 an hour, swim instructors $18, concession staff $15. The district job board (read Oct 2026) lists swim instructor at $18 and concessions at $15.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who are 18 or younger and either live in Skokie or attend a Skokie school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Service contact form to join the email list. Or email teenteam@skokielibrary.info. You can also come to an upcoming teen volunteer event.
notes: Some opportunities are only on school breaks or days off. If you need hours for a ticket or a court order, the page says to email the teen team with your name and school.
duration: Teen Library Council meets Thursday afternoons
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. St. Charles Public Library cardholders and returning volunteers come first. Under 18 needs parent or guardian permission.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. It takes about 10 minutes. Answer every question. Applying does not mean you get a spot, because openings are limited.
notes: For summer, enter the grade you are going into. List dates you cannot volunteer. Contact details are behind a hidden email on the page.
duration: Not stated. There is a summer session.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: The library accepts volunteers age 13 and older. VolunTEENs is for ages 13 to 18. The district serves Sugar Grove and parts of Montgomery and Aurora.
how_to_apply: Fill out the library volunteer form from the circulation desk. For short projects, use the Service Hour Project form. Contact Nichole at 630-409-1589. Or contact Christine Edison, Adult and Teen Services Manager, at 630-409-3131.
notes: The apply link is the Service Hour Project form for ages 13 to 18.
duration: Summer reading volunteers help 2 to 6 hours a week for the 8 week program. Shelving volunteers commit to a weekly 2 hour shift for at least 6 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens can earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Students or recent high school graduates who want to learn about skilled trades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student intake form on the Student page. Parents can email info@thetradecollective.org.
notes: The page does not list specific internships or pay. It says the group is forming partnerships with high schools, colleges and universities. Address on the site: 1910 Greenwood Street, Evanston.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The student page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Ask the group.

who_can_apply: High school students. Beginners and advanced options are listed.
how_to_apply: Register online through the link on the camp page. Aid questions: mnudlcamps@augsburg.edu.
notes: Students on free or reduced lunch with a qualifying GPA may get full tuition for the July 6 to 10 week. The $425 price is for the 4-day HS Debate & Argumentation commuter camp (June 29 to July 2, 2026). The 1-week policy commuter camp is $600.
duration: From 4 days (HS Debate commuter, June 29 to July 2, 2026) up to 3 weeks (June 21 to July 10, 2026)
pay_detail: From $425 (1 week debate and argumentation, commuter) up to $2,500 (3 weeks with partial residential). Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Any student in grades 9 to 12, from public, private, charter and home schools.
how_to_apply: Use the application flyer and FAQ linked on the page, or contact BestPrep.
notes: The page does not state where it is, what it costs or if there are scholarships. BestPrep also lists an Educational Forum on Feb 17, 2027. It is at the Minneapolis Convention Center.
duration: A week (dates not posted)
pay_detail: Cost not posted. The page says it is kept low with sponsor help. Call 763-233-6325.

who_can_apply: Listed on the theatre's Teens page. No age or other rules are stated.
how_to_apply: Email Associate Production Manager Todd Kalina at tkalina@childrenstheatre.org. Say which area you want to shadow. Say what you hope to learn. Say when you are free.
notes: The page also lists youth tryouts for student actors ages 8 to 18. Those roles are unpaid.
duration: Not stated; you give your availability
pay_detail: Not stated; described as job shadowing only.

who_can_apply: Students going into 8th grade through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Not listed. The page links to a position description and key dates document. Call 651-487-8201 to ask when applications reopen.
notes: The page says the program needs a big time commitment over the summer. It gives no hours. Other roles on Como's volunteer page are for ages 17 and older.
duration: Mid-June through mid-August, with training days in May and June
pay_detail: Described as a volunteer program; pay is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 at the start of the summer program. You must be eligible to work in the United States. The page states no school or residency rule beyond the Twin Cities base. If you join through Step Up or Right Track, those programs have their own rules.
how_to_apply: Look for open positions on the Corps Join page (filter for youth programs) or call the youth program staff at 651-209-9900. Step Up and Right Track applicants apply through those programs.
notes: 2026 home bases were Tamarack Nature Center (White Bear Lake), Harriet Alexander Nature Center (Roseville), Mississippi Gateway Regional Park (Brooklyn Park) and Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge (Bloomington). Do not mix this up with the Summer Youth Corps, the live-in camping crew. That program is not active in 2026 and the Corps is rethinking its youth programs.
duration: June to August, 13 to 17 hours a week, usually 9:00 am to 4:00 pm on Monday and Wednesday or Tuesday and Thursday. Staff provide rides between sites.
pay_detail: Most Youth Interns are paid starting at $13.50 an hour. Some positions are unpaid. Pay may be higher depending on your age and whether Step Up, Right Track or the Corps employs you.

who_can_apply: The page says teens and youth. No minimum age or GPA is stated. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for your contact info, school and GPA, and transcript. If you are under 18, a parent must sign. For questions about your status, email onesmartcookie@cookiecart.org. Do not call.
notes: 1119 W Broadway Avenue, Minneapolis. The page does not say whether the 90 day internship is paid.
duration: 90 day internship, then bakery program; new intern training starts in fall, spring and summer sessions
pay_detail: Pay rates are not listed. The bakery program is paid job training.

who_can_apply: Students who will be in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email Lisa Loudon to sign up. Her address is lloudon@dunwoody.edu.
notes: Camp is listed as an example of past offerings; 2027 camps are not posted yet.
duration: 4 days (Aug 3 to 6 in 2026), 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $350 ($300 early bird), includes lunch, supplies and a field trip

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors and seniors interested in a technical career with a 2.5 GPA. Seniors must file the FAFSA and show high financial need.
how_to_apply: Send the online application, a one page essay, transcripts and the FAFSA (Dunwoody code 004641). You also have an interview with staff. Email p2c@dunwoody.edu.
notes: Must attend a fall orientation and at least 85 percent of monthly workshops. Selection is not guaranteed.
duration: Monthly meetings in the school year plus 3 weeks in summer (2026 dates are not on the page)
pay_detail: Hourly stipend for the 3 week summer experience (amount not stated). Scholarship of up to $10,000 a year for two years for those who enroll at Dunwoody.

who_can_apply: Students in high school at schools that partner with Genesys Works, on track to graduate, who can work in the U.S. and can fit a lighter senior-year schedule.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Genesys Works application page. Then you interview for Summer Skills Training. Then you confirm your spot. Twin Cities contact: 651-789-0088 or tcadmin@genesysworks.org.
notes: Internships are earned. They are not promised. Students must get themselves to work. The application page named a rising senior as the target. The FAQ said junior year. The site did not agree with itself, so ask which grade to apply in. The families page gives $10,000-$12,000 for the internship year. Its summary gives $10,000-$13,000. Ask which is right.
duration: 8 weeks of summer training (160 hours), then 20 hours a week during senior year
pay_detail: Paid for hours worked; the site says interns can earn about $10,000 to $13,000 over the internship year. Rates vary by site.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and 17. You need a reliable ride to the hospital. You must be able to keep patient info private.
how_to_apply: Email three things to volunteer@gillettechildrens.com. They are the application, a Student Reference Form from a teacher or advisor, and a Parent Release Form. If a piece is missing, they will not review it. Some applicants are interviewed in person with a parent.
notes: Before starting you must pass a background check and fingerprinting and show proof of vaccination and a QuantiFERON-TB Gold blood test. These may cost money.
duration: One 3 hour weekday shift per week, June through August
pay_detail: Volunteer. There may be a cost to the applicant for the required health screenings.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 12 who like STEM, from across the Twin Cities. The University of Minnesota summer camps page says students entering grades 8 and 9 are eligible to apply. The page describes a pro-girl program. It does not say whether boys can join.
how_to_apply: Use the Eureka! online application or the PDF application on the page. Do this when registration opens. The PDF comes in English, Spanish or Somali. Contact: girlsinc@ywcampls.org or 612-215-4369.
notes: Described as a pro-girl program (Girls Inc.), so ask whether it is for girls only. Interns are treated as volunteers by the worksite because the stipend comes from Girls Inc., not the worksite. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.
duration: Summer camp about 4 weeks (2026: June 29 to July 24), Mon to Thu 8:45 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Fri to 2 p.m.
pay_detail: Eureka! interns get a stipend from Girls Inc. after completing a 4 week internship (20 hours a week). The amount is not stated. The cost of the summer program is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering or in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply or Request Info links on the camp page. For a scholarship, show proof of SNAP, TANF or FDPIR benefits (or tax forms) and proof of at least a C average in science.
notes: Oct 26, 2026 is a Monday, which matches the weekday on the page.
duration: 1 week, July 12 to 16, 2027, 9 am to 5 pm
pay_detail: $598 before April 30; $698 after. Need-based scholarships can cover full tuition.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. High school students bring a reference form, a parent consent form and a health screening form to the interview. Some roles have higher age limits.
how_to_apply: Send the volunteer application and do an interview. Finish an online orientation. Pass a Minnesota background check. Then train on site. For questions, call 651-254-5709. You can also write to volunteerservices@healthpartners.com.
notes: The page does not name which hospitals take teens, so ask when you call.
duration: Year-round program is at least 6 months and 100 hours. Summer program is 10 to 12 weeks.
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 28 who live in Hennepin, Ramsey or Dakota County. You must meet low income (WIOA) rules. You must also have at least one more barrier. Examples are being a parent, not having stable housing, being 1 to 2 grade levels behind, or being at risk of dropping out. You can still ask if you are not sure.
how_to_apply: Submit the youth and young adult referral form or the Inquire Now form on the Hired page. You must enroll to get services. Offices: Minneapolis 612-808-9500, Saint Paul 651-328-2777, Bloomington 952-303-8303.
notes: Funding sets what is offered. Help with school costs and living costs depends on what money is on hand.
duration: About 6 months of programming, with up to 2 years of support
pay_detail: The page does not state pay. It mentions subsidized internships, job shadows and work experience.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21 who have finished one VALT drawing session. Jobs go first to North Minneapolis residents, but teens from around the Twin Cities can join programs.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Program Registration Form. Then take a VALT session. Then you interview. Call 612-588-1148 or email ContactUs@juxtaposition.org.
notes: VALT is the free drawing class that comes first.
duration: Year-round, about 9 hours a week
pay_detail: Starting wage $16 an hour, about 9 hours a week on average during the school year

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Program Registration Form. Send questions to VALT@juxtaposition.org.
notes: Held at 1108 West Broadway, Minneapolis.
duration: About 10 weeks per session. Fall 2026: Sept 16 to Nov 20. Winter: Jan 6 to Mar 12, 2027.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15. Volunteers under 18 need a signed permission slip from a parent. These hospitals take teens. Ridges is in Burnsville. St. John's is in Maplewood. Southdale is in Edina. The U of M Medical Center has an East and a West Bank site. Woodwinds is in Woodbury. Lake Medical Center is in Wyoming. Northland is in Princeton.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then you have an interview and online learning. You also need a background check, fingerprints, a TB test and proof of shots. Last is an online orientation. Call 1-855-324-7843.
notes: A flu shot each year is required. The 100 hour minimum is listed for volunteers in general.
duration: About 100 hours over 6 to 9 months
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the Youth Employment and Training Initiatives page and the Park Board temporary jobs page (minneapolisparks.org/jobs/temporary_jobs/) for the next application.
notes: Pay, season and hours are not stated on the page, so ask the Park Board before you plan. The same page lists Minneapolis Park Corps for ages 18 to 24 as paid training (not for teens). The Park Board teen page also lists Youthline, a mentorship program for ages 12 to 17. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.
duration: Not stated (the page only mentions a '2026 season')
pay_detail: The page lists this under Youth Employment and Training Initiatives but does not say whether Teen Teamworks is paid or give a pay rate. Ask the Park Board.

who_can_apply: Youth leaders ages 14 to 17. Members serve a two year term.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Contact Adrian Waters at Awaters@minneapolisparks.org or 612-849-9048 to ask when the next group is chosen.
notes: The teen programs page calls it a select group. Confirm how to apply and whether it is paid before you plan around it.
duration: Two year term, 5 to 12 hours a month
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page. The page says members get support with professionalism, financial literacy and customer service.

who_can_apply: High school students or recent graduates ages 14 to 18 who are U.S. citizens.
how_to_apply: Online application. Choose YES on the form to request financial aid; aid does not affect admission.
notes: The page does not name the exact camp site. Scholarship details are at mnacecamp.org/scholarships (not read).
duration: 1 week (June 14 to 19 and June 21 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $1,750, due May 1 on acceptance. Travel is not included. $25,000 in financial aid was set aside for 2026.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall. The page also says "current 8th to 11th grade", so confirm before applying.
how_to_apply: Apply online. There is no fee to apply. A deposit is due with the application. It cannot be refunded.
notes: A class that fills moves to a waitlist.
duration: Two weeks per session. Summer 2027: June 14 to 25 and July 12 to 23, 9 am to 4 pm
pay_detail: Tuition is listed as TBA per session for 2027. Discounts: $100 for both sessions and $50 per extra sibling. Financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up can volunteer in the kitchen and farms without an adult. Ages 12 to 15 need an adult who has done volunteer training. Deliveries need an adult driver (18 to drive alone).
how_to_apply: Register for an orientation on the volunteer page. Under 18 needs a parent signed waiver. Call 612-872-1152.
notes: Some equipment use depends on age.
duration: Shift times not listed
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Volunteers under 18 use the teen form. A parent or guardian must sign it. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online teen volunteer application. Pick the roles, the times you are free and the branch you like.
notes: Some positions need a background check. The form asks for a personal reference and emergency contact. It also asks about required service hours if you need them for school.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 who attend a public school in Minneapolis or Saint Paul. The page says no exceptions at this time.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Call 612-624-4745.
notes: Grant funded. Students must commit to the whole program.
duration: 4 weeks (June 15 to July 10 in 2026), Monday to Friday 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $18 an hour

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You must pass a swim test in the first class (150 yard swim, tread water, a 20 yard timed swim and a 12 foot dive to get a 10 pound object) and show a birth certificate with photo ID.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through the city system. Or call Como Park Pool at 651-489-0378, Highland Aquatic Center at 651-695-3773, or Great River Water Park at 651-642-0390. After you pass, call Great River Water Park to apply for a job.
notes: You need 80 percent on the written exam and must pass all skills. Work permit rule for Minnesota minors not checked.
duration: Course dates not listed
pay_detail: Course cost and lifeguard pay are not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21.
how_to_apply: Apply for the YJ2 internship through Right Track. Contact Furo Ejero, Furo.Ejero@ci.stpaul.mn.us or 651-266-8989.
notes: School year meetings may mean being excused from class. Right Track has its own program and application; see its own card.
duration: 8 weeks (June 20 to Aug 10 on the page, no year), then 6 to 10 hours a month for two years
pay_detail: Academy is a paid YJ2 internship at $15 an hour, 20 hours a week, Monday to Thursday. Board members also get up to $125 in stipends for meetings and learning tasks.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The page lists ages 15 to 18 for the high school stage. The page says the youth pathway starts in middle school.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply. Contact the museum at info@smm.org or 651-221-9444 and ask about the Kitty Andersen Youth Science Center.
notes: The season, hours and how to apply are not stated. Check before you plan. There are four STEM areas. They are biological sciences and public health, media and technology, environmental sciences and sustainability, and engineering and design. The work permit rule was not checked.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid as museum employees; the hourly rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Spark-Y serves youth from 14 to 24 and up. No other requirements are listed for the internship.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist through the form on the Spark-Y Engage page.
notes: The page lists several roles. The Pathways Summer Internship is the one for newer workers. Apprenticeships fill fast.
duration: Short term, annual; hours not listed
pay_detail: Described as paid; the rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Contact Mary Morris, the staff contact named on the page.
notes: Site: Baker Outdoor Learning Center. The date pattern comes from the general text on the page.
duration: Training plus at least one week of camp, June to August
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact Vicky Wachtler, the staff contact named on the page.
notes: Site: Eastman Nature Center. The date pattern comes from the general text on the page.
duration: Camps run June to August
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Meant for young people, most of all those who face barriers to work. The minimum age depends on the role. It is 15 for Explorers Camp and Community Engagement. It is 16 for the Camp Internship, Farm Garden, Outdoor Recreation and IT/GIS roles. It is 18 for several others, and some roles do not state a minimum.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Contact Char Myers (Char.Myers@threeriversparks.org) or Terrell Lhotka (Terrell.Lhotka@threeriversparks.org).
notes: The Three Rivers Park District Foundation gives rides money if getting to work is a barrier. The work permit rule was not checked.
duration: June through August, about 20 hours a week (some roles 40)
pay_detail: At least $15 an hour

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Contact Seth Eberle, the staff contact named on the page. No online form is described.
notes: Site: Silverwood Park. The date pattern comes from the general description. It is not a date posted for 2027.
duration: June to March, 30 hours of service
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Twin Cities high school students, new or skilled. Spots are limited. It is hard to get in.
how_to_apply: Use the application links on the Summer Programs page. Questions: denise.huang@stthomas.edu.
notes: Stipend amount is not stated. Radio Camp cost is not listed.
duration: MPR Radio Camp 1 week; Multimedia Storytelling Institute 3 weeks; College Essay Workshop 4 days
pay_detail: Free in 2026 (the Multimedia Storytelling Institute is normally $3,000 and the College Essay Workshop $1,000). Students get a stipend for finishing, plus free lunch and transit passes.

who_can_apply: Students entering their senior year. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: Not described. Phone the department at 612-624-4507.
notes: At the end, interns get a letter of support. It comes from the engineering faculty.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: A stipend and bus transportation are provided; the amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grade 11 or 12. Priority goes to students who have not been in Discover STEM before. Admission is competitive, and the program especially encourages applicants from underrepresented communities.
how_to_apply: Apply online, or by mail on request. Send an unofficial high school transcript and personal statement answers. Do not send the application in pieces. Those are not reviewed.
notes: The camps page for the college also lists other high school options, such as the Run the World AI Explorers Camp (grades 11 and 12) and a Summer Computer Academy for girls in grades 6 to 12. Not a job.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily (day program)
pay_detail: The page says there is no cost to apply and attend, thanks to 3M. It also mentions an enrollment fee or scholarship request after admission, so confirm that nothing is charged.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who have met barriers to science and medicine chances. The program focuses on high schoolers in the Twin Cities area.
how_to_apply: Fill in the enrollment survey on the program site. Send back the signed form by the deadline. You need a letter of reference from a science teacher, an organization leader, or a church pastor.
notes: The site says both ten and twelve students are chosen, so it is a small cohort.
duration: One week (July 20 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free for selected students; meals and travel are covered and students get a $400 stipend.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older, a current junior or senior at the time of application, and a U.S. citizen.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add a resume that lists your test scores, a transcript and two letters from faculty. Also add a statement of interest and a statement of goals.
notes: No housing or meals are provided. Applicants under 18 need an adult chaperone for University housing, or can stay off campus with family or friends. Number of spots is not stated.
duration: 8 weeks, May 31 to July 23, 2027 (tentative), 40 hours a week
pay_detail: Scholars earn an hourly wage; the amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Enrolled high school students who completed a full year of single variable calculus by the end of 2025-26. Graduating seniors still count.
how_to_apply: The student fills out the online form. A math teacher emails a short note of support. UMTYMP students do not need the note.
notes: This is a commuter camp only. You do not stay overnight.
duration: 1 week (June 22 to 26 in 2026), about 9 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not listed. No housing or meals are provided.

who_can_apply: Current 10th graders from groups that are not well represented in STEM. You should plan to go to a four year college. You must commit to one Saturday a month through December of 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It needs a note from a STEM teacher or counselor, personal essays, your GPA and a list of your courses.
notes: You must get yourself to the program. Money for rides is available if you ask. Only 10th graders are accepted from 2025 on.
duration: January of 10th grade to December of 12th grade
pay_detail: Free; lunch and a gift included. No stipend. Students who attend through fall of 12th grade and are admitted to the College of Science and Engineering can get a $40,000 scholarship ($10,000 a year for 4 years, from 3M).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students in grades 6 to 12. High school sessions are for grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register through the online form linked on the VetCamp page, or join the mailing list for new dates.
notes: It is held at the Ben Pomeroy Student-Alumni Learning Center. That is on the St. Paul campus. The Minnesota Veterinary Medical Foundation is the sponsor.
duration: One afternoon. Self-hosted camps are about 3 hours; the Aug 12, 2026 high school camp ran 12 to 5 pm. 2026 high school dates: June 10, July 15, Aug 12.
pay_detail: $15 registration fee for self-hosted camps; families with financial need can ask for a waiver.

who_can_apply: Teens from across the Twin Cities. The page does not state an age or grade range.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps. Applications for 2027-28 open in spring 2027. Follow @walkerteens on Instagram for programming info and updates.
notes: The Walker also offers free Teen Maker Break art sessions, monthly on the third Saturday from 2 to 5 p.m. (materials and snacks provided). Ask the Walker whether WACTAC members are paid and what ages can join.
duration: Weekly meetings during the school year
pay_detail: Pay or stipend is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: The page title says ages 12 to 15 (the University youth programs list says 12 to 16). Applicants attend a February info session, interview, and a mandatory one-day orientation in June.
how_to_apply: Attend the free virtual info meeting in February, get the application, sign up for an interview, pay the fee if accepted, then attend orientation. Call 612-301-1210 for questions.
notes: Good first leadership experience for younger teens. Volunteer hours can be logged.
duration: Flexible half or full days over the summer
pay_detail: One-time $100 registration fee (orientation, training, t-shirt, certificate, supplies); financial aid available for students who qualify for free or reduced school lunch. CIT service is volunteer time.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 with an interest in automotive tech, manufacturing, engineering, planning or robotics. Space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Application steps for 2027 are posted early in 2027 on the camp page.
notes: Competitive: 20 spots. Day camp; the page does not mention transportation.
duration: One week, day camp
pay_detail: Free to attend; lunch is provided

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 9 with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, who have completed or can enroll in pre-algebra and are interested in engineering, science, transportation or technology.
how_to_apply: Application information for 2027 is posted early in 2027. Selection process details are on the camp's admission decisions page.
notes: For younger teens. The University's youth programs list shows ages 13 to 16 for this camp.
duration: Two weeks, day camp
pay_detail: Free two-week day camp

who_can_apply: Middle school students, high school students and adults can apply. Students under 17 need a parent to say yes. The library cannot give drop-in volunteer work. It also cannot give court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student volunteer application (a PDF from the volunteer page) or pick one up at the Welcome or Information Desk. Contact Laura Stone, Volunteer Coordinator, (847) 244-5150 ext. 3059, lstone@wnpl.info. For TAG, complete the registration form on the TAG page.
notes: Adults who apply must agree to a background check for crimes. The page says TAG is a good way to earn volunteer hours for National Honor Society and other service rules.
duration: Weekly assignments or one-time tasks. TAG meets monthly.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library tries to help students who need school service hours, with advance notice.

who_can_apply: Students at East Aurora High School or West Aurora High School only. The pages do not list income or first-generation rules, so ask the staff.
how_to_apply: Fill out the new student application (from your counselor, Room 201 at East or A104A at West, or the website). Staff then set up a family interview, and new students do a 10 to 60 day trial period. Email upwardbound@waubonsee.edu.
notes: The form asks for copies of your transcript and birth certificate. It also asks for your Social Security card and a parent tax return. Give these only to program staff at the school or the Sugar Grove office.
duration: Through high school graduation
pay_detail: Free. Federally funded TRIO program. No stipend is mentioned on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Individuals and groups. People under 18 need a parent or legal guardian to sign the forms. No minimum age is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Agreement Form. A parent signs it if you are under 18. Email it to efallon@waukeganparks.org. Phone: Elizabeth Fallon, (847) 782-3626.
notes: Park projects: contact Bryant Brown. Bryant is the Park Services Supervisor. The phone is 847-360-4756. Read the Volunteer Requirements and Expectations document before you start.
duration: Year-round, event and project based
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. Right now the library does not take volunteers who must do court ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer form. Or visit the Youth and Teen Department during normal hours.
notes: The library's Maker Space (3D printer, laser engraver, sewing machines) is open to teens ages 16 and up, which is a good way to build skills. Hours and training are not on the pages.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. If you are under 15, you can volunteer with an adult who is 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Volunteer Application. You get a confirmation email, then a call or email after approval. Contact Lisa Snow, 630-681-0962 ext. 548, lisasn@wdsra.com.
notes: WDSRA also hires part-time program staff (the volunteer page does not give a minimum age for them). The jobs page lists openings and how to apply.
duration: Flexible. You choose how often. New volunteer orientation takes about 1 hour.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12 can earn service hours. There are separate Teen Library Council groups for middle school and high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Interest Form. Or fill out the Teen Library Council form. Questions: teenread@wheatonlibrary.org.
notes: You can also earn hours by making cards. Four cards earn 1 volunteer hour. You can also write book reviews. Each review earns 30 minutes of service hours.
duration: School year volunteering begins the week of Monday, September 14 (no year printed; the weekday matches 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 can join the teen program. Kids ages 11 to 13 can apply to be library helpers for certain youth programs, with parent or guardian approval.
how_to_apply: Summer 2026 applications are closed for the season. School year applications are open. Go to the volunteering page. Fill out the volunteer form there. If you have a question, write to teenvolunteers@wilmettelibrary.info.
notes: Summer jobs run June to August. Krista Hutley is the teen librarian. Eti Berland is the school engagement librarian. They are the teen volunteer coordinators. The Studio program has its own info sheet.
duration: School year positions, plus summer positions that run June to August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Wisconsin youth in grades 9 to 12 at the time of application.
how_to_apply: Apply through 4-H Online. The team checks references in December.
notes: Key 2027 dates: State Leader Teams Weekend Apr 9 to 11, Fall Forum Nov 5 to 7.
duration: One program year (events April to November 2027)
pay_detail: $500 (shirts, lodging and meals at four events). Scholarships up to 70% on request.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin youth in grades 8 to 11. Each track has its own grade range.
how_to_apply: Register in 4-H Online (make a profile if you are new). A paper form is also on the 4-H site. Apply for a scholarship during registration.
notes: The page says track details are labeled 2026 and may change for 2027.
duration: 5 days (June 13 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $150 per youth, covers lodging, meals, bus and activities. State scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Students entering their senior year of high school next fall. You must be from a Wisconsin high school or home-schooled in Wisconsin.
how_to_apply: School staff such as counselors or the social studies department often help choose students. You can also email info@badgerboysstate.org to say you want to attend. Include your name, high school, phone number and email.
notes: Not a job. The 2027 session is the 83rd. Office: 2930 American Legion Drive, Portage, WI 53901, phone 608-745-1090.
duration: One week, June 13 to 19, 2027
pay_detail: The program says it is 100% funded by donations. A student fee is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Young women in their junior year of high school in Wisconsin. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: The page says to speak to your high school counselor if you want to become a delegate.
notes: Not a job. A tuition sponsor is needed, usually found through the school or the local American Legion Auxiliary. Dates for the next session come from the program site.
duration: One week, June 20 to 25, 2027
pay_detail: The American Legion Auxiliary and Legion family sponsor and pay the tuition for a delegate. Clubs, businesses and school groups can also pay. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin DECA strongly encourages members to also be enrolled in a marketing or business course. Chapters need an advisor with a marketing or business educator license. Detailed rules are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. For eligibility and deadlines, contact the Wisconsin DECA advisor, Tim Fandek, at Timothy.Fandek@dpi.wi.gov.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is wideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Wisconsin.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $18 per student member: $10 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin students interested in the outdoors. It is best suited to high school students and younger students may apply. Some DNR volunteer tasks are only for ages 16 and up. You can take part through the summer after senior year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YCC application and parent consent form from the DNR YCC page. Or contact the YCC Coordinator, Kyle Zenz, at kyle.zenz@wisconsin.gov or 715-299-0925.
notes: Volunteer program, not a job. A parent or guardian must sign the consent form. It can count toward school service-learning or independent study credit if your school agrees. The packet's example activities are from 2025, so check this year's schedule.
duration: Year-round. Two district meetings plus Spring Hearings and a May convention, with extra field days.
pay_detail: No pay. Free to join, apart from your own travel costs.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The applicant page lists no GPA, age or residency rule. You also need an employer to hire you.
how_to_apply: Pick a career area. Talk with your counselor and parents. Contact your local YA Regional Coordinator and apply. Then interview with employers. After you are hired you go to orientation and safety training.
notes: Wisconsin's youth apprenticeship page says work permits are no longer required for 16 and 17 year olds. The Wisconsin work permit page says 14 and 15 year olds still need a permit ($10 fee, repaid by the employer by the first paycheck). A 15 year old junior is possible, so ask your coordinator. Student learner status does not override minor employment laws. DWD phone (608) 266-3131.
duration: Not stated on the program pages. Work and classes run during high school.
pay_detail: You earn a paycheck from day one. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in a school agricultural education program that has an active FFA chapter. The Affiliation page says grades 5th to 12th. No age limit is listed.
how_to_apply: Contact your school's ag education teacher. If your school has no program, contact the state ag education staff. Ask about starting one.
notes: Not a job. The site has a Local Chapter Locator that links to Find a Program. Your school must have an ag program and an FFA chapter. The Affiliation fee is based on enrollment. The page does not say who pays it, so the claim in pay_detail that the school pays is not confirmed by this page.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Traditional membership is $15 total ($8 state, $7 national). Local chapters may charge more. Affiliation program fees depend on enrollment and are paid by the school.

who_can_apply: The Wisconsin Wing site labels the cadet program as ages 12 to 19. The national CAP cadet page says between 12 and 18. This guide uses the national ages, 12 to 18, so ask the squadron if you are 19. The interest form lists grades 6 through 12 and high school graduates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the Wisconsin Wing site. The wing aims to pass your info to a local unit within 48 hours, and the unit should contact you within 48 hours after that. If you hear nothing in four days, email Major Todd Mandel at todd.mandel@wicap.us.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ages differ between the Wisconsin page (12 to 19) and the national page (12 to 18), so confirm with the squadron. Wing address: 2400 Wright Street, Madison, WI 53704.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the program pages. Ask the squadron.

who_can_apply: Students who join a delegation near them. The page does not list grades. Media spots are by application and may be limited.
how_to_apply: Find a delegation near you on the Wisconsin YG site. Then register at wiyg.org/register before the closing date for your role. Use the Contact Us page if you need help starting a delegation.
notes: Not a job. Legislative and Media materials are due in January and Judicial materials in February.
duration: Fall to March: prep, a Pre-Gov session, then the Model Government conference
pay_detail: Dues and conference fees are not listed on the program page. Ask your delegation.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12. Teens should limit in-person volunteering to no more than two events a month.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a teen volunteer event on the library page. Or send a book review of at least 5 sentences through the form. Questions: askus@woodridgelibrary.org.
notes: If you register and cannot come, cancel so someone else can take the spot. Some events have waitlists.
duration: Event based. Hours depend on the event length.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Library staff give letters with the service hours earned.

who_can_apply: Eligible young adults ages 17 to 24. The page does not list other rules or say which counties qualify.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Now or Get Started at worknetdupage.org/job-seekers/get-started/, or call 630-955-2030. Career Center: 2525 Cabot Drive, Suite 302, Lisle.
notes: Starts at 17, so it fits only older high schoolers. Spanish-speaking services are available. The Get Started page was not read, so check eligibility there.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience is offered; pay rates and length are not stated. Training or school help is up to $10,000.

who_can_apply: Incoming 9th to 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Register online for the day camp or residential option; a separate summer program scholarship application is available. Questions: summerprograms@xavier.edu.
notes: Xavier's Summer Programs page also lists other high school options: Summer in Cincy (one-week residential pre-college), D'Artagnan Summer Business Academy (rising juniors and seniors), CSI Forensics Camp (grades 10 to 12) and STRONG eXplorer Career Camp. Check each page for 2027 prices. High school students who attend may get a $500 to $1,000 award if they later enroll. Checked 2026-10-10: the open 2027 scholarship applications are for the Summer Programs in general. The page gives no application dates for STEAM@XU, so left unconfirmed.
duration: 1 week (2026: July 19/20 to 24)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: day camp $495 ($545 after May 1, 2026); residential $1,095 ($1,195 after May 1, 2026). Scholarships offered.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 25 in the greater Chicagoland area. Services are free.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the sign-up page. Current clients can talk to their career coach about a Paid Work Experience. Phone (847) 864-5627, 1114 Church Street, Evanston.
notes: A Chicago-area nonprofit that has worked with young people for over 40 years. Text YJCNEWS to (224) 253-6233 for updates. Ask the staff about work permits if you are under 16. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.
duration: Paid Work Experience: 10 weeks
pay_detail: Paid Work Experiences: Youth Job Center covers all costs, including salary. The pay rate is not stated on the program pages. Coaching and training are free.

who_can_apply: One high school senior who lives inside School District U-46 lines. You show leadership. You plan to go to college or higher education.
how_to_apply: Submit the scholarship application and essays when the call opens. The page lists writing help resources, and in 2026 offered free one-on-one feedback on up to two drafts.
notes: Recent winners came from Larkin, Bartlett and Elgin high schools. Contact YWCA Elgin at 847-742-7930 or info@ywcaelgin.org.
duration: Yearly award
pay_detail: Unpaid. The $2,000 scholarship each year is an award, not wages.
